- resolved: 2026-10-08, B16 g4 step 4 landed `t.footer.line` as `A product of Omnikom.`: the skip line is deleted from `copy.test.ts`, `b12g2-p-credit` is a `file` entry, and the rule above no longer applies. Proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/reel/copy.test.ts` → `Tests  7 passed (7)`, and `grep -c skip app/tests/unit/reel/copy.test.ts` → `0` (measured 2026-10-08, B16 g4 follow-up).

## P-2102 · B12 says `specHash` from `spec.ts` "is not changed", but its parameter type is `RenderSpec`, which a `ReelSpec` is not
- symptom: `reel-spec.test.ts` calling `specHash(spec)` with a `ReelSpec` failed `bun run typecheck` with `TS2345: Argument of type 'ReelSpec' is not assignable to parameter of type 'RenderSpec'. Type 'ReelSpec' is missing the following properties from type 'RenderSpec': images, out`. The same call is planned in `render-reel.ts` (`spec_hash = specHash(spec)`).
- cause: B9 typed the hash for its own three kinds; the plan took the function as generic because its body is `sha256Hex(JSON.stringify(spec))`.
- rule: widen the parameter, type only (`spec: RenderSpec | ReelSpec` and `import type { ReelSpec } from "./reel-spec.ts"` in `spec.ts`); the body and the hash of every B9 spec stay as they were. A cast is not the answer (G-103). B12 g2 made this one-line change in B9's file and said so in the log; a lane that does not want it there widens the type itself.
- proof: `cd app && bun run typecheck` → exit 0 with the change; `git diff origin/main -- src/server/assets/spec.ts` shows the import line and the signature line only; the watched-fail `b12g2-s-hash-bed` (make `specHash` ignore `sound`) is red in `reel-spec.test.ts`.
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2103 · A weight shift between two stacked spans wraps the heavier one: the title lost its last words behind the mask
- symptom: the first still of the reel at 5.0 s showed the title as `A residence / shaped / the` with a stray `d` between lines; the DOM said three lines of 650 px at 112 px, so the line split was right.
- cause: M3 stacks a 400 span and an absolutely positioned 500 span (`.w5`); the absolute one is only as wide as the 400 line, 500 is wider, so it wrapped, and the `.ln` mask hid the wrapped words. The launch film never met it because its lines were short.
- rule: every `.m1 .ln > span` gets `white-space: nowrap`, so the stacked weight cannot wrap; when a still shows missing words, measure `getBoundingClientRect` of each `.ln` in a page before changing the break code.
- proof: `grep -n "white-space: nowrap" launch/reel/scene.html` → the `.m1 .ln > span` rule; the 5.0 s still shows `A residence / shaped around / the landscape.` (measured 2026-10-05, B12 g2).
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2104 · `bun run check` stops at `stubs` on main: the `STUB(B15)` marker in `crypto.ts` outlived its slice
- symptom: B12 g2's `bun run check` printed `src/server/lib/crypto.ts:47 STUB(B15) slice is closed: first used by src/server/omnikom/payload.ts ...`, `stubs: 8 markers, 1 on closed slices`, then `error: script "stubs" exited with code 1`; `format:check` and `test`, which come after it in the chain, never ran.
- cause: B15 was recorded closed on main (d68b75c, "B15 closed") while its marker stayed; `git diff origin/main --stat -- src/server/lib/crypto.ts` is empty in the lane, so the red is main's.
- rule: when `check` stops at `stubs` on a marker no lane file touches, bring main in first (`git fetch -q origin && git merge origin/main`): main removed this marker in 46fcbfb, so the merge clears the red. Run the rest of the chain by hand (`bun run format:check`, `bun run test`, `bun run build`) only when main itself still holds the marker, say in the log that the stubs gate is red on main, and leave the marker to the slice that owns `crypto.ts`. Do not copy the by-hand chain from this entry as a first move.
- proof: `git show origin/main:app/src/server/lib/crypto.ts | grep -c "STUB(B15)"` → `0` (46fcbfb removed the marker; at 643aa51 the same command on the branch printed 1 because the branch had merged main before 46fcbfb, recorded by the g2 review follow-up).
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2105 · A headless reviewer that writes "gate passed" has its answer replaced by the agent-os stop hook
- symptom: B12 round 1's `round-1.json` held `result: "No stage gate is met, and I am not writing to PROJECT-STATE.md..."` and nothing of the review; `num_turns` 23, the review itself was an earlier assistant message in the session transcript (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session_id>.jsonl`).
- cause: the reviewer's brief asked for the gate's final line, which is the text `GATE PASSED`; the plugin hook `agent-os/hooks/stop.sh` reads "gate passed" in a final message as a build stage closing, rejects it for a missing `PROJECT-STATE.md` write, and the reviewer's reply to that rejection became the `result`.
- rule: a headless reviewer's brief forbids the words "gate passed" and "gate met" and says its final message is the review and nothing else; the designer adds the line `Gate at review time: GATE PASSED (...)` to `ROUND-<n>.md` from `gate.txt` itself. A `result` that does not start with the review is not the round: read the transcript to see what happened, then rerun the round.
- proof: `grep -n "gate passed" launch/reel/review/brief.md` → the line of the brief that forbids the words.
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2106 · `launch/engine/sheet.mjs` squashes vertical frames into 16:9 tiles, so a reviewer cannot judge a reel from its sheet
- symptom: the first review sheet of the 1080x1920 reel showed every frame as a wide 300x169 tile, trees stretched and type squashed; a fresh reviewer scoring from that sheet would score the distortion. A replacement script that put `C\:/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf` into the ffmpeg filter through a Bash heredoc lost the backslash and failed with `No option name near '/Windows/Fonts/arial.ttf'` (P-008 again), and printed the whole 4 KB filter graph.
- cause: `sheet.mjs` sets the tile height to `w * 9 / 16` for every input; the film it was written for is 16:9.
- rule: for a vertical reel make the sheet with tiles at `w * 16 / 9` (a scratch script under `.tmp/`, written with Write, labels from the frame number divided by 30), nine tiles to a row, and print only the last lines of ffmpeg's error. Read the sheet yourself before the reviewer does.
- proof: `grep -n "w \* 9" launch/engine/sheet.mjs` → `const cols = Number(colsArg), w = Number(widthArg), h = Math.round((w * 9) / 16);`
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2107 · The reel's gate counts a cut only where a frame differs by more than 0.30: split slides and the growing tile are not cuts
- symptom: the first full render of the B12 fixture failed `cuts 3-8` with 2 and `avg shot 2.0-5.5s` with 6.00 s while looking edited: the three M9 split slides and the M10 growth are continuous motion; the two counted cuts were frame 1 of the file and the hard cut to black (the return from black onto the dark grid scores under 0.30). A later render failed `motion coverage` (83.8 percent) and `longest static run` (1.33 s) because the end card held its finished lock under a camera that moves 2 percent per second (P-025 again).
- cause: `launch/tools/motion-gate.mjs` counts `select='gt(scene,0.30)'` on a 480 px copy; a split slide changes a small part of the frame per frame, so it never reaches the threshold.
- rule: a reel needs at least one more real hard cut between two photographs (M13) besides the cut to black, with the whoosh just before it; the end card keeps a camera at 3 percent per second or more, and the light sweep is timed over the hold, not before it. Run `node launch/engine/probe.mjs motion <mp4>` to read the static runs with timecodes.
- proof: `grep -n "gt(scene,0.30)" launch/tools/motion-gate.mjs` → `37:const cutsRun = run("ffmpeg", [..."select='gt(scene,0.30)'..."`
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2108 · B12 step 5 names `ROUND-3.md` as the SHIP round, but a fresh reviewer needed twelve rounds, and each round scores the same reel differently
- symptom: rounds 1 to 11 of the fixture reel all ended `Verdict: ANOTHER ROUND`, each with one to six axes at 3 (round 6 Depth, 7 Typography, 8 Motion Depth Rhythm, 9 five axes, 10 Depth Rhythm, 11 six axes); round 12 scored 4 on all seven and said SHIP. The plan's proof (`grep -c "Verdict: SHIP" launch/reel/review/ROUND-3.md` prints 1) can never hold in that case.
- cause: the plan assumed the third round is the last. A new Opus session reads the reel again from nothing, so its score of a shot moves by a point between rounds (Depth was 3 in rounds 8 to 11 and 4 in round 12, with the grid hold still the first worst shot of round 12 as it was of round 11), and advice of one round contradicts the next (round 9: shorten the hold after the lock; round 10: bring the lock forward; round 11: end on Obsidian).
- rule: a review-loop proof names the last round, never a fixed number; run the loop until a round says SHIP and keep every round's file (`ROUND-<n>.md`, `round-<n>.json`) so the history is honest. Act on a complaint that two rounds repeat or a number can show (a frame difference, a cut count, a seam), not on every sentence; price a round at 10 to 30 minutes on an idle laptop (render 85 s, review 5 to 8 min). Never renumber rounds to make the file name fit.
- proof: `grep -m1 -o "Verdict: [A-Z ]*" launch/reel/review/ROUND-3.md launch/reel/review/ROUND-12.md` → `Verdict: ANOTHER ROUND` for round 3 and `Verdict: SHIP` for round 12 (measured 2026-10-05, branch slice/b12).
- added: 2026-10-05
- hit again: 2026-10-05, B12 g3 second pass: after the camera moves were restored to the bible's sizes (P-2114) round 13 said ANOTHER ROUND (Depth and camera 3) and round 14 said SHIP with seven axes at 4; the plan's proof still names `ROUND-3.md` (`5`, `0`, `1`), it holds on `ROUND-14.md` (`7`, `1`, `1`), and the plan line of B12 should name the last round (a change of B12.md for the orchestrator).

## P-2109 · `shot(tl, el, 0, ...)` leaves frame 0 black: the first still of a reel, and a platform thumbnail, is an Obsidian frame
- symptom: round 9's reviewer wrote "Frame 0 is a single Obsidian frame, then the oak photograph pops in on frame 1"; `ls -l .tmp/reel/frames/0000{0,1}.png` showed 37843 and 2306543 bytes. The gate had counted that false cut as one of its three (`cuts 3-8` was 3), so showing frame 0 correctly dropped the count to 2 and the gate failed until a real hard cut between photographs was added.
- cause: `shot()` of `film.js` sets the shot hidden at time 0 and visible at `tin`; with `tin` equal to 0 the second set does not run on the first seek, so the shot stays hidden. `.shot { visibility: hidden }` in the page is the other half.
- rule: the opening shot is visible from the page (`#s1 { visibility: visible; }` after `.shot`) and the scene only hides it with `tl.set(..., { autoAlpha: 0 }, <end>)`. After any change to the first frame, count `cuts` again: a cut the gate counted may have been the artefact.
- proof: `grep -n "#s1 { visibility: visible; }" launch/reel/scene.html` → one line; `ls -l .tmp/reel/frames/00000.png` after a render is over 1 MB.
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2110 · A blurred legibility pool drawn in one half of a split photograph leaves a hard edge at the seam, and a wider parallax factor doubles hard edges
- symptom: the local pool behind photograph 2's headline (`scrim(parent, opacity, box)`, a solid Obsidian box softened by `filter: blur(90px)`) drew a straight dark edge across the whole frame at y 960 in frame 130, where the two clipped halves meet. Raising the parallax factors of photograph 2 from `[1, 1.15, 1.3]` to `[1, 1.25, 1.5]` showed a second sofa cushion at the left edge (still at 5.35 s).
- cause: each half is a full-frame element clipped to 50 percent, so a pool that exists in only one half is cut at 960 px; the front plane of `depth` is the same photograph shifted by `(k - 1) * camera travel`, so a large factor against an object with a hard edge shows two copies.
- rule: draw the pool in both halves with the same box (`pool2`), and look at a still of each camera's end position before a review when a factor or a travel grows. Photograph 3 (foliage and haze) takes `[1, 1.25, 1.5]` with 30 px of drift each way (it had 180 px before the B12 g3 rework, P-2114), photograph 2 keeps `[1, 1.15, 1.3]`.
- proof: `grep -n "pool2" launch/reel/scene.mjs` → the definition and its use in both `scrim` calls; `grep -n "PAR_ROOM = " launch/reel/scene.mjs` → `[1, 1.15, 1.3]`.
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2111 · A "the hash changes" test must change only the field the hash is meant to cover, or it stays green under the mutation that breaks the hash
- symptom: B12 g2's first `specHash` test made its second spec by changing the bed through the property type; under the watched-fail that makes `specHash` ignore `sound` the test stayed green, because the property change moved the hash by another path. Watchfail printed no red, so the test measured nothing, and a second version had to be written.
- cause: a difference between two inputs proves a field matters only when that field is the one thing that differs; `buildReelSpec(property, rows)` carries the property into several fields of the spec, so a change at the property alters more than the bed.
- rule: build the second input from the first with a spread that replaces the single field under test (`{ ...spec, sound: { ...spec.sound, bed: "water" } }`), assert the same-input case equal and the changed-field case different, then watched-fail by making the hash ignore exactly that field and see the assertion red.
- proof: `grep -n "otherBed" app/tests/unit/reel/reel-spec.test.ts` → the spread of `spec.sound.bed` and the two `specHash` expectations; `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/reel/reel-spec.test.ts -t "same spec hash"` → `Tests  2 passed | 40 skipped (42)` (measured 2026-10-05); the watched-fail `b12g2-s-hash-bed` is red in that file.
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2112 · A second job in `render.yml` cannot repeat the `render` job's env lines, and the plan's reel job step list has no node 22
- symptom: B12 step 6 says the `reel` job takes "the two upload values of B8's `render` job with the same expressions". Copied as lines, `MOP_ENV: ...`, `SUPABASE_URL: ...` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: ...` would occur twice, and `render-job.test.ts` "gives the scripts MOP_ENV and the one project's Storage keys" counts each exactly once; B8's registry entries `bl` and `z` find those lines and would go stale (a find must occur once, P-066). The same step lists checkout, setup-bun and upload-artifact only, but `launch/node_modules/puppeteer-core/package.json` says `"node": ">=22.12.0"`, which the engine scripts need.
- cause: B8 wrote its tests and registry for a file with one job; the plan was written before the engine's puppeteer-core 25 was installed.
- rule: share the job env with a YAML anchor (`env: &job-env` on `render`, `env: *job-env` on `reel`; GitHub Actions and actionlint 1.7.12 both read anchors, merge keys `<<` are not supported, so a job-only value such as `CHROME_PATH` goes on its step); a job that runs `launch/engine` scripts adds `actions/setup-node` at node 24 with the pin already in the file. Before adding any job to a workflow, run the find-count one-liner of P-1100 over the registry entries of that file.
- proof: `grep -c "SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY: " .github/workflows/render.yml` → `1`; `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/jobs/render-job.test.ts` passes; `.tmp/actionlint/actionlint.exe -shellcheck= .github/workflows/render.yml` → exit 0, and on a copy with `*job-envx` → `unknown anchor 'job-envx' referenced`; the `reel` job of run 37342756765 (`gh workflow run render.yml --ref slice/b12`) read `MOP_JOB` through the alias and ended green (measured 2026-10-05, B12 g4).
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2114 · A camera move larger than the bible's passed twelve reviews because the gate's static limit asked for it, and a 5.6 s end shot at the bible's size is static to the gate
- symptom: the reel handed in by B12 g3's first pass pushed 11 percent (photographs 1 and 3), 12 percent (the colonnade) and 40 percent on the last shot (`z` 0 to 0.4), with 140 to 320 px of sideways travel; the last shot opened with a 52 px Obsidian bar down its left edge that shrank to 0 over 15 frames (12.40 to 12.87 s), because the planes extend only 10 percent (108 px) past the frame and the travel started at `x: 160` with `align: 0`. MOTION-BIBLE M6 says 6 to 9 percent. Restoring the sizes alone failed the gate: `motion coverage 77.7%`, `longest static run 2.07s` (15.90 to 17.97 s).
- cause: a 9 percent push over 5.6 s is 1.6 percent a second, below what the gate reads as motion (P-2107 asks for 3), and the first pass met the gate by enlarging the push and the travel instead of adding a move of the vocabulary; `moves.test.ts` checks ease literals and banned words, not the size of a move, and no reviewer sheet showed the first 15 frames of a shot (P-2116).
- rule: a push is 9 percent or less (`z` at most 0.09), a crane is M7 (vertical drift, 1.5 degrees at most), a sideways drift is 30 px at most, and every travel is checked against the plane margin, which is 108 px sideways and 192 px up and down before the factor of the front plane (`inset: -10%`). When the static limit fails on a long shot, add a move of the vocabulary: an M7 crane and an M11 light sweep timed over the hold. Measured on the last shot (12.4 to 18 s, share of frames the probe counts as moving in that window): 20 px drift and the sweep at 13.0, 77.7 percent of the whole reel with a 2.07 s run; sweep at 15.3, 44.0; sweep at 15.3 and no 1.5 px softening, 53.6; 30 px drift each way and the sweep at 15.9, 73.5; the same without the softening, 93.4; final (crane 80 px each way and 0.8 degrees, 30 px drift, no softening, sweep at 15.9), 97.2 percent of the whole reel and a longest run of 0.50 s.
- proof: `grep -n "dolly(" launch/reel/scene.mjs` → five lines, every `z` at or under 0.09 and every `x` between -30 and 30; `node launch/tools/motion-gate.mjs .tmp/reel/reel.mp4 --w 1080 --h 1920 --min-s 15 --max-s 25 --min-cuts 3 --max-cuts 8` → `PASS  motion coverage >= 85%  97.2%`, `PASS  longest static run <= 1.0s  0.50s`, `GATE PASSED` (measured 2026-10-05, B12 g3 second pass). A guard in `app/tests/unit/reel/moves.test.ts` on the `z` and `x` of each `dolly` call is a follow-up of another group.
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2115 · Two audio renders of the same cues are not the same bytes, and the gate's true peak moved by 0.3 dB between full pipelines
- symptom: a reviewer re-ran the pipeline on B12 g3's first-pass code and measured `-2.59 dBTP` where the ROUND-12 header says `-2.29`. This pass measured both on unchanged cues: `-18.23 LUFS, -2.59 dBTP` on its first pipeline, then `-18.19 LUFS, -2.29 dBTP` and `-18.23 LUFS, -2.29 dBTP` on the next two; two `audio.mjs` renders of the same cues gave different SHA-256 (`e5db3b7367b52224...` and `905c6df25942aef3...`) while `loudnorm` printed the same `input_i -33.69` and `input_tp -18.02` for both.
- cause: UNPROVEN. The sound is rendered by an offline audio context in headless Chrome and then normalised in two passes by `encode.mjs`; a float difference in the render or the limiter pass is the likely source.
- rule: contract invariant 6 (same bytes) holds for the stills, not for the audio; never assert byte equality of an audio render, and read a gate line of a ROUND header as the render that reviewer saw: a re-run agrees on the pass marks and differs in the third digit of the peak. Compare the gate by pass or fail, with the margin kept (true peak well under -1, flatness 0.160 against 0.15 is the thin one).
- proof: `node launch/engine/audio.mjs launch/reel/scene.html .tmp/a1.wav --query "spec=/launch/reel/fixture-spec.json&cues=/.tmp/reel/cues.json"` twice (a different `.wav` name each time), then `sha256sum .tmp/a1.wav .tmp/a2.wav` → two different hashes (measured 2026-10-05, B12 g3).
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2116 · A review from sheets taken every half second cannot see an artefact that lasts under half a second at the start of a shot
- symptom: the 52 px bar of P-2114 lasted 15 frames; the sheets of twelve rounds sampled 12.25 s and 12.75 s, where it is under 20 px, and none of the twelve reviewers named it although the brief asks for seams at an edge.
- cause: a sheet of 18 frames per 9 seconds cannot show 0.5 s; a reviewer reads what the sheet shows.
- rule: before every round the designer scans every frame: from each edge count the consecutive columns (rows) whose mean luma is under 22 (Obsidian is luma 17, so 15 misses it) and treat any run above 0 outside the cut to black, the empty field and the grid (frames 246 to 340), whose Obsidian is by design, as a defect; and each round's material holds `sheet-c.jpg`, six frames 0.1 s apart after each hard cut. The scan is a scratch script (a `sharp` read of each frame); with the old geometry (`x: 160`) it printed `"l":52` on frame 372, with the fixed scene `0` on all 540 frames except the black ones.
- proof: `grep -c "sheet-c.jpg" launch/reel/review/brief.md` → `1` (the brief names the cut sheet); the scan's result is in the log block of `workspace/05-plans/logs/B12.md` (measured 2026-10-05, B12 g3).
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2117 · A `( ... ) &` subshell in the Bash tool keeps running after the call returns, and a second start writes into the same folder
- symptom: a reviewer started a reel capture as `( node launch/engine/capture.mjs ... > .tmp/reel-capture.log ) &`, saw no log, started a second capture into the same `frames` folder, and both wrote it at once: the shared log ended `done: 287 frames in done: 540 frames in 150s`. Every PNG had to be validated before the encode, because a frame can be half written by one process while the other reads it.
- cause: the Bash tool returns while a backgrounded subshell is still alive, and its output file is only visible after the first flush; "no log yet" was read as "not running".
- rule: start a long job with the tool's `run_in_background` (it names an output file and notifies on exit), or check `.tmp/<name>.log` and the process list before a second start; never start a second writer into a folder the first may still own (P-011), and clear the folder (`rm -rf`) only after the first process is known to have ended.
- proof: `tail -c 120 .tmp/reel-capture.log` in the reviewer's tree ended `done: 287 frames in done: 540 frames in 150s` (measured 2026-10-05, B12 g3 review; the log is a scratch file, so the line is quoted from the review report).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2118 · `will-change` on a layer fixes its raster scale at the first paint, so a frame of a full capture differs from a still of the same time by up to 48 levels
- symptom: with the GPU off (P-052), frame 00510 of a full 4-worker capture of the reel differed from the `--at 17` still by up to 48 levels over 1.2 million samples (box 0,36 to 1079,1722), and frame 00045 from the 1.5 s still by 2 levels over 205 thousand; frame 00270 matched. A reviewer had measured the same difference with the GPU on (max 47) and suspected the layers.
- cause: `scene.html` carried `will-change: transform, filter` on `.plane` and `will-change: transform` on `.half`, `.tile`, `.tile > div` and the title spans. Chrome rasterises such a layer once, at the scale it has when it is first painted, and keeps that raster while the transform animates, so a capture that seeks forward through a push paints the first scale and a fresh seek paints the target scale. Without the property: 510 differs from the still in 6 samples by 1 level, 45 by 0.
- rule: a scene captured frame by frame carries no `will-change`: the capture seeks, so no layer is promoted for an animation Chrome has to predict, and each frame is painted at its own transform. Compare a range capture and a still of the same frame before trusting a fixed scale.
- proof: `grep -c "will-change" launch/reel/scene.html` → `0`; `node launch/engine/capture.mjs launch/reel/scene.html --query "spec=/launch/reel/fixture-spec.json&cues=/.tmp/reel/cues.json" --w 1080 --h 1920 --workers 1 --from 16.5 --to 17.1 --out .tmp/t-range`, then the same with `--at 17 --out .tmp/t-still`, a pixel compare of `00510.png` and `t017.00.png` → 6 differing samples, max 1 (measured 2026-10-06, B12 g3 third pass, GPU off).
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-06, B12 g3 review: the 6 samples above are the one-worker range capture only. In a full 4-worker capture frame 00510 still differs from the `--at 17` still on 1,087,467 samples by 1 level, in two separate full captures (max 1 is invisible, so the reel is not at fault, but "full-render frame against still, 6 samples" in the proof JSON is imprecise). Proof of the full figure: the full capture `node launch/engine/capture.mjs launch/reel/scene.html --query "spec=/launch/reel/fixture-spec.json&cues=/.tmp/reel/cues.json" --w 1080 --h 1920 --workers 4 --out .tmp/full`, then a pixel compare of `.tmp/full/frames/00510.png` and `t017.00.png` of the `--at 17` still → 1,087,467 differing samples, max 1.

## P-2119 · Two full captures of the reel with the GPU off still differ in 14 frames by one level on 6 samples, so byte equality of the MP4 is UNPROVEN
- symptom: after P-052's flags and P-2118, two full 4-worker captures of the same spec gave `diff` of the two `sha256sum *.png` lists = 14 of 540 frames (473 to 478, 480, 484, 486, 490, 494, 496, 501, 507, 15.77 to 16.90 s), each differing in 4 to 6 samples by 1 level in one column near x=494, y=1015. Stills at 1.5, 9 and 17 s are byte-identical over three runs.
- cause: UNPROVEN. The frames sit in the last shot with the 80 px crane and the 30 px drift; frames before the sweep starts (15.9 s) differ too, so the sweep alone is not it, and a frame differs between two runs that have the same seek history, so it is not only history.
- rule: invariant 6 holds for stills (same spec, same SHA-256), not for the full MP4: never assert MP4 byte equality, compare a render by the gate and by pixel difference with a margin (1 level on a few samples is noise). Anyone who finds the cause records it here.
- proof: `cd .tmp/reel/frames && sha256sum *.png > ../hash-a.txt`, the same for a second capture, `diff hash-a.txt hash-b.txt | grep -c '^<'` → `14` (measured 2026-10-06, B12 g3 third pass).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2120 · B12 step 7 lines that could not be built as written: `write_audit` refuses the approver on `properties.video_attach`, and `<ts>_reel.sql` has nothing to hold
- symptom: B12 g5. The plan's `attach_reel` audits through `write_audit` with `actor_id = assets.approved_by` and `actor_kind 'human'`, and `reel.db.test.ts` is to assert that actor. On mop-dev `select count(*) from public.action_roles where action like 'properties.video%'` printed `0`, and B7's `write_audit` raises `forbidden` (42501) for a non-null actor on an action with no `action_roles` row (`actor.db.test.ts` "an action with no action_roles row"), so every reel approval would roll back. Four smaller lines: the Files list names `<ts>_reel.sql` and a separate `db:fn` migration, but Data changes puts the `create trigger` in the function file, so `<ts>_reel.sql` would be empty; the plan's `p_caption: null, p_alt_text: null` cannot be sent through the typed client (P-721), and leaving them out is the same default null; the duration formula `floor(d / 60)` with `round(d) % 60` gives `0:00` for 59.6 s; and the trigger falsified B9's `assets.db.test.ts` reel guard case (one `main` file) and `tests/unit/error-codes.test.ts` (`reel_files_missing` not a key), two files the step does not name (P-1202).
- cause: the plan was written before B7's actor check (invariant 18, DB-04) was on main: the audit action of a state change must be a matrix action, and `properties.video_attach` is not one. The file list was written per object, not per migration.
- rule: before writing an audit call, check that its action has an `action_roles` row (`git grep -n "'<action>'" -- app/supabase/migrations/*_action_roles.sql`); a trigger-written row with no matrix action is a system row (`actor_id` null, `actor_kind` null, note `system`, G43), and the human stays on the row of the function that fired the trigger. B12 g5 built it that way and returned `blocked` for the orchestrator's ruling between that and a matrix entry. A migration that is only function sources is one `bun run db:fn --name <name>` file. Round to whole seconds before splitting minutes and seconds.
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run db:psql -- -Atc "select count(*) from public.action_roles where action like 'properties.video%'"` → `0` (measured 2026-10-06); `git grep -n "no.such_action" -- app/tests/db/actor.db.test.ts` shows the refusal case; with the B12 migration as prelude, `tests/db/assets.db.test.ts` gave `Tests  1 failed | 53 passed (54)` (`reel approves when complete`) before the reel row got its video and poster, `54 passed` after.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2122 · A scratch registry folder reused from an earlier session replays every old file in it
- symptom: B12 c7 built a scratch registry for the eight `reel.db.test.ts` `sql` entries (the migration prepended, `run` rewritten to node, P-312) in a folder that already held `B12.json`, `B15.json`, `B7.json`, `B8b.json` and `R.json` from an earlier lane. `watchfail --registry <folder>` printed `replayed 135: ok 84, bad 0, stale 51`, ran for about 9 minutes and said nothing about the eight entries, because the tail showed only B8b and R lines.
- cause: `--registry` replays every `*.json` in the folder, and the scratchpad of a session is shared across tasks, so `mkdir -p` kept the old files.
- rule: build a scratch registry in a folder you create new (`rm -rf` then `mkdir`, or a name with the task in it) and read `ls <folder>` before the replay; ask for the count (`replayed 8`) you expect.
- proof: `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry <fresh folder holding only the eight reel entries>` → `watchfail: replayed 8: ok 8, bad 0, stale 0` (B12 c7, 2026-10-06; the reused folder gave `replayed 135`).
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B11 g3 and its review: the author left a stale `B3.json` in the scratch folder, and the reviewer's 7-entry replay, built in a folder that already held `B10.json`, `B10g3.json` and `B7.json`, printed `replayed 77: ok 7, bad 1, stale 69` with `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: wrong reason (B7:b7-5a-db-email-case)` and exit 2. Make the folder with `mktemp -d`, run `ls` on it, and expect the count of your own entries.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2123 · A `<video>` without a captions track fails `jsx-a11y/media-has-caption`; the reel has none by design
- symptom: B12 g1's first `bun run check` stopped at `lint`: `ReelPlayer.tsx 44:9 error Media elements such as <audio> and <video> must have a <track> for captions  jsx-a11y/media-has-caption`. The dossier's `<video>` in `gallery.tsx` passes only because it is `muted`; the admin reel player plays sound, so the rule applies.
- cause: the reel has sound design and no speech (S36), so there is no captions track to give (ASSUMED G30), and the rule has no way to know that.
- rule: a player of the reel, or of any other speechless film that plays sound, carries `// eslint-disable-next-line jsx-a11y/media-has-caption -- the reel has no speech, so it has no captions track (G30)` on the line above the element (R03 asks for the reason); never add a fake `<track>`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx eslint src/admin/assets/ReelPlayer.tsx` → no output; with the comment removed → the error above (B12 g1, 2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2124 · `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` in a long-lived lane replays every earlier group's entries too: 187 replays, over 10 minutes
- symptom: the reviewer's pass (ruling H60 (c)) says to replay `--changed origin/main`; in slice/b12 it selected 187 entries of B9 and B12 (`replayed 187: ok 125, bad 62`), ran past the 590 s tool limit, and left `src/db/types.ts` modified for as long as it ran (a replay mutates a file, so the tree is not yours to edit meanwhile). Whether the 62 bad ones are db entries that need a database the lane lacks was not measured: UNPROVEN.
- cause: `--changed` compares each entry's file and test with the ref, and a lane that carries earlier groups differs from main in all of them.
- rule: replay the entries of the files of your own group by id (`for id in ...; do node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only <id>; done`) and run it in the background with a bounded wait; read `git status` after any replay that was interrupted.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b12g1-film-label` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B12:b12g1-film-label` in seconds (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B10 g2: the brief's pass (c) `watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` was run in the foreground under `timeout 110`; the killed replay left a mutation of `B2:anp-exact` in `scripts/lib/assert-not-production.mjs` (`git status` showed the file modified, restored with `git checkout`). Replay own entries by id, never under `timeout`.

## P-2125 · A scratch output file with a common name is overwritten by another lane's run: the review read someone else's results and ran the 15-minute check again
- symptom: the g1 review of B12 wrote `bun run check > check.txt` into the shared session scratchpad; the tail showed `RUN  v5.0.2 E:/mop-build/email/app` and `Failed to start forks worker for test files E:/mop-build/site-review/app/tests/unit/consent-notice.test.tsx`, although the command ran in `E:/mop-build/video-review/app`. The result was unusable and the check, about 15 minutes, ran again (about 20 minutes lost).
- cause: `C:/Users/DELL/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/E--Matter-Of-Place/<session>/scratchpad` is one folder shared by every parallel lane agent and reviewer of the build; another lane's `> check.txt` replaced the file mid-run.
- rule: a scratch output file carries the lane, the group and the process id in its name (`b12g1-videoreview-check-$$.txt`), and before a result is trusted, the paths inside it are read back: every path must lie in your own tree.
- proof: `out=b12g1-demo-$$.txt; (cd "$PWD" && pwd -W) > "$out"; grep -c "$(pwd -W)" "$out"; rm "$out"` → `1` (a file named with `$$` is yours alone, and the path inside it names your tree; a file that names `E:/mop-build/<another lane>` is not your result).
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-06, B5 g5: a scratch script named `add-entries.mjs` was overwritten by B7 g4's script of the same name between two reads (harmless, mine had already run); scratch files carry the lane and group in the name (`b5g5-...`).

## P-1212 · Resend's `GET /domains` list carries no record status, so a plan line that prints `spf pass` and `dkim pass` from that one call cannot be built
- symptom: B5 step 5 says `resend-check.ts` reads the three domains "with one `GET /domains`" and prints `spf pass` and `dkim pass` for each. The answer of `GET /domains` holds `id`, `name`, `status`, `region` and `capabilities` per domain and no `records`; printing `spf pass` from `status: verified` would be a guess dressed as a reading.
- cause: the per-record statuses (`record: "DKIM"` or `"SPF"`, `status: "verified"`) are only in `GET /domains/<id>`. Resend labels the return-path records (MX, TXT and CNAME on `send` and `rsend`) `SPF`.
- rule: `resend-check.ts` lists once and then reads each verified domain by id, a read only; `spf pass` means every record labelled SPF reads `verified`. A plan line that prints a finer fact than the call it names returns must read the call that holds it, and the log says so.
- proof: with `.env` loaded, `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RESEND_API_KEY" https://api.resend.com/domains | grep -c '"records"'` → `0`, and the same on `https://api.resend.com/domains/<id>` of `matterofplace.com` → `1` (2026-10-06, B5 g1).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1213 · A new write in a hook's effect leaves rows behind in a committed-mode api test that cleans only the tables it knew
- symptom: B5 step 6 made `hooks/resend.ts` call `apply_email_event` after every verified event. B3's `tests/api/resend.api.test.ts` (committed mode, run against `mop-dev`) sends `email.complained` for random `complaint+<uuid>@example.invalid` addresses, stayed green, and left one `email_suppressions` row and one `email_events` row per case on `mop-dev`.
- cause: the test's cleanup deletes `subscribers`, `webhook_receipts` and `rate_limits` only; a green run does not show a table the cleanup never heard of. The DL-06 case has its own cleanup block, so patching the shared `run` helper alone still left one row of each.
- rule: when a step adds a write to code that a committed-mode test drives, count the rows that test leaves (`select count(*) ... where email like '<its prefix>%'`) after a run, and add every table to every cleanup block of that file.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx vitest run --project db tests/api/resend.api.test.ts; bun run db:psql -- -Atc "select (select count(*) from email_suppressions where email like 'complaint+%'), (select count(*) from email_events where to_email like 'complaint+%')"` → `0|0` (measured 2026-10-06, B5 g2: `1|1` before the second block was fixed).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1214 · A bank line that quotes a backslash escape, written through the shell, lands as a real line break and the entry loses the fact it records
- symptom: B5 g1 step 5 wrote its P-008 hit-again line (the `node -` heredoc whose find strings held a `\n`) through the Bash tool; the line was stored as "... with backticks and `" and then "` in its find strings ...", so the text that broke the heredoc was gone. The same defect sat in the B3 g1 hit-again line (`\n` became a real newline). The reviewer found both; `check-gotchas.mjs` printed `check-gotchas: OK` throughout because it reads headings and field names, not bullet bodies.
- cause: the Bash tool turns a backslash-n typed inside a shell argument or heredoc into a line break (P-008), and the check cannot see a bullet that was split in two.
- rule: a bank line that holds a backslash goes in with the Edit tool, and after writing it you grep for a line that starts with a backtick (a split bullet): none may exist outside the two code fences of the entry template.
- proof: `grep -nE '^`' GOTCHAS.md` → only the two template fence lines (`33:` and `42:` with three backticks) after the repair; before it, lines 199 and 212 also matched (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1215 · B5 step 7's plan lines that could not be built as written: five places where the change reaches files the step does not name
- symptom: settled in the code and named in the log, none a block: (1) the plan's page is `src/routes/place-notes.tsx`, but the route file that redirected `/place-notes` is `src/routes/_site.place-notes.tsx` (the pathless `_site` layout), so the page replaced that file; (2) "the server allow-list imports that array, so there is no second edit" is false: `tests/unit/analytics.test.ts` holds a `Record<AnalyticsEvent, true>` and fails the typecheck until it names `newsletter_confirmed`; (3) the new landing `/place-notes?confirmed=0` is also asserted by `tests/api/resend.api.test.ts` (the DL-06 c complaint case), which the step does not name; (4) "append" to `analyticsEvents` staled B3's registry entry `b3-g4-an-unique` (P-066); (5) `docs/runbooks/email.md` said both ends were still the `STUB(B5 step 7)` bodies, which became false in this step.
- cause: the step's file list was written from the plan's own files, not from `git grep` over the strings and types the change moves (`stories?confirmed`, `AnalyticsEvent`, `STUB(B5 step 7)`).
- rule: before building a step that changes a public string, a union or a stub, `git grep` the old value across `app/` (tests, registries and runbooks included) and change every hit in the same commit; take the route file name from `src/routes`, never from the plan.
- proof: `cd app && git grep -n "stories?confirmed" -- .` prints only `tests/mutations/B5.json`, once, the `replace` of `b5-api-landing` (the first proof was scoped to `src tests/api tests/unit docs`, left out `scripts/`, and passed while `scripts/api-smoke.mjs` still expected `/stories?confirmed=0`; the review found it and the fix round changed it, 2026-10-06); `git grep -c "STUB(B5 step 7)" -- .` prints nothing (exit 1); `ls src/routes/_site.place-notes.tsx` lists the file (2026-10-06, B5 g3).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1216 · `quiet.mjs` on a green Playwright run shows the last 12 lines, which are `[WebServer]` warnings, so the `N passed` line is lost and the run must be repeated
- symptom: `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8868 node ../workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- bun run test:e2e -- redirects.spec.ts sweep.spec.ts` printed `quiet: ok (236 lines, showing the last 12)` and twelve `[WebServer]` lines from wrangler; the count of passed tests and the `/place-notes` row were not among them, so the 9-minute run was repeated with the output written to a file.
- cause: `quiet.mjs` keeps the tail of a green run, and wrangler's webServer writes its warnings after Playwright's summary line.
- rule: run a Playwright proof with its whole output redirected to a file in the session scratchpad (absolute path) and grep that file for `passed|failed|flaky` and the rows the proof names; keep `quiet.mjs` for vitest and builds.
- proof: `cd app && E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8868 bun run test:e2e -- redirects.spec.ts sweep.spec.ts > "$SCRATCH/e2e.txt" 2>&1; grep -aE "[0-9]+ passed" "$SCRATCH/e2e.txt"` prints `114 passed (8.9m)` on slice/b5 at B5 g3 (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1217 · `GET /auth/v1/admin/users` on `mop-dev` answers 500 `Database error finding users`, so a test auth user is found by SQL and deleted by id
- symptom: B5 g4 cleaned up the auth user its invite test made. Listing users through the Auth admin API (`?per_page=1000`, then `?per_page=50`) answered `{"code":500,"error_code":"unexpected_failure","msg":"Database error finding users"}` both times, so the user could not be found that way; supabase-js `auth.admin.listUsers()` calls the same endpoint.
- cause: 2 of the 9 rows of `auth.users` hold a null in a token column (`confirmation_token`, `recovery_token`, `email_change_token_new` or `email_change`), the shape a row inserted by SQL rather than through Auth has, and a known cause of this GoTrue error. UNPROVEN that these two rows are the cause here (nothing was changed to test it), and which script inserted them is not established.
- rule: on `mop-dev`, find an auth user by SQL (`select id from auth.users where email = '<address>'` through `bun run db:psql`) and delete it with `DELETE /auth/v1/admin/users/<id>` and the service role key; never rely on the list endpoint until the null columns are fixed. A script that seeds `auth.users` by SQL writes `''` into the token columns, never null.
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run db:psql -- -Atc "select count(*) filter (where confirmation_token is null or recovery_token is null or email_change_token_new is null or email_change is null) from auth.users"` → `2` on 2026-10-06, and `curl -s "https://$DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF.supabase.co/auth/v1/admin/users?per_page=50" -H "apikey: $DEV_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY" -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"` → the 500 above; the delete by id answered `200`.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1218 · Playwright cannot start a browser from Bun on this laptop: `chromium.launch()` never returns, `connectOverCDP` times out
- symptom: B5 g5's first `scripts/email-shots.ts` imported `chromium` from `@playwright/test` and ran under `bun run email:shots`. It printed nothing and had to be stopped after more than 2 minutes, with `chrome-headless-shell.exe` children still running; a 6-line scratch script printed `launching` and then nothing for 60 s (`timeout` exit 124). A second approach, starting Chrome by hand with `--remote-debugging-port=0` and calling `connectOverCDP(ws://127.0.0.1:<port>/...)` from Bun, failed with `TimeoutError: connectOverCDP: Timeout 30000ms exceeded` while the log said `<ws connecting>`.
- cause: Playwright talks to Chromium over a pipe or a WebSocket; both fail under Bun 1.3.13 on Windows. The same `chromium.launch()` under `node` returned in about a second and `setContent` worked. `bunx playwright test` is not affected because the `playwright` bin runs under Node.
- rule: a script that drives Playwright is a Node file (`.mjs` with JSDoc, R02: the runner cannot be Bun). When the rest of the work needs Bun (TSX, `src/` imports), the Bun script writes its files and spawns `node scripts/lib/<name>.mjs`, as `scripts/email-shots.ts` does with `scripts/lib/email-shots-page.mjs`. Never wrap a Playwright launch in a `bun run` command without a `timeout`, and never try a third way into the browser from Bun.
- proof: `cd app && timeout 60 bun scripts/zz-t.ts` (a file that only does `await chromium.launch()`) → exit 124; the same call in `zz-t.mjs` under `timeout 60 node` → exit 0 (measured 2026-10-06, B5 g5); `bun run email:shots` → 13 `ok <key> 600x900` lines.
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B7 g1 step 6 review: a signed-in admin probe written as TypeScript (`scratchpad/b7rev-signed.ts`, calling `chromium.launch()` and importing `tests/e2e/helpers/session.ts`) hung silently under `bun` twice (`timeout 150`, exit 124, no output, about 5 minutes) before the same logic as `.mjs` under `node` exited 0. A signed-in admin probe that uses `session.ts` runs under `node`, or as a spec through `bunx playwright test`, never under `bun`. `confirmIn()` calls `page.goto` with a relative URL, so outside the Playwright runner it needs a browser context created with `baseURL` (for example `http://127.0.0.1:8949`). Proof: `timeout 60 bun <probe>.ts` → exit 124 and `timeout 60 node <probe>.mjs` → exit 0.

## P-1219 · The chain proof's `admin_notify` is `skipped not_allow_listed` on mop-dev: the admin recipient is the public contact address, not `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL`
- symptom: B5 g5's first `bun run scripts/email-chain.ts` on mop-dev exited 1 after 180 s with `email-chain: no complete chain within 180 s; jobs: send_received done ; notify_admin_received done`. `email_messages` held `received skipped dry_...` (dry_run) and `admin_notify skipped` with no `resend_id` and error `not_allow_listed`. The g3 log had predicted two `dry_` rows from the allow-list reading alone.
- cause: `resolveAdminRecipients` takes `settings.notifications.recipients`, then `settings.site.contact.email`, then `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL`. mop-dev has no `notifications` row and `site.contact.email` is `hello@matterofplace.com`, which `settings.email.dev_recipients` (`admin@matterofplace.com`, `admin+*@matterofplace.com`, `*@resend.dev`) does not hold. The secret `ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL=admin@matterofplace.com` is never reached.
- rule: a prediction that a send reaches an allow-listed address names the address the resolver returns, read from the settings rows, not the secret. To prove the chain on mop-dev, insert `notifications = {"recipients": ["admin@matterofplace.com"]}`, run the script under the writer lock, and delete the row in the same shell script; never leave it.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run db:psql -- -Atc "select value->>'contact' from settings where key='site'"` shows the contact address, and `select error from email_messages where template_key='admin_notify' order by created_at desc limit 1` → `not_allow_listed`; with the `notifications` row, `bun run scripts/email-chain.ts` printed `received skipped dry_...` and `admin_notify skipped dry_...`, exit 0 (measured 2026-10-06, B5 g5).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1220 · `scripts/automation-smoke.ts` exits 1 on mop-dev with `automation_put_recipe (smoke) failed: forbidden`: its all-zero actor has no `user_roles` row, and B7's `write_audit` refuses it
- symptom: B5 g5's proof "`bun run scripts/automation-smoke.ts` still exits 0" printed `lock mop-dev-tests held` then `automation-smoke: automation_put_recipe (smoke) failed: forbidden`, exit 1, at its first write. Nothing of B5 is on that path.
- cause: the script passes `NO_ACTOR = 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` as `p_actor` with kind `human`. Since B7 g1's migration `20261005050700_admin_audit.sql`, `write_audit` looks a non-null actor up in `user_roles` and raises `forbidden` (42501) when it has no role of that kind (invariant 18, DB-04). B8b's script predates it.
- rule: UNPROVEN for B5; the owner of `scripts/automation-smoke.ts` (B8b) passes a null actor (the system) or a real staff user, then re-runs it. A group that is told to run another slice's script as a proof reports its red result and the cause, and does not edit the script.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run scripts/automation-smoke.ts` → `automation-smoke: automation_put_recipe (smoke) failed: forbidden` (measured 2026-10-06, B5 g5, tree of `slice/b5` merged with main at 99dda79); `grep -n "forbidden" supabase/sql/functions/write_audit.sql` → three raises.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1221 · A new script that copies another script's `.env` reader fails jscpd with a 72-token clone, and the reader is then rewritten
- symptom: B5 g4's `scripts/auth-invite-test.ts` first carried a copy of the `.env` reader of `scripts/email-test.ts` (`readFileSync(new URL("../../.env", import.meta.url), "utf8").replaceAll("\r", "")` and the line parser after it). `bun run jscpd` in `bun run check` reported a clone of 72 tokens between the two files, and the script was reworked, a second attempt.
- cause: the script needed the project URL and the service role key and the quickest source was the file the neighbour already parses. A second `.env` parser is also the shape that read `SUPABASE_URL` from the shell on 2026-10-06 (G-901, P-331): the dev profile is the one place that names mop-dev.
- rule: a new script reads secrets through `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` and gets its project from `devProject()` of `scripts/lib/storage-env.ts`; it never parses `.env` itself. A script that needs a name the profile does not export adds the name to the profile, not a reader to the script.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c readFileSync scripts/auth-invite-test.ts` prints `0` and `grep -n "devProject" scripts/auth-invite-test.ts` prints the import from `./lib/storage-env.ts` and its call; `bun run jscpd` exits 0 on `slice/b5` at B5 g4 (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1922 · B17 step 7 names two proofs a lane cannot reach: the `s-maxage` on the feed's 200, and the W3C validator on a preview
- symptom: the plan says the feed's 200 "reads `public, max-age=3600, s-maxage=3600`", and a test written to that string failed: the answer carries `public, max-age=3600` only. The proof "W3C Feed Validation Service on the public preview URL" cannot run from a lane before the workflow opens the pull request (no preview exists), and the validator refused the fallback: a POST of the feed text (`manual=1`, with and without `output=soap12`) answered `502 error code: 502` twice, and a GET with `rawdata=` of the real 9 KB feed answered `414 URI Too Long`.
- cause: `cachedResponse` stores the long edge lifetime on the stored copy (`toStored`) and `answer` replaces it with `browserCacheControl(kind)` on every response that leaves the Worker, so the `s-maxage` is only on the entry in the edge cache. The validator proof needs a deployed URL.
- rule: read the stored copy's `cache-control` out of a fake edge cache to prove `s-maxage=3600`, and the answer's header for the browser lifetime; a step that needs a public preview URL is UNPROVEN in the lane log until the workflow's preview exists, and the log says so. The feed itself is proved well formed by parsing it as XML (`new JSDOM(text, { contentType: "application/xml" })` throws on a malformed document).
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/essentials.test.ts -t "feed: is stored as kind doc"` passes; registry entry `b17-g6-feed-kind` (`"doc"` to `"json"`) turns it red; `curl -s -D - http://127.0.0.1:8938/feed.xml` on the built Worker shows `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600` (measured 2026-10-06, B17 g6).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1923 · A polling script that checks its deadline only between requests never reaches it when one request stalls
- symptom: B17 g5's review ran `node scripts/wait-status.mjs http://127.0.0.1:8946/ 503 3` against a server that accepts and never answers; under `timeout 25` it printed nothing and ended `exit 124` after 25 s instead of the timeout line and exit 1 after 3 s. That script runs inside `with-maintenance.ts`, so while it hung the maintenance flag stayed true on mop-dev and every preview and local build answered 503, past the plan's 16 second bound. The g5 author's earlier `exit 124 after 60 s with no output` (P-1918's hit-again line) matches it.
- cause: each `fetch` had no `signal`; Node's fetch waits for headers up to undici's default `headersTimeout` (300 s by its documentation, not measured here), and the `Date.now() >= deadline` check ran only after a request returned.
- rule: every request of a poll loop carries `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(1, deadline - Date.now()))` and counts an abort as a miss; a wrapper that holds a shared setting while its command runs never relies on an outer `timeout` for its bound.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/essentials.test.ts -t "wait-status"` passes (1 test, about 1 s); registry entry `b17-wait-status-stall` (the `signal` line deleted) turns it red with `expected null to be 1` after the 10 s spawn limit (measured 2026-10-06, B17 g5 rework).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2004 · `bunx playwright test --project admin <spec>` reads the spec as a second project name
- symptom: B7 step 2's proof, run as written (`bunx playwright test --project admin tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts`), ended at once with `Error: Project(s) "tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts" not found. Available projects: "desktop", ..., "admin"`.
- cause: Playwright's `--project` takes several values, so a separate word after it is another project, not a test file.
- rule: write the project with an equals sign, `--project=admin`, in every Playwright command, as the B4 and B13 proofs already do.
- proof: `cd app && bunx playwright test --project admin tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts --list` → `Project(s) "tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts" not found`; `bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts --list` → `Total: 4 tests in 1 file` (measured 2026-10-05, B7 g2).
- added: 2026-10-05
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B6 g3: step 9's proof line is written `--project admin tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts`; it answered `Project(s) "tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts" not found` and the first run was lost; `--project=admin` ran it.

## P-2005 · Playwright's `page.request` does not send a `Secure` cookie to `http://127.0.0.1`, which the browser does
- symptom: the admin sign-in spec landed on `/admin` after the confirm POST, and `page.request.get("/api/admin/me")` answered 401 while `fetch("/api/admin/me")` inside the page answered 200; `context.cookies()` held `mop_csrf` and the session cookie, both `secure=true`, domain `127.0.0.1`.
- cause: Chromium treats a loopback origin as potentially trustworthy and keeps and sends `Secure` cookies over plain HTTP there; Playwright's own API request context applies the plain rule and leaves a `Secure` cookie off an `http:` request. The admin cookies are `Secure` by contract (invariant 11).
- rule: an e2e check that the admin session holds runs in the page (`page.evaluate(() => fetch("/api/admin/me"))`, `meStatus` of `tests/e2e/helpers/session.ts`), never through `page.request` or the `request` fixture, until a spec runs on an `https` origin.
- proof: in `tests/e2e/helpers/session.ts` make `meStatus` return `(await page.request.get("/api/admin/me")).status()`; with the dev server warm on the lane port, `E2E_TARGET=url E2E_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8948 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts` fails the invite case at that line with `Expected: 200 Received: 401` (measured 2026-10-05, B7 g2, the spec as first written); with `meStatus` as committed, `4 passed`.
- added: 2026-10-05

- symptom: `E2E_TARGET=dev E2E_PORT=8948 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts` ended with `Error: Timed out waiting 120000ms from config.webServer.` and `script "dev" exited with code 1`; with the server started by hand the first run still failed four cases at `toBeVisible` (5000 ms) while vite printed `optimizer bundling dependencies` and reloaded the page. Stop the server by its own `bun.exe` id (P-830).

(56.8s)` and `the confirm page spends nothing... (56.5s)`, both `expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed ... Timeout: 30000ms`) and the second run on the warm server printed `4 passed (6.0m)`. ## P-2007 · A file under `tests/fixtures/` may not read the clock, even when every test that calls it fakes `Date`
- symptom: B7 g2's `tests/fixtures/supabase-auth.ts` minted tokens with `Date.now()`; the nine step 2 test files passed under `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })`, and the full `bun run test` failed `tests/unit/clock.test.ts > the fixture files > read no wall clock, no Math.random and no random uuid` with `expected [ 'supabase-auth.ts' ] to deeply equal []`.
- cause: `clock.test.ts` reads the text of every fixture file and refuses `Date.now()`, `new Date()`, `Math.random` and `randomUUID` (R51); it does not know which callers fake the clock.
- rule: a fixture takes `now` from its caller (`key.token({ now: Date.now() })`, `sessionCookie(token, now)`), and a fixed row stamp is a literal ISO string; run `bunx vitest run tests/unit/clock.test.ts` after adding any file under `tests/fixtures/`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/clock.test.ts` passes; with `Date.now()` back in the `token` default of `tests/fixtures/supabase-auth.ts` it fails naming `supabase-auth.ts` (measured 2026-10-05, B7 g2).
- added: 2026-10-05

## P-2008 · Any new client route can move the public script size by 2 KB: Rolldown regroups the shared chunks, so the growth is not a leaked module
- symptom: B7 step 2 added `/admin`, `/admin/sign-in` and `/admin/auth/confirm` and CI's bundle-check failed `_site.property.$slug` at 155,613 and `_site.$market.index` at 154,023 gzip bytes (main: 153,512 and 151,926, budget 153,600). No server module had reached the client: the entry chunk got 1.3 KB smaller and Rolldown moved `src/lib/seo.ts`, `src/config/site.ts` and the router's `route.js`, `useSearch` and `useNavigate` out of it into three new shared chunks that every public route loads. Gzipping them apart cost about 1.9 KB. Three empty public routes (`_site.zz1..3.tsx`) cost 492 bytes the same way, and the admin layout with two empty children cost 689 bytes. A first build without `VITE_API_BASE_URL` bundled the seed and read 166,643 bytes, which measured nothing. Loading `fetchMe` with `await import("../admin/team/team-api")` in the `/admin` `beforeLoad` saved only 212 bytes and added `FAIL a chunk a public route can reach holds src/admin/team/team-api.ts`: a dynamic import of a `src/admin/` module becomes a chunk whose `src` bundle-check refuses.
- cause: with no `codeSplitting` groups, the client build puts modules into chunks by the set of entries that reach them. A route chunk with a new set of imports splits a shared chunk in two, and it does not matter whether the route is public or admin. On main the property route had 88 bytes of headroom, so any route that adds a chunk goes over.
- rule: measure on the build CI makes (`export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; export VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public; export VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA` as separate statements, then `bun run build`). Compare it chunk by chunk against main's own `build-output` artifact (`gh run download <main run id> -n build-output -D <dir>`, then `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs <dir>`). Find which modules moved with `vite build --sourcemap` and the per-source byte counts of each chunk's map. Do not look for a leak first. Measured on B7 c2: a single `$initial` group in the client `build.rolldownOptions.output` (`codeSplitting: { groups: [{ name: "initial", tags: ["$initial"] }] }`) puts every module the entry statically loads into the entry chunk. With it, every public route was smaller than on main (property 151,270, market index 149,623). That is a change to `vite.config.ts`, which the plans of B1b, B3, B3b, B8, B8b and B13 name and B7's does not.
- proof: on slice/b7 at 3c2701a, `cd app && export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; export VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public; export VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA; bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs | grep FAIL` prints the two FAIL lines above; with the group added to `vite.config.ts` the same command prints `bundle-check: OK 21 routes under 153600 gzip bytes`, each of the 21 routes 2,173 to 2,348 bytes under main's artifact (measured 2026-10-06, B7 c2).
- also measured (B7 c2b, H62 applied): the group reaches the Nitro server build too. `.output/server` held 91 files and 3,346,732 bytes with it, 97 files and 3,351,212 bytes without (without it `_libs` also holds zod, hookable, cron-parser+luxon and two h3 chunks; with it they are gone, `h3-v2+rou3` appears and the `_ssr` chunks regroup). The build's `WARN inlineDynamicImports option is ignored because the codeSplitting option is specified` prints with and without the line, so it is not the group's. The worker still boots under `wrangler dev` and `admin-signin.spec.ts` passes on it.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2009 · After a client-side navigation, `waitForURL` and `networkidle` resolve before the new route has rendered: the first `h1` read is the old page's
- symptom: B7 c2b, a headless check clicked a property link on `/properties`, awaited `page.waitForURL("**/property/<slug>")` and `waitForLoadState("networkidle")`, and read `h1: Properties`, which looks like a failed navigation.
- cause: the router updates the URL before its loader data arrives and the new route mounts; `networkidle` after the click can already hold because the listing's requests are done.
- rule: after a client navigation, wait for something only the new page has (`page.waitForFunction(() => document.querySelector("h1")?.textContent !== "<old h1>")` or a locator of the new heading) before reading the page.
- proof: the same script with that wait printed `h1: A townhouse on a quiet block.`, `document requests after the click: 0`, `page errors: 0` (2026-10-06, the group build under `wrangler dev --port 8948`).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2010 · A red build job hides every job behind it: PR 158's e2e job ran for the first time once bundle-check passed, and its admin step fails on `DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF is not set`
- symptom: CI run 37401095820 on 9e5a731: build passed, then job e2e failed in step `admin`, both sign-in cases (`admin-signin.spec.ts:16` and `:34`, with retries) at `Error: e2e session: DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF is not set`; the two cases that need no session passed. The runs on d528532 and 3c2701a never showed it: their e2e job was `skipped` behind the failed build.
- cause: `tests/e2e/helpers/session.ts` builds its client from `https://${DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF}.supabase.co` and `DEV_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, and its header says CI supplies them under the same names; the e2e job of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs its own `supabase start` stack and exports only `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. The laptop proofs passed because the dev profile sets the DEV_ names.
- rule: a job that `needs:` a red job has not run, so a fix to that red job is not finished until every job behind it has run once. An e2e helper reads the same variable names the CI job writes; prove an admin spec in CI, not only under the laptop's dev profile.
- proof: `gh run view 37401095820 --job 112068339794 --log-failed | grep -c "DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF is not set"` → 4; `gh run view 37398925655 --json jobs -q '.jobs[]|.name+" "+.conclusion'` → `e2e skipped`.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2011 · Plan line `retry: (n, e) => n < 2` retries a 5xx twice; the same step's proof says "a 503 is retried once"
- symptom: B7 invariant 20 gives the admin query default as `retry: (n, e) => n < 2 && !(e instanceof AdminApiError && e.status < 500)`, and step 3's proof lists `src/admin/query.test.ts` with "a 403 is not retried, a 503 is retried once". Written as the invariant has it, a failing query runs three times, not twice.
- cause: TanStack Query calls `retry(failureCount, error)` with `failureCount` 0 after the first failure, so `n < 2` allows two retries; the plan author read `n` as the attempt number.
- rule: for "retried once" write `failureCount < 1`. `src/admin/query.ts` does, and `src/admin/query.test.ts` counts the calls (403 once, 503 twice, a lost connection twice). A later slice that wants a different count changes the test with it.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit src/admin/query.test.ts` → `Tests  7 passed (7)`; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b7-g3-query-503` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B7:b7-g3-query-503` (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2012 · The plan's `adminFetch<T>(path, init?)` returns unchecked JSON, which the lint and R33 refuse; the built signature takes the Zod schema
- symptom: B7 step 3 and the plans of B6, B8, B8b, B9, B10 and B11 quote `adminFetch<T>(path, init?)`. A body of `await response.json()` returned as `T` fails `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-return`, and `body as T` fails `no-unsafe-type-assertion` (G-103).
- cause: the sketch typed the answer without saying who checks it.
- rule: call `adminFetch(path, schema, init)` with a Zod schema (`src/admin/ui/admin-fetch.ts`); the answer is parsed with it and a mismatch throws `ZodError`. A lane that follows the plan's old signature gets a type error on the second argument: read `src/admin/ui/README.md`, do not cast.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "export async function adminFetch" -A4 src/admin/ui/admin-fetch.ts` → the `schema: z.ZodType<T, z.ZodTypeDef, unknown>` parameter; `bunx vitest run --project unit src/admin/ui/admin-fetch.test.ts -t "parsed with the schema"` passes (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2013 · A dynamic import of `src/admin` from the admin guard fails bundle-check; the static import costs about 1.1 KB gzip on every public route
- symptom: moving the three imports of `src/routes/admin.tsx`'s `beforeLoad` (admin-fetch, query, team-api) into `await import(...)` saved 0.8 KB on `_site.property.$slug` (152569 to 151813 gzip bytes) and made `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs` print `FAIL a chunk a public route can reach holds src/admin/query.ts` (also `AdminRouteError.tsx`, `AdminPending.tsx`, `team-api.ts`).
- cause (inferred from the manifest, not from Start's source): the guard is route code outside the split component, so its static imports are inlined into the entry chunk and no manifest key names them; as dynamic imports each becomes a chunk with its own `src/admin/...` key, and `bundle-check` walks the entry's dynamic imports and refuses any such key (FORBIDDEN, R39).
- rule: keep the guard's imports static. The admin code the entry carries after step 3 is what `admin.tsx` imports statically (`admin-fetch.ts`, `query.ts`, `team-api.ts` and their imports, not itemised); live build, before and after: `_site` 141873 to 143015, `_site.property.$slug` 151270 to 152569 of 153600. That leaves 1031 bytes on the tightest route: a later admin slice that puts more in the entry (a route file's `head()`, `adminRouteOptions()`, a hotkey table) needs the orchestrator's ruling on the bundle check, not a quiet trim.
- proof: `cd app && export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA && bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs | tail -3` → `ok   _site.property.$slug 152569 gzip bytes` and `bundle-check: OK 21 routes under 153600 gzip bytes` (2026-10-06).
- hit again: 2026-10-06, B7 g4: `src/routes/admin/requests.index.tsx`, the first route to spread `...adminRouteOptions()` as `src/admin/ui/README.md` step 1 says, failed the live build's bundle check with `FAIL a chunk a public route can reach holds src/admin/ui/AdminRouteError.tsx` and the same for `AdminPending.tsx`: the manifest shows the two as `dynamicImports` of the client entry, because a spread is route-tree code the router's splitter cannot see. The route now names `errorComponent: AdminRouteError` itself, which the default split groups (`component`, `errorComponent`, `notFoundComponent` in `@tanstack/router-plugin` constants) move into the route's own chunk, and drops `pendingComponent` (no loader, the table draws its own loading rows): `bundle-check: OK 21 routes`, `_site.property.$slug 153115` of 153600 (485 bytes left). The README line and `adminRouteOptions()` are g3's and still say spread: every later admin route meets the same failure until they change.
- added: 2026-10-06

- hit again: 2026-10-07, B7 g2 (step 5a): the two People screens (`people.index.tsx`, `people.$id.tsx`, each with `head`, `errorComponent` and, on the detail, `notFoundComponent`) put CI's live build over the budget: run 37559848282 printed `FAIL _site.property.$slug loads 153768 gzip bytes, over the budget of 153600`. Measured in the lane with the variables of P-2129: 153771 with the two files, 153462 with them moved out (about 155 bytes per admin screen), main at ec1b4f0 153238 in CI (the other 224 come from g1's work on the branch that main does not have yet, inferred, not measured file by file). The two routes would have to cost 138 bytes instead of 309; no trim was tried, about 20 B7 screens remain, so the group stopped for the orchestrator's ruling on the bundle check as this entry says. Proof: `cd app && MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs | grep property` on slice/b7 at the g2 commit.

## P-2014 · Testing the admin UI in jsdom: no `showModal`, and a route may not take both `id` and `path`
- symptom: `HTMLDialogElement.prototype.showModal` and `close` are undefined in jsdom 30.1.1 (`node -e "const {JSDOM}=require('jsdom');const d=new JSDOM('<dialog></dialog>').window.document.querySelector('dialog');console.log(typeof d.showModal)"` prints `undefined`), and `createRoute({ id: "/admin/people/", path: "/admin/people" })` throws `Route cannot have both an 'id' and a 'path' option.`; the first run of `src/admin/ui/shell.test.tsx` failed 10 cases on it.

- rule: a test of a `Dialog`, `Drawer` or `ConfirmDialog` stands in `showModal` and `close` on the prototype (they only toggle `open`; `dialogs.test.tsx` says so), and a test route is `createRoute({ path: "/admin/people/" })`, whose id comes out as the file route's. `src/admin/ui/test-router.tsx` does it. The proof of the real dialog's modality and focus trap in a browser is UNPROVEN until an e2e spec opens one.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project component src/admin/ui/dialogs.test.tsx src/admin/ui/shell.test.tsx` → 2 files passed (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06
