## P-2016 · The admin sign-in e2e failed on mop-dev with `Could not find the 'display_name' column of 'user_roles' in the schema cache` while the column exists: PostgREST's cache was stale
- symptom: `admin-signin.spec.ts` on the group build, 2 of 4 failed after 2 minutes each: the invite case at `expect(granted.error).toBeNull()` with `PGRST204 ... Could not find the 'display_name' column of 'user_roles' in the schema cache`, and the magic-link case ended on `/admin/sign-in?state=expired` ("That link has expired or was already used"). The same spec had passed 4 of 4 at c2b.
- cause: the column is in `20261001090100_people_audit.sql` and in the database (`select count(*) filter (where column_name='display_name') from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='user_roles'` printed `1`, newest migration `20261005161634`), so PostgREST's schema cache was stale after other lanes' pushes to the one mop-dev. That the magic-link failure has the same cause is inferred: it passed after the reload with no code change.
- rule: before reading an admin e2e failure as a code defect, run `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'` through `bun scripts/psql-dev.mjs -At -c "notify pgrst, 'reload schema'"` (profile dev, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`); it changes no data and is not a migration. The e2e takes about 4 minutes on a failure, so check the `PGRST204` text first.
- proof: after the `NOTIFY`, `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8948 env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-signin.spec.ts` → `4 passed (1.8m)` (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2017 · A watched-fail mutation that turns a bounded retry into an endless loop hangs the replay: `watchfail.mjs` has no time limit per entry
- symptom: replaying `b7-g3-fetch-csrf-loop` (B7 g3) ran 190 s and ended `BAD`: the first mutation changed an `if` that retries a 403 once into a `while`, so the test under it never returned and waited out its own `--testTimeout=60000` on each case. The entry was rewritten to add a second `send` instead of a loop. The log named P-066 for it, but P-066's rule covers `find` and `expect` hygiene only.
- cause: `scripts/watchfail.mjs` starts each entry's `run` with `spawn(...)` and waits for `close`; there is no timeout, so a mutation that stops a function from returning costs the test's full timeout times its cases, and a replay killed midway leaves the mutated file on disk.
- rule: write a mutation of retry, loop or wait code as a change that runs one more time or none, never as one that can run forever (`if` to `while`, a removed break, a removed counter). When one hangs, stop it by its process id, then run `git status --short` and `git checkout` the file the entry names before the next edit. Replay a suspect entry alone, from a background call, with a wait bounded under nine minutes (P-027).
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "timeout" scripts/watchfail.mjs` → `0` (no per-entry limit, 2026-10-06); `grep -n '"id": "b7-g3-fetch-csrf-loop"' -A5 tests/mutations/B7.json | grep -c "await send(path, init);"` → `2` (the `find` line and the `replace` line, which carries the call twice: a second call, not a loop).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-2018 · A watched-fail replay run in the same tree as `bun run check` can make check read a mutated file and answer green or red for the wrong reason
- symptom: in the B7 g3 review, `bun run check` in the review snapshot ran past the Bash tool's 600 s maximum and was moved to the background (P-027 again); watched-fail replays were run in the same tree while it ran. A replay writes the mutated source for the seconds its test runs, so a typecheck, lint or test phase of the check that reads that file in that window reports the mutation, not the code. The check later ended `quiet: ok`, exit 0; whether any phase read a mutated file was not established (UNPROVEN).
- cause: the check and the replays share one working tree, and `watchfail.mjs` mutates files in place (`mutatedNow` in `scripts/watchfail.mjs`).
- rule: start `bun run check` first, alone, as `node workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- bun run check` in the background writing to a file, and replay no watched-fail entry in that tree until it has ended; replay afterwards, or in a second worktree. A check result taken while a replay ran is not evidence.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "mutatedNow" scripts/watchfail.mjs | head -3` → the map of files mutated in place and its `restoreAll`; `git status --short` is empty before a check and after a clean replay (2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B17 g10 review: the brief asked for `bun run check` and for a replay of the group's `b17-obs-*` entries together, and the reviewer ran the replay while check ran in the background. Check went red on `tests/unit/observatory.test.ts` (`- "...fetch failed (ETIMEDOUT)" + "...fetch failed"`, exit 1) while the replay printed `mutated scripts/observatory.mjs:34  ? error.message`; one full check run of about 10 minutes was lost, and the rerun on the untouched tree gave exit 0. A brief or a reviewer flow that asks for both runs them one after the other, check first (`node workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- bun run check`, then the replay), never side by side in one tree.

## P-2126 · `bun run gen:types` with the access token answers, but its output is not CI's layout: it differs from the committed `src/db/types.ts` by 4769 lines
- symptom: B7 g4 review, full `.env` loaded so `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` was present: `bun run gen:types` (no flag) exited 0 and wrote `src/db/types.ts`; `git diff --stat src/db/types.ts` showed 3275 insertions and 1494 deletions against the committed file. P-508 (403 for this account) did not reproduce.
- cause (inferred, not confirmed): P-508's 403 depends on the profile and token in the shell, so the no-flag form can work in one shell and fail in another; its output is laid out differently from the `--local` output that CI's `type drift` step compares against (G-008, P-526).
- rule: never commit a `src/db/types.ts` written by the no-flag form of `gen:types` over CI's; the `--db` form of P-508 formats to CI's layout. When the `db` job fails at `type drift`, run `bun run types:from-ci -- <pr>` and commit what it copies; after a bare `gen:types` run, `git checkout -- src/db/types.ts`.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "types:from-ci" package.json` → `1` (the copy-from-CI script exists); `git diff --stat src/db/types.ts | tail -1` after a bare `bun run gen:types` with the token loaded printed `1 file changed, 3275 insertions(+), 1494 deletions(-)`, as the g4 reviewer measured (2026-10-06; that half is the reviewer's measurement, not re-run here).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1924 · The live bundle has no headroom on slice/b17 after the merge of main: `bundle-check` fails on `property.$slug` before any group-7 edit, and the `Picture` component pushes `$market.index` over
- symptom: B17 g7 step 8, `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs`. On the tree before any g7 edit (the merge of origin/main d4a17ce into slice/b17 at 8deb33b) it printed `FAIL _site.property.$slug loads 155847 gzip bytes, over the budget of 153600` and `ok _site.$market.index 153322`. With `Picture` and its seven callers: `property.$slug` 156305 and `$market.index` 153719 (a new failure, 119 bytes over). CI on slice/b17 at 8f842f7 had printed 153054 and 150673, and main's own CI at d4a17ce 151434 for `$market.index`: each side fits, the sum does not.
- cause: the first-load limit (R60) is 150 KB gzip and the groups of one slice each add a little shared code; a new shared module costs about 400 bytes gzip even when its source is 40 lines, because Rolldown gives a component imported from several chunks a chunk of its own (import and export glue, gzip header). Rewriting `Picture` with rest props and with a compact `srcSet` changed the total by 13 bytes in the wrong direction.
- rule: after `git merge origin/main` on a slice branch run the live build and `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs` once before the first edit, so the base overflow is named as the base's and not as the group's; a group that adds a shared component states its measured cost in its log. Not fixed in g7: the files that would give the bytes back are other groups' (UNPROVEN whether one trim of 2.7 KB exists).
- proof: `cd app && MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs | grep -c "^FAIL"` → `2` at g7 (measured 2026-10-06); CI's log of `bundle-check` for a run shows the per-route numbers (`gh run view <id> --log | grep "gzip bytes"`).
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-06, B17 g8: `bun add web-vitals` (v6.2.3) put 2967 gzip bytes into every route of the live build and turned five `bundle-check` lines red (base: one, `property.$slug`). Importing it with `import("web-vitals")` inside `startWebVitals()` (loaded after hydration; its observers read buffered entries) left the first-load closure at base plus 168 bytes (`property.$slug` 155972 to 156140, `$market.index` 153392 to 153561, 39 bytes of headroom). The base overflow of `property.$slug` is still not repaired, so `bundle-check` exits 1 on this branch for that route alone.
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B17 c8: repaired. Moving the server-only `cspReportBatchSchema` out of `contracts.ts` (-324 bytes) and lazy-loading `InquiryDialog` on the property route (-3 KB) gave `property.$slug` 153102 and `$market.index` 153497 on the live build (P-1932); `bundle-check` exits 0.

- symptom: B17 g7, live build under `MOP_ENV=production` on port 8938, `bun run lhci:local` over `/`, `/properties`, `/california`, `/exposure`, `/submit` (3 runs each) exited 1: performance 0.94 / 0.91 / 0.87 / 0.93 / 0.92; LCP 2.7 to 3.3 s (limit 2.5 s); script transfer 152.7 to 167.8 KB (limit 150 KB); best practices 0.96 on `/` and `/california` (`errors-in-console`: `/media/o/california/0-2bf01698.webp` answers 404); accessibility 0.98 on `/exposure` (`heading-order`); CLS 0 and SEO 1 everywhere. - cause: the simulated mobile profile (1.6 Mbps, 4x CPU) charges every request that finished before the observed FCP (351 ms, because a local server answers everything at once), among them the 145 KB gzip entry script; the bytes of P-1924 are the same bytes. The media rows of the markets name keys the `media` bucket does not hold because B2's seed has not run `--images upload` on mop-dev, and no property is published there.
- rule: treat the performance and budget assertions of `lighthouserc.local.json` as a measurement of the bundle, not of the images; read `.lighthouseci/lhr-*.json` for the audit that fails (`node -e` over `r.categories` and `r.audits`) before changing a page. A plan line that needs a published property or uploaded variants on mop-dev says so in its own proof, because a lane never seeds it (H57).
- proof: `cd app && bunx lhci assert --config=lighthouserc.local.json` after a run prints the failing assertions with their values; `curl -s --compressed http://127.0.0.1:8938/api/public/properties` → `[]` (measured 2026-10-06, B17 g7). Not repaired in g7.
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B17 c8, live build on 8938 after the bundle repair: median of 3 runs perf 0.89 / 0.92 / 0.87 / 0.91 / 0.92, LCP 2.81 to 3.35 s, script transfer 156.3 to 171.3 KB (higher than g7's 152.7 to 167.8 KB: UNPROVEN cause: lazy chunks that load after hydration, g8's `web-vitals` among them, count in `resource-summary:script` and `bundle-check` does not measure them; the request list was not read), best practices 0.96 on `/` and `/california` (the 404 of `/media/o/california/0-...webp`), accessibility 0.98 on `/exposure`; CLS 0 and SEO 1 everywhere. LCP and script size are the two lines H61 holds at `warn` until H1 in `lighthouserc.json`; `lighthouserc.local.json` keeps them at `error` on purpose and was not loosened, so `lhci:local` stays red until H1.

## P-1926 · React 19 writes `srcSet` and `fetchPriority` in camel case in the HTML it serves, so the plan's `grep -o 'srcset="[^"]*"'` finds nothing
- symptom: the `picture` unit cases passed only with `srcSet="..."` and `fetchPriority="high"` in the expected markup; a lower-case `srcset=` expectation was red. The live proof line of B17 step 8 (`curl -s <page> | grep -o 'srcset="[^"]*"'`) is case sensitive and would print nothing on a correct page.
- cause: `renderToString` keeps the React prop names; browsers read attribute names without case, so nothing is wrong for a visitor.
- rule: a proof or a test that looks for a React-rendered attribute reads it without case (`grep -io 'srcset="[^"]*"'`) or asserts the camel-case form.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/essentials.test.ts -t picture` → `7 passed`; with `Picture` reduced to `[variants?.card]` the first case is red (registry entry `b17-g7-pic-srcset`).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1927 · `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` on a slice branch replays the whole slice registry and a taskkill of it leaves the file it was mutating changed
- symptom: B17 g7 ran `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` for the reviewer's step (c): 26 entries ran in the first ten minutes (B17 has 169), and the run blocked every build and test in the tree meanwhile. `taskkill //PID <node> //F` stopped it, and `git status` then showed `src/server/public/routes.ts` modified (the entry `b17-report-limit` was mid-replay); the SIGTERM handler of the tool never runs on a Windows hard kill.
- cause: `--changed <ref>` selects every entry whose file differs from the ref, and on a slice branch that is most of the slice. A kill by process id is `TerminateProcess`, not a signal.
- rule: replay only the entries of the files the group touched, with `--only <id>` one entry per call from a list (`node -e` over `tests/mutations/*.json` filtering `entry.file`), and after any kill run `git status --short` and restore the file named on the last `mutated` line with `git checkout HEAD -- <file>` (only a file the group did not edit; P-068).
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b17-g7-pic-srcset | tail -1` → `watchfail: replayed 1: ok 1, bad 0, stale 0; manual 0 not replayed; 3155 not selected` (about 15 s).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1928 · A lane's `node_modules` keeps a package the lockfile dropped, so `bun run check` passes in the lane and fails on a clean install
- symptom: B17 g5 signed off `bun run check` exit 0 on a head whose `tests/unit/essentials.test.ts` imports `jsdom`; a reviewer's fresh `bun install --frozen-lockfile` of the same commit answered `TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module 'jsdom'` and 36 `no-unsafe-*` lint errors, which is what CI's check job would print.
- cause: `@types/jsdom` (with `@types/tough-cookie`) was installed in the lane during B17 g1 and dropped from `package.json` and `bun.lock` (P-1903), but bun left both folders in `node_modules`, and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` answers `no changes` without removing them. The lane's typecheck read types the lockfile does not carry.
- rule: after removing a dependency, and before signing off a check that a later group's import could lean on, list the packages in `node_modules` that `bun.lock` does not name and delete them (or `rm -rf node_modules && bun install --frozen-lockfile`). jsdom stays untyped here: the feed cases load it with `await vi.importActual<{ JSDOM: XmlDom }>("jsdom")`, which types the one constructor they use without `@types/jsdom`.
- proof: `cd app && ls node_modules/@types/jsdom` → `No such file or directory`, and `bun run typecheck` exits 0; with `import { JSDOM } from "jsdom";` put back in `tests/unit/essentials.test.ts` it prints `error TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module 'jsdom'` (measured 2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1929 · The catalog carries the publish day, not the publish time, so a feed built at midnight UTC shows every item on the evening before in the United States
- symptom: B17 g6's feeds wrote `pubDate: Wed, 02 Sep 2026 00:00:00 GMT` for a row published at `2026-09-02T17:30:00+00:00`; a reader in New York shows Sep 1, 8:00 PM, and two rows of one day cannot be ordered by time. The feed test passed because every fixture was at `T00:00:00`.
- cause: B3's mapper cuts the timestamp to `YYYY-MM-DD` (`isoDate` in `src/server/public/mappers.ts`, used for `publishedAt` of properties and stories); `new Date("2026-09-02")` is midnight UTC. A fixture at midnight cannot tell a lost time of day from a kept one.
- rule: a feed built from the catalog states the publish day at 12:00 GMT (`publishDay` in `src/server/public/feeds.ts`), which is the same calendar day in every zone from UTC-11 to UTC+11; same-day items keep catalog order (properties before stories), which is not newest first. Fixtures for a date use a time of day that is not midnight. Carrying the full timestamp means changing B3's mapper, the `publishedAt` type and the parity tests together.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/essentials.test.ts -t "feed: every pubDate"` passes; registry `b17-g6-feed-noon` (`new Date(day)` for the noon one) turns it red naming New York and the noon instants (measured 2026-10-06).
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-1930 · `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" 2>&1 | tail` loads nothing: a pipe runs `eval` in a subshell, and the warning about a missing name looked like the cause
- symptom: B17 g8, from `app/`: `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" 2>&1 | tail -2` printed `load-env: .env has no OMNIKOM_MOCK_SECRET`, and the next `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run db:psql -- -c "select 1"` answered `DEV_DB_URL is not set`. Two calls went to the missing name, which is only a warning: `node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev >/dev/null; echo $?` prints `0` and still exports the other names.
- cause: `eval ... | tail` runs `eval` in the pipeline's subshell, so the exports die with it. The warning text came from the same pipe and pointed at the wrong thing.
- rule: run the loader as its own statement, never in a pipeline: `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` and then the command, in the same Bash call.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run db:psql -- -c "select count(*) from analytics_events" | tail -3` prints a count (811 on 2026-10-06, measured on this lane's `.env`).
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B6 c3h round 3: the first replay in CI's form (`watchfail.mjs ... --changed origin/main --kinds unit,sql`) ran with `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` inside a pipe, so the replay saw no `DEV_DB_URL` and stopped at `refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set`; 12 minutes went before the cause showed. The hand-in's cost line named P-310, which is about the `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` refusal and not about the pipe; this entry is the one to open.
- added: 2026-10-06
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 g2: `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` was started in a call that never loaded the dev profile; after 25 minutes it ended `replayed 631: ok 546, bad 84, stale 1`, and 83 of the 84 were `sql`/db entries stopping at `refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set`. Load the profile in the same call as the replay, or pass `--kinds file` for a unit-only window.

## P-1931 · A dynamic import of a mocked module can hand the module under test a second copy of the mock, so a "called once" assertion stays green with the guard removed
- symptom: B17 g8's `web-vitals` case called `startWebVitals()` twice and asserted `onLCP` (a `vi.fn()` from `vi.mock("web-vitals", () => library)`) was called once. With the `if (started) return;` guard deleted the registry replay printed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: stayed green`, although a counter inside the module showed the `import("web-vitals")` callback ran twice: the two callbacks held different `onLCP` functions and only one of them was the hoisted mock.
- cause: not found (UNPROVEN why vitest returns a second copy for the second `import()` of one mocked specifier made from a module loaded with `vi.importActual`); three static `import("web-vitals")` calls from the test file itself gave one copy (a scratch test, 2026-10-06).
- rule: a test of "once" never counts calls on a mock that a dynamic import resolves, and a guard whose only proof is such a count is not proven; the group dropped the guard (a layout that mounts twice would report each metric twice; no such mount is known) rather than keep it unproven, and its registry holds only mutations the cases catch.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b17-g8-vitals-inp` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B17:b17-g8-vitals-inp`; the guard variant stayed green in three forms of the case (a `vi.fn`, a hoisted `vi.fn`, a recorder over a shared array) on 2026-10-06.
- added: 2026-10-06

## P-532 · A workflow script (`.claude/workflows/*.js`) can stop parsing while `node --check` and the post-write hook stay green: both parse it as CommonJS, the Workflow tool parses it as an async function body
- symptom: 2026-10-07 01:05, the first lane launch on the second laptop: `Workflow({ scriptPath: ".claude/workflows/build-slice.js", … })` → "Invalid workflow script: Script parse error: Unexpected token (92:137)". Line 92 was the one-database brief line added in becb161 (2026-10-06 10:50) with two unescaped backticks inside the `rulesFor` template literal; every launch from main between those two commits would have failed the same way. `node --check` passed the file, and so did `hooks/postwrite-sanity.mjs`, which calls it.
- cause: a workflow script is not a module. The tool hoists `export const meta` and wraps the rest in an async function (top-level `return` is legal there), so neither `node --check` (CommonJS; a backtick inside a template literal is legal text until the next backtick) nor `import()` (fails on the top-level return) parses it the way the tool does. The text that broke it was a shell command quoted with backticks inside a template literal, written by a node one-liner through the shell, where escaping is easy to lose (P-008).
- rule: a change to a workflow script is proved by parsing it as the tool does: strip `export ` from the meta line and feed the text to `new (Object.getPrototypeOf(async function(){}).constructor)("agent","parallel","pipeline","phase","log","args","budget","workflow", text)`; "ok" or the real error. `~/.claude/hooks/postwrite-sanity.mjs` does exactly that for every file under `.claude/workflows/` on Write and Edit since 2026-10-07, so an edit through the editor tool is caught at once; an edit through a shell one-liner is not, one more reason to edit these files with the editor tool. Inside a template literal every backtick of quoted shell text is escaped with a backslash.
- proof: with main's build-slice.js at 7531328 the parse above throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'eval'`; with the two backticks escaped (PR 179) it prints ok; `node --check` prints nothing for both.
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-08 09:30, orchestrator: the mergeOnly brief (PR 235) carried two raw backticks; `node --check` passed, the post-write hook never ran because the edit came through a `node -e` script in Bash, and the Dell runner found it with the vm wrap at launch. Rule stays: workflow files are edited with the Edit tool so the hook parses them, and the wrap check runs before the push.

## P-1932 · What gave the bundle its bytes back: a server-only schema inside `domain/contracts.ts` and a click-only dialog imported by a route, found by attributing the built chunk to source files
- symptom: B17 c8, merge of main at 7e4b7a9: `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs` printed 156,440 for `_site.property.$slug` and 153,855 for `_site.$market.index` against 153,600. Guessing which module to trim cost the first half hour: the shared small chunks (Picture, cards) are 100 to 600 bytes each and the entry chunk is 144 KB.
- cause: `cspReportBatchSchema` (72 lines of zod calls, server only) lived in `src/domain/contracts.ts`, and a zod schema built at module level is a side effect Rolldown cannot drop, so every browser downloaded it (324 gzip bytes). `_site.property.$slug.tsx` imported `InquiryDialog` statically, so the dialog, `attribution.ts`, `use-field-errors.ts` and the form notices were in the route's first load (together `property.$slug` went from 156116 to 153079 gzip bytes when the dialog became lazy) although nothing shows before a click.
- rule: a schema that only the server reads goes in its own file under `src/domain/` (here `csp-report.ts`), never into `contracts.ts`, which the browser bundle imports whole; a component that appears only after a click is `lazy()` behind `Suspense` and rendered only while open. To find what to move, build with `bunx vite build --sourcemap` (same `VITE_*` values, P-015) and sum the mapped bytes per source file of the entry chunk with `@jridgewell/sourcemap-codec`'s `decode` (a ten-line script outside `app/`, P-087), then take the large files that no public page needs at first paint.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c cspReportBatchSchema src/domain/contracts.ts` → `0`; `cd app && MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs | grep -E "property|market.index|bundle-check"` → `ok _site.$market.index 153497`, `ok _site.property.$slug 153102`, `bundle-check: OK 24 routes under 153600 gzip bytes` (measured 2026-10-07). `$market.index` has 103 bytes of headroom: the next shared component added to a public page needs its own lazy boundary.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1933 · A redirect `> ../../x.txt` from `app/` of a lane lands outside the worktree, and the sandbox then refuses to delete it
- symptom: B17 g10, two scratch outputs written with `> ../../wf1.txt` and `> ../../../scratch-list.txt` from `E:/mop-build/site/app` landed in `E:/mop-build/` and `E:/`; the later `rm` of the first was refused with "Dangerous rm operation detected: 'E:\wf1.txt'", so two stray files stay outside the tree for the operator to remove.
- cause: the lane is `E:/mop-build/site`, one folder deeper than the repository root `E:/Matter Of Place` that the habit "two levels up is the root" was learned in; `../..` from `app/` is `mop-build`, not a scratch place.
- rule: write scratch output only to the session scratchpad directory or through `node workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs --`, never to a relative `../..` path; count the levels with `pwd` first when a relative path is unavoidable.
- proof: `cd E:/mop-build/site/app && realpath ../..` → `/e/mop-build`; `ls /e/mop-build/wf1.txt /e/scratch-list.txt` lists the two strays (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1934 · `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` on a slice branch replays every entry of every file the slice touched, not the group's, and `--kinds file` selects nothing
- symptom: B17 g10, the reviewer's pass (c) `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main --kinds file` printed `replayed 0: ... 3119 not selected`; without `--kinds` it replayed the whole slice's entries (101 `WATCHED-FAIL OK` after about ten minutes, still running) and left `app/scripts/alt-audit.mjs` mutated when I stopped it.
- cause: `--changed <ref>` diffs `<ref>...HEAD`, which on a slice branch is every group's files; `kindOf` gives "file" only for entries with a `find`, and the flag documented as `unit,sql` does not match them.
- rule: replay a group's own entries with `--only <id>` per id (a loop over the ids of the group's files); never stop a replay by killing it without `git status` afterwards, and restore a mutated committed file with `git checkout -- <file>`.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b17-obs-host` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B17:b17-obs-host`; `git diff --name-only --relative origin/main...HEAD | wc -l` on slice/b17 → well over 100 files (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-533 · After a Claude Code session restart, a workflow run cannot be resumed from the new session until its journal is copied over: resume reads only the current session's folder
- symptom: 2026-10-07 02:38 on the Dell, the first resume after the session restart that loaded `unit-reviewer`: "The journal for workflow run wf_b52b8501-a01 is not on disk, and this session cannot fetch a remote copy". The run's `workflows/<id>.json` and `subagents/workflows/<id>/` sat under the old session's folder (`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<old session id>/`), and `resumeFromRunId` looks only under the new one.
- cause: workflow journals are stored per session; a restart (needed whenever `.claude/agents/` changes, because the agent registry loads at session start) gives a new session id and an empty folder.
- rule: before the first resume in a restarted session, copy without moving (`cp -n`) `workflows/<id>.json` and `subagents/workflows/<id>/` for every run to resume from the old session's folder into the new one; then resume; the cached builds replay and the new agents run. The lane runner reports the copy, it is not a fix of a script (operator rule, lane-runner.md).
- proof: on the Dell, after `cp -n` of the five ids into `33ddf8d3-…/`, all five resumes took and `review:B11:g1:1-2` started at 02:40:42; before the copy the same call printed the "not on disk" refusal.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1935 · A hit-again line was inserted by line position into an entry whose earlier line had been split by a backslash-n, so the new line sat inside the old one
- symptom: B17 c8, `git diff ea5c056 d3f9e6f -- GOTCHAS.md` (hunk `@@ -196,6 +196,7 @@`) showed the new P-008 hit-again line of c8 between the opening of the 2026-10-03 B3 g1 hit-again line (which ended in an open backtick) and its continuation (which began with a backtick and ` became a real newline`), so the B3 g1 line read as two and the c8 line seemed to end in the B3 sentence. The code reviewer found it; the author had not read the neighbouring lines back.
- cause: the B3 g1 line was itself damaged by P-008 (its `\n` became a real line break when it was written through `node -e`), so the entry held a line that began with a backtick; the c8 author appended "after the last hit-again" by looking at the line above the continuation, and nothing in `check-gotchas.mjs` flags a line of an entry that does not begin with `- `.
- rule: after any edit of a bank entry, read the changed lines back (`git diff -U2 GOTCHAS.md`) and run the proof below; a line of an entry that does not start with `- ` is a break, repair it at once (join it to the line above) before adding anything beside it.
- proof: `grep -c '^` became' GOTCHAS.md` → `0` (it printed 1 on d3f9e6f); `git show d3f9e6f:GOTCHAS.md | grep -c '^` became'` → `1`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1936 · A preview page waits for `/media` images that are missing from an empty bucket, Storage answers them slowly under parallel load, and the load event times out
- symptom: the first deploy.yml `essentials` step went red on run 37550497051 (3 cases flaky, each `page.goto: net::ERR_ABORTED` on `/` with `networkidle`; `failOnFlakyTests` turns a pass on retry into a failed run). The review suspected the service worker. The same spec run from this laptop against https://pr-142.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/ failed the same way, and `getDynamicRoutes` of `tests/e2e/fixtures/routes.ts` (a plain fetch with a 15 s timeout, no retry) failed the whole run in 2 of 3 attempts.
- cause: not the service worker. Traces of the failed cases show `/media/o/<property>/0-<hash>.webp` requests that never finish (the objects are missing from Storage, so they are 404 at best), and plain `curl` shows the Worker itself sending no first byte for 6 s or more on routes that read data: stalls out of 20 requests were `/` 8, `/api/public/properties` 8, `/stories` 3, and `/robots.txt`, `/sw.js` and a built asset 0. The same loop against the dev Worker (main's deploy) gave 0 of 30 and against pr-163 and pr-185 0 of 25 each, so it belongs to the b17 build or its preview, not to this laptop's network or to Cloudflare in general. ROOT CAUSE FOUND (g10 rework 3, 2026-10-07 05:00 +0300, `wrangler tail pr-142` with the dev profile's token works from this tree): the stall is in the `/media/*` route, not in the HTML. The `media` bucket of mop-dev is empty, so every image of the live catalog (31 `/media/o/...` addresses on the home page of pr-142 and of pr-163) is a missing-object lookup that Supabase Storage answers with 400/404, normally in 0.5 to 1.3 s. Under 12 requests in parallel the same direct lookup took up to 7.6 s, and through the Worker four of them waited 16.2 s together (tail: `wallTime` 16238, `cpuTime` 1, `outcome` ok, status 404), while `/` itself had a median `wallTime` of 5 ms and a maximum of 230 ms over 69 requests. A page loaded with JavaScript off (`consent-noscript`) has no script to defer images, so its `load` event waits for them and passes 30 s. workers.dev has no edge cache (cache.ts), so no 404 is kept. Why `/` showed 8 of 20 stalls at 03:30 is not explained (UNPROVEN: the same loop now gives 0), and why pr-163 and the dev Worker showed 0 is not either: their HTML was measured, not their images.
- rule: an e2e run against a deployed preview is only as steady as the preview. Before blaming a spec or a browser feature, run `curl --max-time 6` twenty times against the page and count `000`. deploy.yml runs the essentials step plain, with `CI` set, so `failOnFlakyTests` fails a case that passes only on its retry (B4 invariant 6); a first version that emptied `CI` and gave `--retries=2` hid the stall and was rejected. The step is not the place to absorb it. The fix is outside g10's files: put the seed images in the `media` bucket (`bun run seed -- --target dev --mode full --images upload`, run from main, since a lane never seeds mop-dev, H57; UNPROVEN that existing objects answer faster than missing ones), or let the preview Worker remember a missing key for the isolate's life. Until one of them is on main, a run of the essentials step can fail on a load that waits for these images, and that is a failure of the preview's data, not of the spec.
- proof: `n=0; for i in $(seq 1 20); do c=$(curl -s -o /dev/null --max-time 6 -w "%{http_code}" https://pr-142.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/); [ "$c" = 000 ] && n=$((n+1)); done; echo $n` → `8` on 2026-10-07 around 03:30 +0300, then `0` of 20 on `/` and `0` of 20 on `/stories` after the preview was redeployed (a reviewer saw 1 of 60 on `/stories`); the stall is now rare and its root cause is still not found. The CI run 37554969153 of 9bdc694 passed the essentials step with 0 flaky; the same loop on pr-163 prints `0`. The cause: `eval "$(node app/scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; curl -s -X POST "$SUPABASE_URL/storage/v1/object/list/media" -H "authorization: Bearer $SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY" -H "apikey: $SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY" -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{"prefix":"","limit":20}'` → `[]`; and `for i in $(seq 12); do (curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_starttransfer}\n" https://pr-142.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/media/o/la-courtyard/0-bed58333.webp &) ; done` repeated for a minute printed times from 0.5 s to 16.7 s, all status 404 (2026-10-07 05:01 +0300).
- hit-again (2026-10-07 07:15, orchestrator): the stall reached an unrelated records pull request (206): the phone web-vitals case timed out at `page.goto` 30 s on both attempts in the runner. From this laptop against the same preview, twelve parallel `/media/<missing key>` requests answered in 0.6 to 1.3 s and the whole phone essentials spec passed 25 of 25 in 1.3 min, so the empty-bucket cause above is not what the runner sees; the cause is UNPROVEN and the step is advisory under ruling H67 until it is found. Next measurement: a Playwright trace from inside the runner (upload the trace of a failed case as an artifact).
- hit-again (2026-10-08 05:00 +0300, B7 g2): PR 213's preview job at b960dcd (run 37714114735) ended `cancelled` at the job's `timeout-minutes: 20`, inside the Lighthouse step, which H67 does not make advisory: Lighthouse's third run of `/` took 9 min 47 s (01:50:43 to 02:00:30 UTC). Essentials (6 failed, 9 flaky, 35 passed, all `page.goto` aborted or timed out) and overflow (`TimeoutError`, then `No tests found`) were red but advisory. Run 37712652492 of e85bdcc, whose `app/` and `.github/` equal b960dcd's (`git diff --stat e85bdcc b960dcd` lists only logs and the bank), passed every preview step with Lighthouse in 3 min 49 s. So the stall can now cancel the preview job through Lighthouse, not only redden an advisory step. Before reading a cancelled preview as a code fault, list the step times (`gh run view <run> --json jobs`) and compare with the last run of the same `app/` tree (P-1937).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1937 · A preview proof marked UNPROVEN was already settled by a CI run of a descendant commit
- symptom: the g10 builder and its reviewer both treated "the preview job log shows essentials passing" as unprovable ("no CI run exists for this commit"); `gh run view 37550497051 --log-failed` of PR 142 had already run the same code and failed.
- cause: a pull request builds a merge commit on every push, and a later commit that touches only docs and the bank leaves the code of `app/` and `.github/` as it was, so its run proves the earlier snapshot.
- rule: before writing UNPROVEN for a thing CI proves, list the runs of the branch (`gh run list --workflow deploy.yml --branch <slice> --limit 8`) and read the newest one whose commit descends from the snapshot (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <snapshot> <head>`) with only docs changed (`git diff --stat <snapshot> <head>`).
- proof: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 6f78f05 789aa6c && echo descends` → `descends`; `gh run list --workflow deploy.yml --branch slice/b17 --limit 3 --json conclusion,databaseId` lists run 37550497051 with `failure`.
- hit again (g10 rework 3): the review of 4f428e5 wrote "no CI run exists for this commit" and the builder listed it UNPROVEN, while deploy run 37557550150 had started 10 s after the commit and was red within 4 minutes (`gh run list --workflow deploy.yml --branch slice/b17`). Before writing UNPROVEN or "no CI run" about a pushed commit, wait for its own run and read it.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-534 · The board counts only this laptop's workflow journals: a lane run on another machine is invisible to it until its journal is mirrored here
- symptom: 2026-10-07 03:20, two groups accepted on the Dell (B11 g1, B10 g1) and the board still read 145 of 259 with "5 in work"; `board.mjs readRuns` walks `~/.claude/projects/<project>/*/subagents/workflows/*/journal.jsonl` on the machine that serves the board, nothing else.
- cause: the journals are per session and per machine; nothing carries a remote lane's journal to the board's machine.
- rule: on the orchestrator's machine a loop copies every run folder's `journal.jsonl` from the lane machine with `scp -p` (the mtime is what the board uses for "running now" against stale) into `~/.claude/projects/E--Matter-Of-Place/dell-mirror/subagents/workflows/<run>/` every five minutes (script `dell-journal-mirror.sh` in the orchestrator's scratchpad; the lane machine's session folder is in lane-runner.md). A board figure taken while a remote lane runs is a floor, not the count, until the mirror has run.
- proof: after the first mirror, `node workspace/05-plans/board.mjs --check` printed `overall: 148 of 259 steps accepted (57.1%), 6 of them not yet re-run by the orchestrator, 16 in review`; before it, 145 and 5 in review from the same ledger.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2300 · The Dell has no native PostgreSQL: P-718's throwaway cluster starts from the EDB binaries zip, and initdb needs the whole `share` folder
- symptom: B6 g1 needed a database holding its two unmerged migrations (the `void` enum value cannot be used in the transaction that adds it, so the P-312 prelude on mop-dev cannot run any void case, and `committed()` never sees a prelude). On the second laptop `command -v initdb pg_ctl psql pg_dump` printed nothing, `/c/Program Files/PostgreSQL` does not exist and `scripts/psql-dev.mjs` failed with `spawnSync psql ENOENT`. The first `initdb` from a partial unzip (`unzip pg18.zip "pgsql/share/*"`) failed with `could not open directory ".../pgsql/share/timezonesets"`.
- cause: ASSUMED E7's native PostgreSQL 18 is a fact of the first laptop; the Dell setup (lane-runner.md) lists psql only, and it was not installed. unzip's `share/*` pattern did not take the nested folders.
- rule: on a machine without `initdb`, download `https://get.enterprisedb.com/postgresql/postgresql-18.0-1-windows-x64-binaries.zip` (334 MB) into the session scratchpad, unzip it whole except `pgsql/pgAdmin 4/*` and `pgsql/doc/*`, then follow P-718 with that `bin` folder (port 55462 for lane b6). Dump with `pg_dump --schema-only --no-owner -n public -n app` (keep the privileges: the RLS tests read them) plus `--data-only` of settings, retention_policies, pii_columns, action_roles, automation_recipes, email_templates, schedule_settings, channel_settings and migration_checksums; create the roles inside a `do` block that checks `pg_roles`, since a second database errors on them. Keep a `mop_base` copy (`create database mop_base template mop`) before applying the lane's migrations: `gen types` from it equals main's `src/db/types.ts` byte for byte, which proves the pipeline before it writes the lane's file. `storage.buckets` does not exist there, so a bucket case runs on mop-dev.
- proof: `gen types` (P-718's command, then prettier as `scripts/gen-types.mjs` does) from `postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55462/mop_base?sslmode=disable` gives a file whose diff against main's `src/db/types.ts` (CR removed) has 0 lines; `DEV_DB_URL=postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55462/mop env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/payments.db.test.ts` passes every case but the bucket case (measured 2026-10-07, B6 g1).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2301 · A node patch passed its replacement as a string to `String.prototype.replace`, which turned a doubled dollar sign into one
- symptom: B6 g1's `createInvoice` was written by a `node -e` patch whose replacement text held the SQL placeholder template (a dollar sign, then the `${String(index + 1)}` interpolation, inside backticks); the file got the interpolation without its dollar sign, so the insert listed the numbers 1, 2, 3 as values and `tests/db/factories.db.test.ts` failed at the value list. The other replacements of the same patch were fine.
- cause: in a replacement string two dollar signs mean one (and `$&`, `$1` are patterns), so any SQL placeholder or template literal with a dollar sign is rewritten.
- rule: a patch script replaces with a function (`text.replace(find, () => replace)`) or with `split(find).join(replace)`, never with a replacement string; SQL or template text with a dollar sign goes in through the Edit or Write tool.
- proof: `node -e 'console.log("a".replace("a", "$$1"), "a".replace("a", () => "$$1"))'` → `$1 $$1` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2302 · Events written by one transaction share `at` (`now()`), so ordering them by `(at, id)` is random
- symptom: B6 g1's "mark paid, waive and void" case listed `invoice.issued` and `payment.marked` in the opposite order: the helper first said `order by occurred_at, id` (`column "occurred_at" does not exist`: the column is `at`), then `order by at, id`, which compares random uuids.
- cause: `emit_event` stores `now()`, the transaction's start time, and every case of a db test runs in one rolled-back transaction, so all its events tie on `at`.
- rule: a db test that lists several events of one transaction orders them by a field it controls (`type`) or compares them as a set; never by `at` and `id`.
- proof: from `app/` with a database holding the B6 migrations, `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/payments.db.test.ts -t "mark paid, waive and void"` passes with `order by type`; with `order by at, id` it failed with the two payloads swapped (measured 2026-10-07, B6 g1).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2303 · A registry replay on the native PostgreSQL 18 cluster: one entry goes BAD on PG18's foreign key wording, and `B2:o-commit` leaves a committed fixture row
- symptom: B6 g1's reviewer pass ran `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` with `DEV_DB_URL` on the P-2300 cluster: `replayed 140: ok 136, bad 2, stale 2`. `B4:fd-contact-kept` was BAD because the red run said `violates RESTRICT setting of foreign key constraint "submissions_contact_id_fkey"` where the entry expects `violates foreign key constraint`; `B2:g11-rls-own-row` was BAD because it seeds through an API (P-1203). Afterwards `tests/db/factories.db.test.ts` went red at `leaves no fixture row behind once it returns` (`expected { count: 1 }`): the replay of `B2:o-commit` (rollback turned into commit) had committed the `fixture+801` submission.
- cause: PostgreSQL 18 names the RESTRICT action in that message, Supabase's PostgreSQL 17 does not; and a mutation that turns the harness's rollback into a commit leaves its rows in whatever database it ran on.
- rule: read a BAD replay on the native cluster against the message before calling it a defect (the CI `db` job is the judge for wording); after a registry replay on a throwaway database, recreate it (`drop database mop_g1v; create database mop_g1v template mop_base`, then the lane's migrations) before quoting any db proof from it.
- proof: `"$PSQL" postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55462/mop_g1v -Atc "select submitter_email from public.submissions"` printed `fixture+801@fixtures.invalid` after the replay; after recreating the database `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/factories.db.test.ts` → `Tests  11 passed (11)` (measured 2026-10-07, B6 g1).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2304 · A storage-bucket watched-fail on the native cluster prints OK for the wrong reason: `storage.buckets` does not exist there
- symptom: B6 g1's registry entry `b6-g1-documents-private` (`update storage.buckets set public = true where id = 'documents'`) printed `WATCHED-FAIL OK` on the P-2300 cluster, and the author counted it as red for the expected reason. The plain run of the case on that cluster fails with `relation "storage.buckets" does not exist`, with or without the mutation.
- cause: the entry's `expect` pattern matches only the failing test title (`× .*keeps the PDFs in B2's private bucket documents`), not the message, and the native stand-in has no `storage` schema, so the case is red before the mutation changes anything.
- rule: a watched-fail of a case that reads `storage.*` is judged on mop-dev inside a rolled-back transaction or in the CI `db` job, never on the native stand-in; on the stand-in read the red message before calling the replay OK. A new entry's `expect` for such a case names the assertion text, not only the title.
- proof: `"$PSQL" postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:55462/mop_g1v -Atc "select to_regclass('storage.buckets')"` prints an empty line on the stand-in; on mop-dev from `app/`: `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b6-g1-documents-private` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK`, and the bucket still reads `documents|f` afterwards (replayed by the B6 g1 reviewer, 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1938 · bank-merge refuses a merge when main still holds a hit-again line that a lane repaired, because the line is split over two physical lines on main
- symptom: `git merge origin/main` on slice/b17 left GOTCHAS.md conflicted; the by-entry driver printed "ours kept, compare by hand" and left 11 of main's lines out, and `node workspace/05-plans/bank-merge.mjs` printed `bank-merge: refused, nothing written` and `line lost: main P-008: ` became a real newline inside a string literal)...`.
- cause: main's P-008 had a hit-again line broken in two by a real newline (the very lesson of that entry); the lane had repaired it to one line with `\n`. The carry-through of hit-again lines brings main's first physical line (it starts with "- hit again") but not its continuation line, so the tool's own check finds the continuation lost.
- rule: when the tool refuses on a line that starts with a backtick, repair that line in the base and theirs stages (one pass, exactly one occurrence, written with Write) and run the tool in its fixture mode (`--base --ours --theirs --out`), then copy the output over GOTCHAS.md, run `node workspace/05-plans/check-gotchas.mjs` and `git add` it; never edit the bank by hand. The tool should join a continuation line to its hit-again line: a task for the orchestrator.
- proof: `node workspace/05-plans/bank-merge.mjs` during the conflicted merge of 30c9354 with origin/main (2026-10-07 05:30 +0300) → `bank-merge: refused, nothing written`; the same tool in fixture mode on the repaired stages → `bank-merge: 540 entries, 2 resolved both-sides, 0 lost`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## G-1100 · Resend contacts are global and `POST /contacts` on a known address subscribes it again
- paths: app/src/server/channels/resend.ts, app/docs/runbooks/newsletter.md
- severity: warn
- symptom: B11 step 2 read the plan's Audiences calls (`POST /audiences/{id}/contacts`, `PATCH /audiences/{id}/contacts/{id}`, `DELETE /audiences/{id}/contacts/{id}`) and the account answered a different model. On 2026-10-07 a probe on `mop-dev` created a contact with `unsubscribed: true`, posted the same address again to `POST /contacts` (once with `unsubscribed: false`, once with the field left out) and read `unsubscribed: false` afterwards: a person who had unsubscribed was subscribed again by an add.
- cause: since November 2025 Resend has global contacts and calls Audiences Segments; the Audiences API is deprecated but still answers. A contact id is global, `unsubscribed` is a flag of the contact, removing it from a segment leaves it in the account, and a create on a known address answers 201 with the same id and resets the flag. The webhook's `contact.updated` still lists `audience_id` next to `segment_ids`, so B5's `apply_email_event` filter on `audience_id` may drop real unsubscribes (UNPROVEN until step 8).
- rule: never call `POST /contacts` for an address the account may already hold: `addContact` looks it up with `GET /contacts/{email}` first and only adds an existing contact to the segment (`POST /contacts/{id}/segments/{segment}` leaves the flag alone); only `updateContact` clears `unsubscribed`. Contact calls go through the Segments and Contacts endpoints, never `/audiences`. Broadcasts leave from `notes.matterofplace.com`, so tracking is set on that domain, not on `matterofplace.com`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/newsletter/send.test.ts -t "does not resubscribe"` passes; with `if (existing !== null) {` changed to `if (existing === null) {` in `src/server/channels/resend.ts` it fails (registry entry `b11-resend-readd-unsubscribed-contact`).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2400 · `bun run db:psql` fails on this laptop: there is no `psql` on the PATH
- symptom: B11 g1's first proof, `bun run db:psql -- -c "select count(*) from subscribers where confirmed_at is not null;"`, printed `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"`; a `find / -name psql.exe` search then ran past the 120 s limit and was moved to the background.
- cause: ASSUMED E11 measured `psql` on the operator's laptop; this machine (user `ka`, `D:\mop-build`) has the Supabase CLI neither, and no PostgreSQL client. The `pg` package is in `app/node_modules`.
- rule: do not search the disk for `psql`. A read-only proof of a database fact runs through `pg` under bun with the dev profile loaded (`eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"`, then `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun -e 'import pg from "pg"; const c = new pg.Client({ connectionString: process.env.DEV_DB_URL }); ...'`), and the log says the proof ran through `pg`, not `db:psql`.
- proof: `cd app && command -v psql || echo none` → `none` on this laptop; the `pg` query `select count(*)::int as n from subscribers where confirmed_at is not null` printed `[{"n":0}]` against mop-dev on 2026-10-07.
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B10 g10: the proof `bun run db:psql` stopped at `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"`; the same `pg` query through a node script printed the audit and `social_posts` rows, and the log says so. `bunx supabase secrets set` does work here (the CLI comes through bunx, not the PATH), with the `.env` loaded by the set -a line.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 g2: `bun run db:psql` printed `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"`; the read-only checks (tables, draft, roles) went through `bun -e` with `pg` and the dev profile, and the write path was proved inside a transaction that ends in `rollback`.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 g2 (second laptop, user `ka`, tree D:/mop-build/b11): `bun run db:psql` printed `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"` again; no PostgreSQL folder exists under Program Files either. The migration was proved in a rolled-back transaction through a node script that loads `pg` from `app/` (`.tmp/` is ignored) with the dev profile.
- hit again: 2026-10-09, B7 g3 (step 13): `bun run db:psql` printed `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"` again (tree D:/mop-build/admin); the mop-dev facts (`action_roles` rows for `markets.*`, the markets' `coming_soon`, the newest applied migration) were read through a `node -e` script with `pg` and the dev profile.

## P-2401 · A step that calls a SQL function a later step's migration adds cannot be typed: `db.rpc("newsletter_set_audience")` is not in the generated types
- symptom: B11 step 2 writes `ensureAudience`, which stores the segment id through `newsletter_set_audience`, a function of step 4's migration. A structural stand-in (`const store: { rpc(name: "newsletter_set_audience", ...) } = db`) failed `tsc` with `Types of parameters 'fn' and 'name' are incompatible`; the test's `fakeDb({ rpc: { newsletter_set_audience } })` is typed the same way.
- cause: `Db` is `SupabaseClient<Database>`, whose `rpc` accepts only the names of `src/db/types.ts`, and the types come from CI after the migration is merged (P-312, H57), never from this lane.
- rule: stand in with one cast under `// STUB(B11 step 4): ...` and an `eslint-disable-next-line ... -- <reason>` (R03, R05), and build the test's fake with `Object.assign(fakeDb({ tables }), { rpc })`. The group that lands the migration replaces the cast with the typed call and deletes the interface. Better, when a plan orders a caller before the function it calls, say so in the log.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "STUB(B11 step 4)" src/server/channels/resend.ts` → one line, and `bun run stubs` passes.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2402 · A resolver change that B5's own test pins fails B5's suite: `variables.test.ts` held the old `digest.due` headline
- symptom: B11 step 3's plan line says "B5's suite still passes after the two B5 file changes", but `tests/unit/email/variables.test.ts` has a row for `digest.due` with the headline "Place Notes draft ready" and no job, and the resolver now reads the sibling `queue_digest` job of the event, so that row failed once the resolver changed. `fakeDb` also answers whole tables whatever the filter (`is`, `gt`, `eq` do nothing), so a test of a query's filters (published only, taken down, since the last send) cannot use it.
- cause: the plan names two B5 source files and not the B5 test row that pins the behaviour the step replaces; `tests/fixtures/fake-db.ts` leaves filters to the database by design.
- rule: when a step changes what a B5 resolver answers, grep `tests/unit/email` for the event name first and move the row to the new test (here `tests/unit/newsletter/digest-notify.test.ts`). A test of a query's filters builds its db with `filteredFrom` (`tests/fixtures/email-send.ts`, now with `eq`, `in`, `is`, `gt`, `limit`) through `tests/fixtures/newsletter-world.ts`, and a filter without a mutation that turns its test red is not proved.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "digest.due" tests/unit/email/variables.test.ts` → `0`; `bunx vitest run tests/unit/newsletter/digest-notify.test.ts tests/unit/email` → all passed (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2403 · B11 step 4's `standalone` row update needs B9 step 5's render work, which was never built: the row would carry an empty body that B5's code refuses
- symptom: B11 step 4 asks the newsletter migration to set the `standalone` row of `email_templates` to `body = '[]'`, variables `{subject,preheader,block}` and `enabled = true`, and `src/domain/email.ts` to give `standalone` a sample `block` object. On main, `src/templates/email/standalone.tsx` is still B5's placeholder paragraph, there is no `src/templates/social/NewsletterBlock.tsx`, `renderTemplate` parses the body with `z.array(emailBlockSchema).min(1)` and takes `Record<string, string>` variables, and `emailTemplateSchema` (which `tests/db/email.db.test.ts` parses every row with) also says `min(1)`. So the row update makes every render of `standalone` throw, fails B5's seed test, and `render.test.ts` compares B5's seed row of `standalone` with the definition key by key.
- cause: B9 marked steps 1 to 9 accepted while its log (lines 84 and 85 of `workspace/05-plans/logs/B9.md`) records the standalone block, `NewsletterBlock.tsx` and the `render.ts` object-variable change as not built (blocked on B5 at the time). B11's plan line was written against B9's plan, not against main.
- rule: before a step writes a row, a seed or a sample that another slice's code renders, open that code on main and check that the shape it needs is accepted there (`grep -n "min(1)" src/server/email/render.ts src/domain/email.ts`). B11 g3 left the `standalone` row and its `variablesByKey` entry as B5 seeded them (`enabled = false`, so B5's `send_email` returns `template_disabled` for it) and reported the item BLOCKED on B9 step 5's render work.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "NewsletterBlock" src/templates/email/standalone.tsx; grep -n "const body = z.array(emailBlockSchema).min(1)" src/server/email/render.ts` → `0` and line 21 (measured 2026-10-07 on slice/b11 at origin/main adb13e7).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2404 · A new `public` table goes red in four shared db tests until each names it, and only one of them says so before a full run
- symptom: B11 g3's `newsletter_issues` needed a `schemaManifest` entry (`schema.db.test.ts`), an `rlsMatrix` row (`rls-matrix.ts`), and then a fixture row in the `FIXTURES` block of `tests/db/rls.db.test.ts`: with only the matrix row, all seven role probes failed with `newsletter_issues select: refused` (the probe selects a row the fixtures wrote, and an empty table reads as refused). A new template key also needs its class in `tests/db/email.db.test.ts`'s `classes` map when it is not `transactional`.
- cause: the RLS probe works on one fixture row per table, written as `postgres` in the test's transaction; the matrix alone gives it nothing to read.
- rule: a migration that creates a `public` table adds, in the same commit, its columns to `tests/db/schema-manifest.ts`, its row to `tests/db/rls-matrix.ts` and one insert to `FIXTURES` in `tests/db/rls.db.test.ts`; run `schema`, `rls` and `function-source` with the migration as prelude (P-312) before the first push.
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile and the two B11 migrations exported as `MOP_MUTATION_SQL`, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/rls.db.test.ts` → `Tests  7 failed | 7 passed (14)` without the `FIXTURES` insert and `Tests  14 passed (14)` with it (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-537 · A change to a file that registry entries anchor on must replay every entry of that file before the push, not only the new ones; two CI cycles were lost to stale anchors in one hour
- symptom: 2026-10-07, PR 190 (hygiene cap: four B1b entries BAD or STALE), PR 196 (budget: `b3-bc-budget`, `b3-bc-exit` named the old fixture size), PR 215 (`reach()` signature: `b3-bc-nesting`, `b3-bc-lazy` STALE). Each time the author replayed only the entries it had just written, pushed, and CI's db job found the rest; each cost a CI cycle of 10 to 20 minutes and a second push.
- cause: `watchfail --only <id>` takes one id, so the habit is to replay what one remembers; the entries that anchor on the same source line are not in view.
- rule: before any push that touches a source or test file, run `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` from `app/` (it selects every entry whose test file or target changed against main) and push only on `bad 0, stale 0`; when that run is too long for the Bash limit, run it with `run_in_background` and wait. An entry's `find` names the smallest stable text, never a whole line that a signature or a format change rewrites.
- proof: PR 215's db job printed `replayed 144: ok 142, bad 0, stale 2` for the two entries the author had not replayed; `--changed origin/main` run on the branch afterwards selected both.
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-08 14:20, orchestrator, PR 244: the lint script gained an env prefix and the push ran `bun run lint` alone; CI's mutation replay found two stale anchors on package.json (`hy-lint-warnings`, `hy-lint-warnings-app`) and the hygiene pin on the script text failed. The rule is every push, including one-line script changes.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B6 c3h round 3: after `git merge origin/main` brought B7's `copySubmissionMedia` into the system job list, `b6-g5-job-registered` (find `  invoicePdf,\n];`) was STALE and only the 12-minute `--changed origin/main` replay showed it; the find is now `  invoicePdf,\n`, one line, so a neighbour appended after it cannot break it. A find that spans the end of a list is stale the day another slice appends to that list.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B10 g9 round 3: three entries of `app/tests/mutations/B10.json` (`b10g9-rs-db-error-throws`, `-usage`, `-vault`) were STALE after the fix round rewrote `isPlatformError`, because their `find` was the old line and only the one-id replays of the 31 entries on `reconcile-social.ts` and `reconcile.ts` showed it. The cost was listed under P-2454, which holds the defect, not the replay rule; this entry is the one to open. Proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b10g9-rs-db-error-throws` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK`.
- hit again: 2026-10-09, B7 g4: step 14 took the ten `team.*` lines out of `routesPending` in `tests/unit/admin-routes-parity.test.ts`, and the CI `db` job's mutation replay on PR 250 (run 37868492649) ended `replayed 212: ok 211, bad 0, stale 1` on `STALE B7:b7-g1-routes-pending-literal: find occurs 0 times` (its `find` was the `"team.users_list"` line). The entry now anchors on the `"settings.get"` line; both entries on that file (`b7-g1-routes-pending-literal`, `b11-g6-routes-pending-stale`) replayed `WATCHED-FAIL OK` with `--only`. A step that removes `routesPending` lines replays every entry whose `file` is the parity test before the push.

## P-538 · The root checkout is read by the board and shared with background gate chains: a `git checkout` there while another command runs puts edits on the wrong tree
- symptom: 2026-10-07 09:05, a background chain's `git checkout --detach origin/main` ran while the orchestrator was re-anchoring registry entries on `chore/bundle-check-entry-lazy` in the same checkout; the edit landed on a detached main tree, the replay reported one entry STALE against the wrong file, and the work was redone in a worktree.
- cause: one working tree, two writers; `git checkout` is global to the tree.
- rule: the root checkout `E:/Matter Of Place` stays detached on `origin/main` and nobody runs `git checkout` or `git merge` in it; records branches and branch syncs are worked in the orchestrator's worktree `E:/mop-build/orch` (`git -C`), a lane branch in its own lane worktree, and a background chain that must bring main into a branch does it there too. The board reads the root; it never changes under it.
- proof: `git -C "E:/Matter Of Place" branch --show-current` prints nothing (detached) and `git -C E:/mop-build/orch branch --show-current` names the records branch in work.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-535 · A slice launch that lists a step the lane's log already shows as done fails at the P-516 coverage check: the sizer leaves done steps out, the check then says the sizing omits them
- symptom: 2026-10-07 04:40 (B13, steps 8 to 13 with startAt g2) and 07:02 (B16, steps 2 to 8): `Error: sizing of B13 omits plan steps 8, 9 (P-516)` and `sizing of B16 omits plan step 2 (P-516)` at build-slice.js line 166, two minutes and about 95k tokens of sizing each time, before any builder.
- cause: the sizer reads the tail of `workspace/05-plans/logs/<slice>.md` and treats a step with an accepted block as done (as the brief asks), while the coverage check compares the groups against `args.steps` literally; a step both done and listed has no group.
- rule: a launch or relaunch passes only steps the log does not show accepted (read the log's last blocks first, or the ledger's `accepted` list); `startAt` is for resuming a run with a cached sizing, never for skipping done steps in a fresh run. A relaunch after a stop lists the remaining steps alone.
- proof: B13 relaunched as steps ["10","11","12","13"] sized and built; B16 relaunched as ["3","4","5","6","7","8"] sized and built (the second sizer then still grouped the step 2 remainder on its own, which the check accepts because 2 was not in args.steps).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-536 · Agents of one session share one scratchpad folder, so a builder's or reviewer's scratch file is overwritten by another lane's agent while it runs
- symptom: 2026-10-07 on the Dell, four times: a reviewer's scratch registry `B10.json` held another reviewer's copy and `watchfail` replayed 69 entries instead of 45 (B10 g3 review ac85eb06); the B6 g4 builder's registry-script file was overwritten by another lane (a6892ffb); a seven-entry replay reported `replayed 77: ok 7, bad 1, stale 69` (B11 g3 review a4a83cb8); one more in B10 g5.
- cause: every agent of a Claude Code session receives the same scratchpad path (the session's `scratchpad/`), and five lanes run as agents of one session on a lane machine.
- rule: an agent writes its scratch files under `scratchpad/<its agent id or group label>/` and reads only there; a scratch registry for a replay is created fresh per replay. The brief says it (build-slice.js, at the next run boundary); until then a clobbered scratch file is re-created under the agent's own folder, which is the agent's own scratch and not one of our scripts, so the report-not-fix rule does not apply.
- proof: `watchfail` replays with `--registry <own folder>` report exactly the entries the agent wrote (B10 g5 review2 a08c8b4b: 28 entries, 28 replayed).
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B6 g1 step 7 review: the reviewer's replay summary (`wf.txt`, `wf-one.txt`) and its first check log (`check.txt`) in the scratchpad root were overwritten by a B11 registry replay that used the same names (the first `wf.txt` held `WATCHED-FAIL OK B11:b11-g9-hy-order` lines from a loop over `b6-s7-*` ids only), so the full `bun run check` and the 44-entry replay ran twice, about 15 minutes. The rerun in `scratchpad/b6g1-rev-7q2/` gave `ok=44 total=44` and check exit 0. Name the folder after lane, group and a random suffix, never a common file name at the scratchpad root. Proof: `grep -c "hit again: 2026-10-08, B6 g1 step 7 review" GOTCHAS.md` prints 1.

## P-2019 · A db test's raw insert went red in CI after a merge of main brought another slice's check constraint on the same table
- symptom: B7 g2's `tests/db/people.db.test.ts` passed on mop-dev (8 of 8) and failed in CI's `db` job at 3462975 (run 37561577159): `new row for relation "payments" violates check constraint "payments_number_unless_waived"`. The fixture inserted a `payments` row without `invoice_number`.
- cause: B6's `20261006224201_invoicing.sql` landed on main between the lane's mop-dev proof and the CI run and added `check (invoice_number is not null or status = 'waived')`. The lane's proof was older than the schema it ran against in CI.
- rule: after every `git merge origin/main` that brings a migration, list the tables it alters (`git diff --stat <old base> origin/main -- app/supabase/migrations`, then `grep -n "add constraint" <file>`) and re-run every db test of the branch that inserts into one of them before pushing. A fixture insert gives every column a constraint of the newest migrations requires (here `invoice_number => 'TEST-' || gen_random_uuid()`, as `gate.db.test.ts` does).
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "payments_number_unless_waived" supabase/migrations/20261006224201_invoicing.sql` → line 33; with the dev profile and the two B7 migrations as `MOP_MUTATION_SQL` (P-312), `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/people.db.test.ts` → `Tests  8 passed (8)` with `invoice_number` in the insert (measured 2026-10-07 05:35 +0300).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2020 · A watched-fail entry that went red only because the schema lacked a name stayed green once main added the name
- symptom: CI's `db` job at 80a5917 (run 37564493046, step "mutation replay") failed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: stayed green (B7:b7-g5-db-payments-status)`; the same entry was OK when B7 g1 recorded it.
- cause: the entry replaced the payments filter with `.neq("status", "void")`. Before B6, `void` was no value of `payment_status`, so the query errored and the test went red; B6's `20261006224200_invoicing_enum.sql` added `void`, the mutated query became valid and the test (`newestPaymentId` for an unknown id answers null) stayed green. The earlier CI run had stopped at the test step, so the replay first ran a round later.
- rule: a mutation whose red depends on a name the schema does not have uses a name no migration will add (`voided`, `__missing`), never a word a later slice may adopt; after a merge of main that brings a migration, replay every entry of the branch's registry whose `run` names `--project db` before pushing (`--only <id>` each, dev profile, P-312 prelude for unmerged migrations); a file mutation with a db run has no `kind`, so `--kinds sql` does not select it.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" && env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b7-g5-db-payments-status` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B7:b7-g5-db-payments-status` with `voided` (measured 2026-10-07 06:05 +0300).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2021 · Ruling H66's shell (`await import()` of `src/admin` in `beforeLoad`) fails bundle-check: every public route chunk imports the entry, and the walk follows the entry's dynamic imports
- symptom: B7 g3 (step 6) turned `admin.tsx`, `admin/auth.confirm.tsx`, `admin/sign-in.tsx`, `admin/requests.index.tsx` and `admin/requests.$id.tsx` into shells as the step says (static imports only the router, `lib/seo` and `?url`; helpers and pages through `await import()` in `beforeLoad`, the error and not-found screens through `lazyRouteComponent`). `admin-route-shells.test.ts` passed with `LEGACY` empty and the live build shrank (`_site` 145945 to 145195, `_site.property.$slug` 153690 to 152974 gzip bytes), but `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs .output` printed `FAIL a chunk a public route can reach holds src/admin/ui/AdminLayout.tsx` and eight more, `bundle-check: FAILED 9`. The conversion was taken back out of the group.
- cause: in the live manifest all 24 public route chunks list the client entry in `imports`, and `checkManifest` walks each with `reach(key, true)`, so it descends into the entry and then into all 37 of the entry's `dynamicImports` (every route's split chunk and every `await import()` target). A dynamically imported module gets a chunk whose `src` is that module, so `src/admin/...` matches FORBIDDEN; modules a split component imports statically sit in unnamed shared chunks and pass. P-2013 measured the refusal on 2026-10-06; H66 (2026-10-07) prescribes the mechanism the check refuses. - rule: do not move an admin route's imports into `await import()` of `src/admin/**` (or `lazyRouteComponent` of one) until the orchestrator rules between changing bundle-check's walk as above and allowing `.lazy.tsx` siblings again (their chunk `src` is under `src/routes/admin`, which is why the People routes pass); the five files stay in `LEGACY` until then.

## P-2023 · B7 step 7 asks that a wrong preview signature cost no database call, and B2's token format cannot check a signature without the nonce
- symptom: the proof list of B7 step 7 says `previews.service.test.ts` shows that "wrong signature, expired token and an undefined key make zero database calls". The token is `<property_id>.<exp>.<hmac>` with the HMAC over `<property_id>.<exp>.<preview_nonce>` (invariant 14), and the nonce lives on the row, so a well formed token signed with another key reaches the one `preview_property` call before `verifyPreview` can refuse it.
- cause: the plan's `checkPreviewSignature` is defined as "signature shape and expiry, no database"; the sentence in the proof list reads "signature" as the HMAC itself.
- rule: test the three cases the format allows with no call (a malformed or expired token, an unset key) and the wrong HMAC as one `preview_property` call then 404, and say so in the log. A zero-call HMAC check needs a second, nonce-free MAC in the token: a format change of B2's, not a test fix.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/previews.service.test.ts` → `Tests  9 passed (9)`, with the cases "a malformed signature is 404 with no database call" and "a well formed signature under another key is 404 after the one read of the nonce" (measured 2026-10-07, B7 g1 step 7).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2024 · A preview-token page answered no `x-mop-cache` header: the pipeline keeps it from the cache hook, so nothing labelled it `bypass`
- symptom: B7 step 7a's proof `curl -sI "http://localhost:8080/property/<slug>?preview=<token>"` showed `cache-control: no-store` and `x-robots-tag: noindex, nofollow` but no `x-mop-cache` line, while the API form with `?draft_token=` showed `x-mop-cache: bypass`; the cf:preview leg greps for `bypass` on the page.
- cause: `handle()` in `src/server/lib/pipeline.ts` computes `page = !neverCached(...) && isPageRequest(...)`, so a `?preview=` page never calls `deps.cache` (`cachedResponse` is where `bypass` is written); the API route calls `cachedResponse` itself, which labels it. Step 7's tests asserted the skipped hook and `no-store`, never the label.
- rule: a request that is never cached for being a preview link (`framing === "self"`) gets `x-mop-cache: bypass` in the `neverCached` branch of `handle()` when no layer set one; a header a plan's proof greps for gets its own assertion, not only the behaviour behind it.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/pipeline.test.ts -t "labels a preview-token answer"` passes, and the registry entry `b7-g3a-pipe-bypass` turns it red (`WATCHED-FAIL OK B7:b7-g3a-pipe-bypass`); on the built Worker at port 8948 the preview page printed `x-mop-cache: bypass`, the plain page `miss`, then `hit` (measured 2026-10-08, B7 g3).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2025 · A response-header change passed every unit case and went red only in the e2e job, which a draft pull request skips
- symptom: B7 g3 step 7a labelled every `?preview=` answer `x-mop-cache: bypass` in `src/server/lib/pipeline.ts` (P-2024). The unit cases and `bun run check` were green; once PR 230 left draft, the `e2e` and `preview` jobs failed on desktop and phone at `tests/e2e/essentials.spec.ts:155` (`consent-html`, `expect(response.headers()["x-mop-cache"]).toBeUndefined()` on `/?preview=consent`).
