## P-2026 · H71's second Lighthouse attempt cannot finish inside the preview job's 20-minute limit
- symptom: B7 g3, PR 230 at aad89d9: the `preview` job failed at 20m16s with `lighthouse cancelled` and `##[error]The operation was canceled.`; every step before it passed, `essentials` included. Attempt 1 hung and printed `::warning title=lighthouse attempt 1 did not finish::preview hang, retried (ruling H71)` at 05:29:26 UTC; attempt 2 had run five pages when the job was cancelled at 05:36:06.
- cause: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` gives the `preview` job `timeout-minutes: 20` and its `lighthouse` step `timeout-minutes: 22` with two attempts of `timeout 600`. The steps before Lighthouse take about 4 minutes and a hung attempt 1 takes 10, so attempt 2 has about 6 minutes left, less than a full run of the page list.
- rule: a red `preview` job whose only failure is `lighthouse cancelled` after the H71 warning is this environment hang, not the branch: rerun the failed job once (`gh run rerun <run> --failed`) and report both runs. The owner of `deploy.yml` raises the job limit above the steps before Lighthouse plus two 10-minute attempts, or the retry never gets its time.
- proof: `gh run view 37731474092 --log --job 113161392010 | grep -a lighthouse | grep -a -E "attempt 1 did not finish|canceled"` prints the warning line at 05:29:26 and the cancel at 05:36:06; `grep -n "timeout-minutes: 20" .github/workflows/deploy.yml` lists line 83 (the `preview` job) (measured 2026-10-08).
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B7 g2 round 1, PR 248 at 965a268f: deploy run 37800785601's `preview` failed after `lighthouse attempt 1 did not finish` and an `lhci` SIGTERM at 15:42 UTC; `gh run rerun 37800785601 --failed` gave attempt 2 `preview success`.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-09, B7 g4: PR 250's `preview` job (run 37868492661) failed at 14m1s with `lighthouse cancelled` and `##[error]The operation was canceled.` during the third Lighthouse run of `/submit`; every step before it passed. Rerun once with `gh run rerun 37868492661 --failed`, as the rule says: the rerun (job 113624749057, 01:25 to 01:52 UTC) ended `cancelled` too, its log stopping at `Run #3...` of `/exposure` and `Process completed with exit code 1`. The group changed admin routes, server code and the generated route tree, no public page file; the job stays UNPROVEN and the orchestrator reads it.

## P-2127 · `fakeDb` answers a table with all its rows, has no `or` or `maybeSingle`, and a stub that sorts per `order()` call hides a wrong order
- symptom: B7 g1 step 5 (`getSubmission`, `entityTimeline`) reads through filters, `.or(entityJobsFilter(id))`, `.maybeSingle()` and two `.order()` calls. `tests/fixtures/fake-db.ts` answers every registered table with all its rows whatever the query, and its query object has no `or` and no `maybeSingle`. The first stub written for it applied each `order()` call on its own, so the second call replaced the first; the registry entries `b7-g5-get-order` and `b7-g5-payment-order` (ordering reversed) replayed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: stayed green`.
- cause: PostgREST composes every `order()` call, the first as the primary key; a stub that re-sorts per call keeps only the last, and a test passes whatever the first key does.
- rule: a service that reads through filters, `or`, `maybeSingle` or a sort is tested with `withTables(fakeDb(), { table: rows })` of `tests/fixtures/table-stub.ts`, which applies `eq`, `in`, the PostgREST `or` text of `entityJobsFilter`, composed `order` calls, `limit` and the column list; it does not add a table the test did not register. A stub with its own semantics is itself watched-failed through the service's registry entries (an ordering mutation must go red).
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/timeline.test.ts tests/unit/submissions.service.test.ts` passes, and `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b7-g5-get-order` and `--only b7-g5-payment-order` print `WATCHED-FAIL OK` (both printed `BAD: stayed green` with the per-call sort, 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2128 · Four gates of `bun run check` for new admin files only fail at the end, and `quiet.mjs -- ... | tail` hides which step failed
- symptom: B7 g1 step 5 ran `bun run check` four times (about four minutes each). Reds, in order: prettier on a new route file in `src/routes/api/admin` that no one had formatted; knip `Unused exports (2)` (`submissionPhotoSchema`, `timelineEntrySchema` exported but used only in their own file); `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` `keeps admin components away from *-api modules` (the new `RequestDetail.test.tsx` imported `./requests-api`, a `.tsx` under `src/admin`); `tests/unit/admin-motion.test.ts` `takes the tokens and its own files only` (the new `requests.css` was imported after `ui.css`, the test wants `index.css` to list the sheets in file-name order). Piping `quiet.mjs -- bun run check | tail -3` showed only `script "test" exited with code 1`, not the failing test.
- cause: those gates (formatter, knip, two repository tests) run after typecheck and lint, and the one-line summary hid the failing step.

## P-2129 · A `loader` in an admin route file keeps its imports in the public entry: `bundle-check` fails five public routes by 1 to 4 KB
- symptom: B7 g1 step 5: `requests.$id.tsx` had `loader: ensureQueryData(submissionQuery(id))` (to throw `notFound()` before the page drew) and `head` read `loaderData`. In a live-mode build `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs` printed `FAIL _site.property.$slug loads 157821 gzip bytes, over the budget of 153600` and four more (`_site.index` 154684, `_site.$market.index` 156026, `_site.$market.$region` 155544, `_site.properties` 155085); main at 7e4b7a9 measures `_site.property.$slug` 153238 and `_site.index` 150100. A build without `VITE_API_BASE_URL` fails 24 routes and holds the seed title, which is not the CI artifact.
- cause: the router plugin splits `component`, `errorComponent`, `notFoundComponent` and `pendingComponent` into the route's own chunk; `loader` and `head` stay in the route tree the public entry loads, with every module they import (the query module, the API wrapper, the admin Zod schemas). The page-level 404 is thrown from the component instead.
- rule: an admin route file has no `loader`, and its `head` reads only `params`; the page reads its data in its own component and throws `notFound()` there on a 404. After any admin route change run the CI live build, `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA; bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs`; every new route file also adds a few dozen bytes to the route tree of every public route (this group: `_site.property.$slug` 153238 to 153453 against 153600), so the next admin route groups should expect the budget to bind.
- proof: with the loader and `loaderData` head back in `src/routes/admin/requests.$id.tsx`, the build above and `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs` print `bundle-check: FAILED 5`; as handed in they print `bundle-check: OK 22 routes under 153600 gzip bytes` (measured 2026-10-07, main baseline measured by stashing the work).
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B7 g1 step 5: `export ...; node workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- sh -c "bun run build && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs"` printed `bundle-check: FAILED 24` (every route over 153600, and `holds the seed title`), a build that was not live; running `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA node workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- bun run build` and then `node scripts/bundle-check.mjs` on its own printed `OK 22 routes`. Why the wrapped form lost the variables is UNPROVEN; give the variables to the build command itself.

## P-2130 · `bun run check` ends red on one hygiene case that has its own 20 s limit, while the script's 60 s flag is meant to cover every test
- symptom: B7 g1 step 5: two full `bun run check` runs (about 6 minutes each, other lanes running) passed every gate before the tests and ended `FAIL |unit| tests/unit/hygiene.test.ts > the orchestrator's merge script is under the app's gates (H42 (2), G-032) > lint gives prettier/prettier the options of .prettierrc for it`, `Error: Test timed out in 20000ms`, `error: script "check" exited with code 1`; `bunx vitest run tests/unit/hygiene.test.ts -t "lint gives prettier"` alone passed in 13.6 s.
- cause: the case ends `}, 20_000);` (`tests/unit/hygiene.test.ts:958`), which overrides `--testTimeout=60000` of the `test` script (G-031); `ESLint.calculateConfigForFile` with the type-aware config takes more than 20 s while two vitest workers and other lanes' builds share the cores. Not this group's file, so it was not changed (UNPROVEN that main fails the same way under the same load).
- rule: a case that builds a type-aware ESLint takes no inline timeout shorter than the script's 60 s (the owner of `hygiene.test.ts` removes the `20_000`); until then a red check whose only failure is this case is re-run alone, and the log says so.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "20_000" tests/unit/hygiene.test.ts | head -3` → the line ending `}, 20_000);` after the `lint gives prettier/prettier` case; `bunx vitest run tests/unit/hygiene.test.ts -t "lint gives prettier"` → `Tests  3 passed | 60 skipped (63)` (measured 2026-10-07 03:04 +0300).
- added: 2026-10-07

## G-902 · A db test that imports a `src/server` module fails at collection with `Invalid environment: RATE_LIMIT_SALT Required`
- paths: app/tests/db/**, app/tests/api/**
- severity: warn
- symptom: B7 g1 step 5: `tests/db/admin.db.test.ts` imported `newestPaymentId` from `src/server/submissions/service.ts`; `bunx vitest run --project db tests/db/admin.db.test.ts -t getSubmission` ended `Error: Invalid environment: RATE_LIMIT_SALT Required` (`src/server/lib/env.ts:70`, reached through `upload-token.ts:2`) and `Tests  no tests`.
- cause: `service.ts` imports `upload-token.ts`, which parses `env.ts` at import. Unit tests set the variable by importing `tests/fixtures/worker-env.ts` first; the db project has no setup file for it.
- rule: a db or api test that loads any `src/server` module imports `../fixtures/worker-env` as its first import (it sets `MOP_ENV` to `local` and the salt). It deletes the ambient `SUPABASE_URL` so a unit test cannot reach another project (G-901), except under `E2E_STACK=1`: that is CI's own stack, `serviceClient()` reads `SUPABASE_URL` there, and a db test that deleted it fails with `SUPABASE_URL is not set`. A db proof runs once in the laptop shape (dev profile) and once in the CI shape (below).
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" && env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx vitest run --project db tests/db/admin.db.test.ts -t getSubmission` → `Tests  1 passed | 16 skipped`; with the import line deleted → `Invalid environment: RATE_LIMIT_SALT Required` (measured 2026-10-07). CI shape, after the dev profile: `U="https://$DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF.supabase.co"; K="$DEV_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY"; env -u DEV_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN E2E_STACK=1 SUPABASE_URL="$U" SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY="$K" bunx vitest run --project db tests/db/admin.db.test.ts -t getSubmission` → `Tests  1 passed | 16 skipped`; with the unguarded fixture delete → `Error: SUPABASE_URL is not set`, `Tests  1 failed | 16 skipped` (measured 2026-10-07, B7 g1 review).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2131 · A db case proven only under the laptop's dev profile can fail in CI's `E2E_STACK` shape
- symptom: B7 g1's getSubmission db case passed on the laptop and failed in the review's CI-shaped run with `SUPABASE_URL is not set`; the author's check (`echo $SUPABASE_URL` shows the dev ref) never exercised the path CI takes.
- cause: `serviceClient()` reads the dev names on the laptop and `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` only under `E2E_STACK=1`; the dev-profile run never reads the second pair, so anything that deletes or renames it stays hidden until CI.
- rule: a new db or api case is run twice, in the laptop shape and in the CI shape of G-902; a fixture that edits `process.env` names which of the two shapes it serves.
- proof: the CI-shape command in G-902 → `Tests  1 passed | 16 skipped` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2132 · `check-gotchas.mjs` does not enforce "keep under 40 live G entries", and the bank stands at 42
- symptom: B7 g1 step 5 added G-902; the review counted the path entries and found the bank over the cap the map states (`Keep under 40 live G entries`, CLAUDE.md "under 40 live path entries"). `check-gotchas: OK` printed throughout. The reviewer's figures (43 on the branch, 42 on origin/main) counted the template heading `## G-0NN` too; the real count is 42 on the branch and 41 on origin/main.
- cause: the check reads headings and field names (P-1214) and has no number for the cap, so a lane that adds a path entry sees nothing, and gardening (moving an entry to "Retired, enforced" once a test holds it) waits for someone to count.
- rule: a lane that adds a G entry counts first (the proof below) and says in its log when the count is above 40; the orchestrator gardens the bank (merge or retire entries a test now enforces) when the gardening pass runs, and does not leave it to a worker's group. Teaching `check-gotchas.mjs` the cap is a change to its own file and goes through the orchestrator.
- proof: `grep -c '^## G-[0-9][0-9][0-9]' GOTCHAS.md` → `42` on slice/b7 and `git show origin/main:GOTCHAS.md | grep -c '^## G-[0-9][0-9][0-9]'` → `41` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2133 · A scratch registry written to a reused short folder name (`reg`) replays other sessions' entries and overwrites their file
- symptom: B7 g3's review wrote a scratch registry to `<scratchpad>/reg` and `watchfail` replayed 147 entries, `ok 7, bad 4, stale 136`, when only 7 were meant. The folder already held B10.json, B10g3.json, B11.json, B8.json and B8b.json from other lanes, and the write replaced whatever B7.json stood there.
- cause: the scratchpad is shared by every session of the project, and folders such as `reg` and `reg2` are reused by name; a replay of a folder replays every registry file in it (P-536 holds the shared-folder fact, this is the reused-name case).
- rule: a scratch registry goes in a folder made fresh for the replay, `mktemp -d "<scratchpad>/reg.XXXXXX"`, never a short name someone may have used; replay with `--registry` on that folder and check the replayed count equals the entries written.
- proof: `ls <scratchpad>/reg` → `B10.json B10g3.json B11.json B7.json B8.json B8b.json` (measured by the B7 g3 review, 2026-10-07; scratchpad = the session's `scratchpad/` folder).
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B16 g8 review: `<scratchpad>/reg` held B7.json and B9.json from an earlier task, so the probe replayed 7 B7 UI mutations against the B16 tree (restored, tree clean). A reviewer's probe registry also gets a fresh folder.
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: B7 g3's step 7a review (2026-10-08) passed a reused scratchpad folder to `watchfail --registry`; it still held B10.json and B11.json, and the summary `replayed 45: ok 10, bad 8, stale 27` read as a regression although every bad id was `B11:b11-g10-*`. Compare the replayed count with the entries written before reading any bad line.

## P-2134 · A review snapshot is a worktree of the lane's repository, so `origin/main` moves under it while the builder fetches and `watchfail --changed origin/main` selects against a moving base
- symptom: during the B7 c6m review, `git rev-parse origin/main` in the snapshot (`D:/mop-build/admin-review`) printed `9c462f5` at the start, `e6f10d9` mid-review and `3ecb616` later, because the builder in `D:/mop-build/admin` fetched meanwhile; a `--changed origin/main` replay in a frozen snapshot picked different entries at different minutes (a few minutes lost to a count that did not repeat).
- cause: a worktree shares the refs of its repository, so a fetch in any tree moves `origin/main` in every tree (P-051 holds the worktree fact, this is the shared-ref case).
- rule: a replay in a review snapshot names the base commit from the author's log (`--changed <sha>`), never `origin/main`; the review states the sha it used.
- proof: `git -C D:/mop-build/admin rev-parse origin/main; git -C D:/mop-build/admin-review rev-parse origin/main` → the same sha twice, and after a `git fetch -q origin` in either tree both print the new one (measured by the B7 c6m review, 2026-10-07: 9c462f5, then e6f10d9, then 3ecb616).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2135 · An admin route shell cannot hold its page: the page moves to src/admin, and a component there reaches an -api module only through a hook file
- symptom: B7 g1 (step 6, H66) turned five admin route files into shells; the page bodies had to leave them (the allowlist forbids `react`, hooks and project modules), and the first `bun run check` after that failed `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts > keeps admin components away from *-api modules` on `src/admin/team/SignInPage.tsx:5 imports ./team-api` (a full check run, about ten minutes, lost). A first attempt to write all files in one heredoc ended in `unexpected EOF` and wrote nothing (P-008).
- cause: in a route file the page called `requestSignInLink` from `team-api` directly, which R41 allows for a route file but not for a component under `src/admin`; moving the body made it a component.
- rule: a page that leaves a shell becomes `src/admin/<feature>/<Name>Page.tsx`, loaded with `lazyRouteComponent(() => import(...), "<Name>Page")` (also for `errorComponent` and `notFoundComponent`), and reads its route through `getRouteApi("<path>")`, not `Route`; whatever it needs from an `-api` module goes through a hook in the feature `-queries.ts` (`useSendSignInLink`). Run `bunx vitest run tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` before the full check.

- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2136 · `watchfail --changed origin/main` on a long-lived lane replays hundreds of entries for tens of minutes, and a shared scratch file name mixes its output with another lane replay
- symptom: B7 g1 step 6 ran `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main > $SCRATCH/wf.txt` after touching five route files; it selected 243 entries (the whole branch diff), ran past two 10-minute tool windows, and the file filled with another lane output (`RUN  v5.0.2 D:/mop-build/b6/app`, a fused line `WATCHEDWATCHED-FAIL`) because two other `watchfail` processes started later wrote the same file name; meanwhile the tree held a mutation of `src/server/submissions/service.ts` and later `src/domain/contracts.ts`. About 35 minutes lost; the process was stopped by id and the mutated file restored with `git checkout`.
- cause: `--changed` selects every entry whose file differs from the base, and a branch that has carried many groups differs from `origin/main` in hundreds of files; the session scratch folder is shared by every worker of the run, so a generic file name collides; a replay in the tree mutates the tree for its whole run.
- rule: replay only the entries of the files the group touched, by id: list them with a node one-liner over `tests/mutations/*.json` (entries whose `file` is one of your files) and run `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only <id> > $SCRATCH/<lane>-<group>-wf-<id>.txt` once each; give every scratch file a lane and group in its name; when a replay is stopped, run `git status --short` and `git checkout` every file that is not yours.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b17-g8-layout-admin` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B17:b17-g8-layout-admin` and `watchfail: replayed 1: ok 1, bad 0, stale 0` in one run of a few seconds (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B8 g1 step 9: a scratch registry put in the session scratchpad's `reg/` folder found three registries another worker had left there (`B7.json`, `B10.json`, `B11.json`); `watchfail --registry <that folder>` selected 45 of their entries with this group's 7 (`replayed 52: ok 7, bad 18, stale 27`, exit 2): the 18 ran against this tree, and nothing of theirs was left mutated (`git status --short` showed only this group's files). A scratch registry goes in a new folder of its own, `mktemp -d`, holding only its one file.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B8 g1 step 10 review: a reviewer wrote `bun run check` output to a generic `check.txt` in the session scratchpad; another agent sharing the scratchpad overwrote it mid-run, the file first read `74 lines ... done` with no exit line from the reviewer's own command and then `93 lines ... exit=0` after the background task ended, so the first read was another agent's `quiet: ok`. Reviewers and builders alike write to a uniquely named subfolder of the scratchpad (`mktemp -d`, or a name with lane and group) and read the exit line of their own command before trusting a file.

## P-2200 · A B10 script cannot call the RPCs and tables of `social.sql` through the typed client before that migration merges
- symptom: B10 g1 (step 0) has to write scripts that call `store_channel_token`, `put_channel_ids`, `get_vault_secret` and read `social_posts`, but `src/db/types.ts` lists none of `store_channel_token`, `put_channel_ids` and `record_channel_check` and no `social_posts` table (`get_vault_secret` is there since B8's retention migration) until step 6's migration is merged and `bun run gen:types` has run. A typed `createClient<Database>` call fails `bun run typecheck`, an untyped client fails the lint (P-810), and a cast fails `no-unsafe-type-assertion`.
- cause: the plan puts the scripts in step 0 and the migration in step 6; "through the service role" assumed the generated types would already name them.
- rule: a script that touches a function or table of an unmerged migration goes through `scripts/lib/dev-db.ts` (`rpc` and `select` over PostgREST, the answer parsed with the schema the caller passes), never a cast or an untyped client; the call is UNPROVEN until the migration is on `mop-dev`, and the group's log says so. Step 6 may move those calls to the typed client once `types.ts` has them.
- proof: `grep -c "dev-db" app/scripts/lib/oauth-consent.ts app/scripts/lib/test-post.ts app/scripts/meta-check.ts app/scripts/x-limits-check.ts` prints one line per file with a count of at least 1; `git grep -n "social_posts\|store_channel_token" -- app/src/db/types.ts` prints nothing on the B10 g1 commit.
- added: 2026-10-07

- hit again: 2026-10-07, B10 g5: the same gap in `src/`, where `scripts/lib/dev-db.ts` is out of reach: `oauth-tokens.ts` calls `store_channel_token`, `record_channel_check` and `record_channel_usage` before step 6 adds them to `src/db/types.ts`. A local interface with a method `rpc(fn: string, args: Record<string, Json>): PromiseLike<{ data: unknown; error: unknown }>` accepts the typed `Db` by assignment (`const client: UntypedRpc = db;`, method parameters compare both ways), so no cast is needed; it sits under a `STUB(B10 step 6)` marker and the answers are parsed with Zod. The unit tests pass the handlers to `fakeDb` as a variable (`tests/fixtures/social-api.ts`), because a literal key the generated types lack fails the excess-property check. Proof: `cd app && bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` prints nothing on slice/b10 at g5.

## P-2201 · Two scripts with the same argument skeleton fail jscpd at 71 tokens, and a closure that sets a flag fails the lint as "always falsy"
- symptom: B10 g1's first `bun run jscpd` printed `x-authorize.ts [19:82 - 30:17]` and `linkedin-authorize.ts [17:83 - 28:17]` as one clone of 12 lines and 71 tokens (threshold 70, R04); the first `eslint` run called `return failed ? 1 : 0` in `meta-check.ts` "Unnecessary conditional, value is always falsy" (a `let failed = false` set from a closure) and the spread `...init.headers` in `x-limits-check.ts` `no-misused-spread` (HeadersInit can be an array).
- cause: the plan lists `x-authorize.ts` and `linkedin-authorize.ts` as two files that both parse `--target` and `--check`, guard the shell and read two secrets; TypeScript narrows a `let` assigned only in a closure to its initial value; `HeadersInit` is a union that includes arrays.
- rule: put the shared argument skeleton of paired scripts in `scripts/lib/` (`authorize()` in `oauth-consent.ts`) before the first `bun run jscpd`; collect check results in an array (`results.every(Boolean)`), never a `let` set in a closure; build headers from a `Record<string, string>`, never by spreading `init.headers`.
- proof: `cd app && bun run jscpd` exits 0 with `authorize(` in `scripts/lib/oauth-consent.ts`; copying the `parseArgs` block back into both scripts makes it print `Found 1 clones` (B10 g1, 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2202 · Meta's documentation cannot be read with a plain fetch: guessed reference addresses answer 404, and the text extraction drops every code span
- symptom: B10 g2 step 3 fetched `developers.facebook.com/docs/...` with curl; `instagram-platform/reference/ig-user/media` and the `instagram-api-with-facebook-login/reference/...` variants answered 404 with a page in Arabic, the one page that worked held its text only as escaped JSON, and an extraction of the quoted strings lost every field name, number and status value, because those are code spans (`DeveloperCode` nodes) and not text.
- cause: the site is rendered client-side from a JSON tree, the reference pages live under `/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/` (the dash-joined ids in the page source are not addresses), and the default locale follows the caller's region.
- rule: fetch with `-A "Mozilla/5.0" -H "Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9"` from `/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/<node>` (`ig-user/media`, `ig-user/content_publishing_limit`, `ig-media/insights`, `ig-container`, `error-codes`) and `/docs/page-stories-api`; split the HTML on the escaped quote `\"` to read the prose, and confirm every name, code and value by grepping the raw HTML for it (`children\":[\"2207042\"]`), because the prose omits them; write a claim you could not grep as UNPROVEN. The Graph reference pages for Page photos and Page posts return no reference text this way.
- proof: `curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" -H "Accept-Language: en-US,en;q=0.9" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media` → `200`, and the same with `instagram-platform/reference/ig-user/media` → `404` (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2203 · A gotcha entry that lists what the generated types lack was written from the plan, not from the file, and named a function that exists
- symptom: P-2200 (B10 g1) said `src/db/types.ts` lists none of `store_channel_token`, `put_channel_ids` and `get_vault_secret`; the g1 reviewer found `get_vault_secret` at `app/src/db/types.ts` line 1177, there since B8's retention migration. Only `store_channel_token`, `put_channel_ids`, `record_channel_check` and `social_posts` are missing. The group's log had the list right, the bank entry did not, and a reader who trusts the entry would route a call through `dev-db.ts` that the typed client already types.
- cause: the entry copied the plan's list of the RPCs the scripts call, and the "missing from the types" claim was never checked against the file.
- rule: a claim in an entry that a name is absent from a generated file is proved by a grep of that file for each name, one grep per name, before the entry is written; the proof line of such an entry names the same grep.
- proof: `git grep -c "get_vault_secret" -- app/src/db/types.ts` prints `app/src/db/types.ts:1`, and the same grep for `store_channel_token`, `put_channel_ids`, `record_channel_check` and `social_posts` prints nothing on the B10 g1 commit (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2204 · R34 asks for an exported error table and R04's knip refuses an export nothing imports: `GRAPH_ERROR_TABLE` failed `bun run check`
- symptom: B10 g3's first `bun run check` stopped at knip with `Unused exports (1) GRAPH_ERROR_TABLE src/server/channels/meta-errors.ts:13:14`, after typecheck and lint were green; the whole check ran a second time once the `export` was removed.
- cause: STANDARDS R34 says each adapter classifies "through an exported error table", but the only reader of the table is `classifyGraphError` in the same file, and the unit tests call the classifier, not the table. knip (R04) counts only imports.
- rule: an error table stays a module constant until a second file imports it; the classifier is the export. When a later step (an adapter, a health screen) needs the rows themselves, it adds the `export` in the same commit as its import.
- proof: `cd app && bun run knip` exits 0 on slice/b10 at B10 g3; with `export` put back before `const GRAPH_ERROR_TABLE` in `src/server/channels/meta-errors.ts` it prints `Unused exports (1)` naming that line (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2205 · B10 step 4 says every metric of the recorded Graph fixture maps to a normalised field, but the fixture is docs-made and holds `total_interactions`, which maps to none
- symptom: `tests/fixtures/graph/media-insights.json` (B10 g2) answers `reach`, `likes` and `total_interactions`, copied from Meta's documentation, not from a live post. `total_interactions` is likes plus saves plus comments plus shares and has no field in `{ reach, views, saves, shares, likes, comments, clicks }`, so the plan's case "every metric in the recorded fixtures maps to a normalised field" cannot hold, and its watched-fail (f) ("map `impressions` back when the live call does not return it") cannot be read from a fixture that never was a live call.
- cause: the plan was written for a fixture recorded from the step 7 test post, which is BLOCKED until the Meta app exists (S59); g2 wrote the fixture from the docs in its place.
- rule: until step 7 records a live insights answer, `meta-metrics.test.ts` checks that every table name in the fixture lands in its field, that `total_interactions` and any other unknown name land only in `raw`, and that every table name is on Meta's documented list for new media (read 2026-10-07, held in the test), which is what turns (f) red. Step 7 replaces the fixture with the recorded answer and tightens the first case to "every name in the answer is a table name".
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/channels/meta-metrics.test.ts` passes 3 tests on B10 g3; `node -e "console.log(require('./tests/fixtures/graph/media-insights.json').source)"` prints `docs`.

## P-2206 · A fake-timer test of code that awaits Web Crypto before its sleep moves the clock too early and hangs
- symptom: B10 g4's first run of `tests/unit/channels/meta.test.ts`: "stops polling at FINISHED" timed out at 5000 ms, "returns in_progress after 5 status calls" saw 0 status calls after `vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(19_999)`, and the publish promise left running turned into an unhandled rejection that failed the next test (its `sent` list began with a stale `POST .../media`).
- cause: `meta.ts` computes `appsecret_proof` with `crypto.subtle` before its first call, and Web Crypto answers on a real tick, not as a microtask. `advanceTimersByTimeAsync` flushes microtasks only, so it ran before the adapter reached its `setTimeout`; the sleep it started later was never advanced.
- rule: for code that awaits Web Crypto, a Response body or any real I/O before a timer, fake only `setTimeout` (`vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setTimeout"] })`, so `setImmediate` stays real), wait with a real-tick loop until `vi.getTimerCount() > 0`, then advance one interval (`nextPoll` in the test); assert a call count only after that wait, and never after one advance taken before the sleep exists.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/channels/meta.test.ts` → `Tests  34 passed (34)`; with the `while (vi.getTimerCount() === 0) await tick();` line of `nextPoll` removed, "stops polling at FINISHED" times out (verified 2026-10-07, B10 g4).
- added: 2026-10-07

## G-1000 · `index.ts` registers the Meta adapter and `meta.ts` imports the pure functions of `index.ts`: build adapters on demand, never at load

- severity: warn

No gate catches it (no cycle rule in eslint or knip); it was found by reading before writing.

- rule: `adapters` in `index.ts` holds factories (`() => createMetaChannel("instagram")`) and `getChannel` calls the factory; step 5a registers x, linkedin and youtube the same way. Do not move `filesFor`, `captionFor` or `targetsFor` into the adapter files.

- symptom: B10 g5's first `bun run jscpd` failed with one clone, `server/channels/meta.ts [57:82 - 69:3] (13 lines, 73 tokens)` against `server/channels/oauth-tokens.ts`, after typecheck, lint and knip were green: the new adapter copied `meta.ts`'s `const jsonValue: z.ZodType<Json> = z.lazy(() => z.union([...]))` to type a provider answer as `Json` for `metrics.raw`.

The author listed it as a cost under G-103, whose line covers only the lint casts (recorded by the g4 review follow-up).

## P-2210 · A stateful fake that does not model the write its SQL function makes lets a test read the fake's gap as a bug
- symptom: B10 g5's first run of the x.test refresh case saw two token refreshes where the code makes one: the fake Vault in `tests/fixtures/social-api.ts` answered `store_channel_token` with `stored` but kept the old set, so the next `get_vault_secret` handed back the expiring token and the code refreshed again. The cost was first banked under P-076, which is about lint idioms; the B10 g5 review named the miss.
- cause: `store_channel_token` (B10 plan, Files; `social.sql` is written in step 6) writes the new set into Vault; a fake that answers the RPC without that write models a database where the store silently fails.
- rule: a fake RPC that stands for a SQL function with a side effect performs that side effect on the fake's state (on `stored`, `socialDb` replaces its Vault list with the stored set); when a test sees the code repeat a call, check the fake models every write before changing the code.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/channels/oauth-tokens.test.ts tests/unit/channels/x.test.ts` → all pass on slice/b10; `grep -n "store_channel_token" tests/fixtures/social-api.ts` → line 112, `if (answer === "stored") vault.splice(0, vault.length, args.p_token_set);`.

## P-2211 · `review-snapshot.mjs create` outlasts the Bash tool's 120 s default timeout and moves to the background
- symptom: the B10 g5 review's first `node workspace/05-plans/review-snapshot.mjs create D:/mop-build/social <sha>` printed `Command did not complete within its 120s timeout and was moved to the background`, and the reviewer did not know when the snapshot (worktree plus `bun install --frozen-lockfile`) was complete. The earlier g5 review hit the same wait and left it in its log (B10.md) for the orchestrator; no entry held it.
- cause: `create` makes a git worktree and runs a frozen install in `app/`, which takes several minutes on a loaded laptop; the Bash tool's default timeout is 120000 ms.
- rule: run `create` with `run_in_background: true`, or with `timeout: 600000`, and wait for its final `rc` line before the first command in the snapshot (P-027: a bounded loop, never a leading `sleep`); never start `bun run check` in the folder while `create` still runs.
- proof: `grep -n "bun install" workspace/05-plans/review-snapshot.mjs` → the line `execSync("bun install --frozen-lockfile", { cwd: join(snap, "app"), ...` (the install that makes `create` slow); `grep -c "^## P-2211" GOTCHAS.md` → 1.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2213 · A step module that imports something reaching `fanout.ts` closes a cycle through the step registry, which is then built with `undefined` steps
- symptom: B10 g6 added `maybeAutoApprove` to the render steps' `onResult` and to `runWriteCaptions`; `auto-approve.ts` imported `fanoutEvent` statically, and `tests/unit/assets/steps.test.ts` failed 17 cases with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'type')` at `steps.find((step) => step.type === type)` in `src/server/jobs/steps/index.ts`.

## P-2214 · fakeDb's typed RPC map cannot answer null for a function whose generated `Returns` is not nullable, such as `enqueue_job` on a key it already holds
- symptom: B10 g6 needed `enqueue_job` to answer null for a second `notify_admin` with the same key (`notifyAdmin` reports to Sentry only for a new job); `tsc` refused the handler: `Type 'string | null' is not assignable to type 'string | Error | Promise<string | Error>'`.

## P-2215 · The CI `db` job skips a draft pull request, so a lane told to open a draft gets no database proof from it

## P-2216 · Changing a SQL function's signature turns other slices' `sql` watched-fails into overloads, and the find-count cannot see them
- symptom: B10 g6 gave `approve_asset` a fifth parameter (`p_evidence jsonb default null`). B9's `sql` entries `b9g6-approve-event`, `-agent`, `-not-pending`, `-og-cover` and `-og-none` still ran `create or replace function public.approve_asset(` with four parameters, which creates a second overload, so every four-argument call in `assets.db.test.ts` failed with `function public.approve_asset(unknown, unknown, actor_kind, unknown) is not unique`, and `b9g6-auth-approve_asset` granted on a signature that no longer existed. The review's replay printed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: wrong reason (B9:b9g6-approve-event)`. The group's H60 find-count (331 entries, 0 stale) passed, and CI's `--changed` replay did not select them because `assets.db.test.ts` was unchanged.
- cause: a `sql` entry carries a whole copy of the function under its old signature; Postgres matches `create or replace` by argument types, so a new signature is a new function. The find-count reads only `file` entries.
- rule: when a migration changes a function's arguments, `grep -o "function public.<name>([^)]*)" tests/mutations/*.json | sort | uniq -c` and rebuild every entry still on the old signature from the new function file with the entry's own one-line mutation (a script that checks the find occurs once), then replay those entries with the unpushed migrations as the P-312 prelude through a scratch registry holding only them (P-1305).
- proof: from `app/` on slice/b10 after the fix, the grep above lists only `(uuid, uuid, public.actor_kind, text, jsonb)` and the five-parameter header, and the six B9 entries replayed with the three B10 migrations in front gave `watchfail: replayed 6: ok 6, bad 0, stale 0` (mop-dev inside rolled-back transactions, measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2217 · A module-level fixture object handed to `channelWorld` is mutated by the fake RPCs, so the next test starts from the earlier test's row
- symptom: B10 g6's new post-meta case "a temporary error while an earlier container is published, near the window end, moves the post" passed alone (`-t`) and failed in the whole file with `{ status: 'done', result: { instagram: { result: 'failed', error: 'token_dead' } } }`: the case before it had failed the same row.
- cause: `const MARKED = { posts: [postRow(...)] }` built the row once; `tests/fixtures/channel-db.ts` keeps the row objects it is given and `fail_social_post` assigns `status` and `error` onto them.
- rule: give each test its own rows: a factory (`const marked = () => ({ posts: [postRow(...)] })`), never a shared constant, for anything a fake database writes to.
- proof: from `app/`, `bunx vitest run tests/unit/channels/post-meta.test.ts` → `Tests  9 passed (9)` with the factory; with the constant the run printed `Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2405 · The Nitro server build can form a chunk cycle on Linux only, and every request of the Worker then answers 500 `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')`
- symptom: B7 g1 (step 7) at 61dacc8: CI's `check`, `build` and `db` passed, `e2e` failed at `[WebServer] ✘ [ERROR] TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` on every request (`.output/server/_ssr/DQNJrwJb2.mjs:207`, the `suffix` line of `src/lib/seo.ts`), and `preview` failed at "the Worker did not answer ten times in a row in 180 s". The laptop's build of the same commit served `/` 200 under `wrangler dev`. slice/b16's CI build on the same main had no cycle and passed e2e.
- cause: Rolldown groups Nitro's server chunks differently on Linux and Windows. In CI's `build-output` artifact two `_ssr` chunks import each other: the one with `siteConfig`, the contracts and the router asset imports `publishChecklist` and 41 more names back from the one with `seo.ts`, which reads 65 bindings of the first at its top level (98 eager reads, counted with an acorn walk). Whichever chunk loads first reads the other's `var`s before they are set. The `$initial` group of ruling H62 sits in the top-level `build.rolldownOptions`, which reaches the Nitro build too (P-2008), but it is not the whole cause: moving the group into `environments.client.build` kept every public size and produced a different cycle that crashed the laptop Worker the same way.
- rule: when e2e or preview answers 500 at module load and the laptop build boots, download the run's `build-output` (`gh run download <run> -n build-output -D <dir>`) and look for a cycle among `server/_ssr/*.mjs` imports before reading any route code. The measured fix is one line in `vite.config.ts`, `rolldownConfig: { output: { strictExecutionOrder: true } }` in the `nitro({ ... })` options, which wraps modules so execution order holds whatever the grouping. That file is outside B7 g1's files, so it waits for an orchestrator ruling (see the B7 log, g1 step 7 block).
- proof: on slice/b7 at 61dacc8, a cycle scan of CI run 37699949767's `build-output` (a 40-line Tarjan walk over `^import ... from "./..."` in `server/**/*.mjs`) printed `_ssr\DQNJrwJb22.mjs <-> _ssr\CLEmPZIM.mjs <-> _ssr\DQNJrwJb2.mjs`, and the same scan of slice/b16's run 37699933243 printed `0 cycles`. On the laptop, `export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1; export VITE_API_BASE_URL=/api/public; export VITE_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY=1x00000000000000000000AA; bun run build` with the group moved to `environments.client.build` gave `1 cycles` and `wrangler dev --port 8948` answered `/` 500 with the same TypeError; with the Nitro line added the scan said `0 cycles` and `/`, `/admin/sign-in` and `/california` answered 200. With H62's config as on main plus the Nitro line: `0 cycles`, `bundle-check: OK 24 routes under 163840 gzip bytes` (`_site.property.$slug` 154214, `_site` 146438, the same as without the line), `/` 200 (measured 2026-10-08 02:20 +0300). CI with the line: UNPROVEN.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2406 · A park's WIP commit can hold a watched-fail mutation in flight, and stopping a replay mid-entry leaves one behind
- symptom: B7 g1 was parked while a registry replay ran; the WIP commit b1a638b held `src/server/public/pipeline.ts` with entry b3-jj's `replace`, and the resumed tree showed that file modified against the commit. Later, stopping a local replay with `taskkill //T //F` left `src/server/submissions/service.ts` and `src/domain/contracts.ts` mutated.
- cause: `watchfail.mjs` writes the mutation into the working tree and restores it only after the entry's run ends; a commit of the tree, or a kill of the process, in between keeps the mutated text.
- rule: a resumed builder first runs `git status --short` and compares each modified or committed file of the WIP with the registry (`find` present once, `replace` absent: a scan over `tests/mutations/*.json`); after stopping a replay, `git status --short` again and restore the mutated file from `HEAD` when no other work is uncommitted. Never commit while a replay runs in the same tree.
- proof: `git -C D:/mop-build/admin show b1a638b:app/src/server/public/pipeline.ts | grep -cF "...[{ bucket:"` → `1` (the mutation), and the same at `61dacc8` → `0` (restored; measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-539 · `watchfail --changed origin/main` skipped a branch's own new registry entry once a merge of main made its target file equal to main's; the entry was stale and only the reviewer saw it
- symptom: 2026-10-08 04:00, B11 step 7 (review af38d8a4): after `git merge origin/main`, `tests/unit/admin-routes-parity.test.ts` on slice/b11 equalled main's, so `--changed origin/main` listed no diff for it and never selected the branch's new entry `b11-g6-routes-pending-stale`, whose `find` still named the pre-merge list end (`"automation.templates_send_test",
];` against `"reports.email",
];`). The author reported `28 replayed, 0 stale`; CI's mutation step would have exited 2 on the next branch to touch the file.
- cause: `--changed` selected by file diff only; an entry is also made stale by main moving its target, and after the merge the branch no longer differs on that file.
- rule: `--changed <ref>` now also selects every entry the registry gained or changed since `<ref>` (`registryAt()` in `scripts/watchfail.mjs` reads each registry file at `<ref>` with `git show`). Keep running it from `app/` before every push (P-537); after a merge of main it covers the group's own entries without `--only`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/watchfail.test.ts -t "P-539"` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK A:three` selected with no target file changed; with the `|| addedSinceRef` term removed the case goes red (`- "WATCHED-FAIL OK A:three"`), measured 2026-10-08.
- added: 2026-10-08
- enforced-by: `tests/unit/watchfail.test.ts` ("--changed <ref> also replays an entry the registry gained since <ref>")

## P-540 · `quiet.mjs -- bun run check | tail -1 && git commit ...` commits and pushes on a red check: the pipeline exit is tail's, not the check's
- symptom: 2026-10-08 05:20, the watchfail PR (226) was pushed with its check having printed `quiet: exit 1`; the chain went on because `| tail -1` ended the pipeline with 0. The same check passed on the next run (load), so the red line's content is UNPROVEN.
- cause: a pipeline's status is its last command's; `&&` after `| tail` tests tail.
- rule: never pipe a gate before `&&`: run `node ../workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- bun run check` on its own line and test `$?`, or `set -o pipefail` first; the gate's exit decides the push, not its last line.
- proof: `bash -c 'false | tail -1 && echo pushed'` prints `pushed`; with `set -o pipefail` it prints nothing.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08 09:40, orchestrator: the same shape twice more in one hour (`bun run migrations:check 2>&1 | tail -1 && git commit`): the b9 restamp was pushed while the check printed exit 1 (it passed on the committed tree, so no harm, but the push did not wait for the proof).

## P-2305 · A merge agent chased a moving main: three merges of origin/main in twenty minutes, each restarting CI, because the gate refused "rebase first" for every records commit
- symptom: `merge-gate.mjs 185` printed `rebase first` three times; each answer was a merge of origin/main, a push and a 7 minute CI run, and main had moved again by the time the checks were green.
- cause: other lanes merge records pull requests (hygiene cap, merge-chores.md, a ruling) into main every few minutes, and the gate required the head to contain origin/main whatever main had gained.
- rule: when the gate says `rebase first`, merge origin/main and push once, wait for green, and run the gate at once; since ruling H65 a head behind main by documents only passes the gate, so a second round happens only when main gained code. Never wait on a clock between the green checks and the gate.
- proof: `grep -c "behind main by documents only" workspace/05-plans/merge-gate.mjs` → 1; PR 185 merged at ec1b4f0 after the third merge, the fourth main advance being documents only.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2306 · B6 g2: three plan lines met a gate that already stood (a server file reading src/data, a schema reading the clock, a state type without void)
- symptom: `bun run check` would have failed three ways on the plan text as written: `pricing.ts` imports `src/data/exposure.ts` and `tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` bans every `src/data` import from `src/server`; `markPaidInput` "refuses a future paid_at" but `src/domain/**` may not call `Date.now()` or `new Date()` (R29, eslint `WALL_CLOCK`); `void` in the state-machine test does not typecheck while `workflow.ts` types `PaymentStatus` without `void`. Knip also refuses an export only a later group imports (`PreparedPayment`).

- rule: `boundaries.test.ts` allows `src/server/payments/pricing.ts` to read `src/data/exposure` and nothing else; a domain schema takes `now` as an argument (`paidAtIsFuture(paidAt, now)`, the service passes its clock) instead of reading the wall clock; widen `PaymentStatus` in `workflow.ts` when the enum gains a value; an export no file imports yet is file-local until the step that imports it.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts tests/unit/payments/domain.test.ts tests/unit/state-machine.test.ts` → all pass; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b6-g2-price-reader` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B6:b6-g2-price-reader`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2307 · A keyset list over a view cannot page with PostgREST `.or()`: R44's lint refuses the built filter string, and a nullable sort column drops rows
- symptom: B6 step 3 says `listPayments` reads the view `invoice_list` "with keyset paging on (issued_at desc, id)". The first version paged with `.or(` and a template literal holding the cursor; `bunx eslint` refused it (`R44: free text goes through an RPC parameter, never a built filter string`), and `issued_at` is null for every waiver recorded without an invoice (`record_waiver`), so a plain `lt` on it would never reach those rows. One rewrite, about 15 minutes.
- cause: a composite keyset needs `or=` in PostgREST, and the `FILTER_STRING` selector in `eslint.config.js` bans a template literal or concatenation inside `.or()`, `.filter()` and `.textSearch()`. B7's submissions list avoids it with an RPC (`list_submissions` and its `p_after_*` parameters); the plan line for payments did not say which.
- rule: page a view with AND-only queries, each ordered and limited to `limit + 1`: the cursor's ties (`.eq(col, at).lt("id", id)`), then older rows (`.lt(col, at)`), then the null section (`.is(col, null)`) only while the page is short; a cursor inside the null section reads `.is(col, null).lt("id", id)`. Or add an RPC with keyset parameters. Never move the string into a variable to slip past the selector.
- proof: `cd app && bunx eslint --max-warnings 0 src/server/payments/service.ts` exits 0 and `git grep -c "[.]or(" -- src/server/payments/service.ts` prints nothing; `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/payments/service.test.ts -t "reads every row once"` passes, and `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b6-g3-keyset-older` prints `WATCHED-FAIL OK` (the case feeds each `next_cursor` back through a view stand-in that applies the filters; the first proof, `-t "answers one page"`, never fed a cursor back and could not fail, B6 g3 review).
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B6 g3 review: the shipped `CURSOR` regex had lost every backslash (`d{4}-dd-ddT[d:.]+`), so every page after the first answered 422; the suite stayed green because no case fed `next_cursor` back. A keyset list gets a round-trip case that reads every row once across pages.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2308 · `supabase gen types` types every column a `returns table` function returns as non-null, so neither the service nor a stub can see the null SQL returns
- symptom: `activate_submission` returns a null `event_id` (and a null `copy_job_id` once B8's prune removed the job) on its idempotent second call, but `src/db/types.ts` types both `string`. A fake rpc answering `event_id: null` failed `tsc` (`Type 'null' is not assignable to type 'string'`), and a service reading the typed row would treat a null as a string. A few minutes.
- cause: the generator writes a plain type for each output column of a table function and never `| null` (the argument side is P-915).
- rule: a service parses a function's rows with its own Zod schema wherever SQL can return null (`z.string().nullable()`, as `activated` in `src/server/payments/service.ts`); a unit stub builds the typed row and then `Reflect.set(row, "event_id", null)` with a comment saying why. Never a cast.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n '"activate_submission"' -A3 src/db/types.ts` shows `"copy_job_id": string,"event_id": string`; `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/payments/service.test.ts -t "second activate"` passes.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2309 · A review run inside the live lane tree tests the group plus whatever the next builder has written, and its replays mutate files that builder is reading
- symptom: the B6 g2 review was pointed at `D:/mop-build/b6`, which is the live lane. `git status --short` was empty when it started and later listed ` M app/src/routeTree.gen.ts`, `?? app/src/server/payments/service.ts` and more (the g3 builder's uncommitted `permissions/payments.ts`, nine `api/admin` routes, a migration, `error-codes.ts`; mtimes 05:17 to 05:22, after the g2 commit at 05:11). A `bun run check` there tested g2 plus a half-written g3, and the watched-fail replays mutated `src/domain/payments.ts` and others while the builder read them.
- cause: P-838 covers commits added after the frozen group and P-2018 covers a replay racing `check`; neither covers a second writer of uncommitted files in the same tree. A review brief that names the lane path names a moving target.
- rule: review a frozen commit from a scratch copy, never from the live lane: `git archive <commit> | tar -x -C <empty scratch dir>`, `git init` there (`check-layout.mjs` calls `git rev-parse`), link `node_modules` by junction, and remove the junction (`rmdir`, not `rm -r`) before deleting the scratch folder, or a recursive delete empties the lane's `node_modules`. Never run a replay in a tree another worker writes (P-011).
- proof: `git archive HEAD app/package.json | tar -tf -` → `app/package.json` (the snapshot needs no checkout and does not touch the working tree); `git status --short` in the lane before and after a review stays what the builder left.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2310 · The generated `Args` type lists every uuid argument as `string`, so a script cannot hand `settings_put_invoice` the null system actor `write_audit` accepts
- symptom: B6 g4's `applyInvoiceSettings` has to pass `p_actor: null` (a script is the system: `write_audit` skips the role check for a null actor, and a zero uuid raises `forbidden` because `user_roles` has no such user); `src/db/types.ts` types `p_actor` as `string`, so `id: string | null` failed `tsc` and `null as unknown as string` fails `no-unsafe-type-assertion`. A few minutes.
- cause: the generator marks an argument nullable only when the function gives it a default; `settings_put_invoice(p_value, p_actor, p_actor_kind, p_request_id, p_note)` has none (the argument side of P-915, the return side of P-2308).
- rule: one helper with one `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-type-assertion -- <reason>` (R03), `actorArg` in `src/server/payments/invoice-settings.ts`, never a zero uuid and never a spread of a widened object; a function that should take the system actor gets `p_actor uuid default null` in its migration instead, where the migration is yours.
- proof: `grep -n "p_actor" supabase/sql/functions/write_audit.sql | head -3` shows `if p_actor is not null then`; `grep -n '"settings_put_invoice"' -A2 src/db/types.ts` shows `"p_actor": string`; `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/payments/invoice-settings.test.ts -t "once with the validated value"` passes with `p_actor: null` in the asserted call.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2311 · The session scratchpad folder is shared by every agent running in this Claude session: another lane overwrote a script there
- symptom: B6 g4 wrote `add-entries.mjs` (eight registry entries for `B6.json`) to its scratchpad folder, ran it, and later the harness reported the file changed on disk: it held another lane's B11 registry script (`tests/mutations/B11.json`). Nothing was lost because the script had already run; a script run a second time would have written another slice's entries. A few minutes.
- cause: the scratchpad path named in the environment block is per session, not per agent, and lanes of one workflow share the session.
- rule: a scratch file that is run more than once, or that names a registry or log of your slice, gets the slice and group in its file name (`b6-g4-add-entries.mjs`), or lives in the lane tree under a git-ignored name that you delete before the commit; never trust an older file in the scratchpad to be yours.
- proof: `head -3 "$SCRATCHPAD/add-entries.mjs"` in the B6 g4 session printed `tests/mutations/B11.json`, not `B6.json`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2312 · B6 g5: three lines of the plan did not match the code or the standards they build on
- symptom: step 5 puts `localInvoiceStore(dir)`, which imports `node:fs`, into `invoice-pdf.ts`, a file the Deno job runner loads, and R07 forbids `node:*` there: it was written, then taken out again (the smoke script writes its `--out` file itself, the tests use a map). Step 5 also calls `issueInvoiceCore(db, input, actor)` exported with a `{ id, kind, note }` actor, but g3 wrote it file-local as `(db, raw, audit: AuditArgs)`. And the plan says the snapshot freezes `billing_email`, but `buildInvoiceSnapshot` did not write it, so the PDF could not name the billing address (E19).
- cause: the lines of a step quote what earlier steps would give, and nobody re-read the earlier code against them; R07 is a standard, not a line of step 5.
- rule: before building on a quoted line, open the file it names (one `grep -n "<symbol>" <file>`); keep a helper that needs `node:*` in `scripts/`; and give a new snapshot field a test that parses the builder's output with the schema the PDF layout reads (`invoiceSnapshotSchema`), so builder and layout cannot drift apart.
- proof: `grep -n "node:" app/src/server/payments/invoice-pdf.ts` → no hits; `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/payments/service.test.ts -t "what the PDF layout parses"` passes and goes red when `billing_email` is dropped from `invoice-snapshot.ts` (`b6-g5-snapshot-billing-email`).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2313 · A Worker route that imports a module with a static `import "pdf-lib"` puts the library (618 KB minified) into the Worker's startup graph
- symptom: `service.ts` (`getPdf`) imports `invoiceSignedUrl` from `invoice-pdf.ts`, which imported `pdf-lib` statically: after `bun run build` the Worker held `_libs/pdf-lib+tslib.mjs` (618,352 bytes) and loaded it on every cold start, to sign a 60-second link.
- cause: the plan keeps `invoiceSignedUrl`, the bucket constant and the renderer in one file, and the bundler follows static imports.
- rule: `pdf-lib` is loaded where a PDF is made, with `await import("pdf-lib")` (`newInvoiceDocument` in `invoice-layout.ts`, `renderInvoicePdf`), and imported as a type only at the top of a file; the Deno runner resolves the same dynamic import through `deno.json`.
- proof: `cd app && bun run build && grep -c "pdf-lib" .output/server/index.mjs` → `0`, and `grep -rho 'import("[^"]*pdf-lib[^"]*")' .output/server` finds the one lazy chunk; `deno check --config supabase/functions/job-runner/deno.json supabase/functions/job-runner/index.ts` exits 0.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2314 · After main is merged into a lane, `bun run check` fails on two things the merge itself does not show: an older `action_roles` migration and a newest one that lacks the lane's actions
- symptom: B6 g5 merged origin/main (B7 people, B11) and `bun run check` went red three checks late: `migrations:check` said `rename supabase/migrations/20261007021713_action_roles.sql to a timestamp after 20261007035723`, and after `bun run migrations:restamp` the sync test said `expected [ …(91) ] to deeply equal [ …(94) ]` (the newest `action_roles` file held 91 of the 94 actions of the merged matrix). `migrations:check` also kept reading the old name until the rename was committed, because it diffs commits, not the working tree.
- cause: `permissions/index.ts` now lists main's groups and the lane's, but each lane's `action_roles` file holds only the actions it knew; `action-roles.sync.test.ts` reads the newest file only.
- rule: right after the merge commit run `bun run migrations:check`, `bun run migrations:restamp` when it asks, commit the rename, then `bun run scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs` (rows are only upserted, so a second file is safe) and commit that before the first `bun run check`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/action-roles.sync.test.ts` → `2 passed` after the generator; `ls supabase/migrations | grep action_roles | tail -3` lists the lane's two files after main's.
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B6 g3: the merge of main (B10 channels, reports) left the lane's newest `action_roles` file without those actions; `bun run scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs` wrote `20261008040840_action_roles.sql` and `action-roles.sync.test.ts` went green.

## P-2315 · `scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs` has no dry run and ignores every flag: `--check` wrote a new migration into a read-only review
- symptom: a reviewer ran `bun run scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs --check` to see whether the file was in sync. It printed `wrote supabase/migrations/20261007043422_action_roles.sql 91 actions` and `git status` showed `?? supabase/migrations/20261007043422_action_roles.sql`: a read-only check had added a migration to the snapshot, which was deleted by hand.
- cause: the script never reads `process.argv`; every run writes a new stamped file with all actions. The read-only check is a test, not a flag.
- rule: never pass a flag to `gen-action-roles.mjs` and never run it to look. To check sync run `bunx vitest run tests/unit/action-roles.sync.test.ts`; run the generator only to write the file you mean to commit (P-2314).
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "process.argv" scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs` → `0`; `bunx vitest run tests/unit/action-roles.sync.test.ts` → `2 passed`, and `git status --short supabase/migrations` prints nothing afterwards.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2316 · The first `bun run check` of a group goes red at `format:check` on its own new files, after six gates have passed
- symptom: B6 g3's first `bun run check` ended at `format:check` (prettier) on new files of the group, after layout, typecheck, lint, knip, jscpd and stubs had passed.
- cause: `check` runs `format:check` late and only reports; nothing formats the files while they are written, and a file written with Write or Edit has the author's wrapping, not prettier's. A registry `find` copied before formatting then goes stale too (P-066, P-415).
- rule: run `bunx prettier --config .prettierrc --write <the files the group added or changed>` from `app/` before the first `bun run check`, then write registry `find` strings from the formatted file. Never run `bun run format` on the whole tree in a lane: it rewrites files the group does not own.
- proof: `cd app && bunx prettier --config .prettierrc --check src/server/payments/service.ts tests/unit/payments/service.test.ts` → `All matched files use Prettier code style!`; `grep -n "^format:check\|\"format:check\"" package.json` shows the gate that fails otherwise.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2317 · `npx tsc` outside a folder with the project's own TypeScript installs a different npm package named `tsc`
- symptom: B6 g4 ran `npx tsc --noEmit` to typecheck one file; npx fetched the package named `tsc` from the registry and printed a notice that it is not the compiler instead of type errors. A few minutes.
- cause: the npm package `tsc` is a deprecated stub, not the TypeScript compiler (that is `typescript`, whose binary is `tsc`). `npx tsc` reaches the real binary only when `node_modules/.bin/tsc` exists in the folder it runs from; from the tree root there is none.
- rule: typecheck with `bun run typecheck` from `app/` (it runs both tsconfigs); for one config use `bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` from `app/`. Never `npx tsc`.
- proof: `npm view tsc description` → `A deprecated release of the TypeScript compiler`; `cd app && grep -n '"typecheck"' package.json` → `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.scripts.json`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2318 · A step that replaces an earlier group's `STUB(...)` edits that group's tests and registry entries too, and the plan does not name them
- symptom: B6 g4 removed g3's `STUB(B6 step 4)` (`missingForInvoice` in `invoice-snapshot.ts`). The real list names `payment_methods.instructions` where the stub said `payment_methods`, so g3's `service.test.ts` case asserting the issue paths went red, and the registry entry `b6-g3-ready-late-terms` pointed at a line that had moved to `invoice-settings.ts`, a file the g4 plan text does not list. About ten minutes.
- cause: a stub is the earlier group's code under the earlier group's tests; the later step owns the real behaviour but the plan names only its new files. Every test and mutation that touched the stub is part of the replacement.
- rule: before replacing a `STUB(...)`, run `grep -rn "<stub name>" src tests scripts` and `grep -n "<stub file>" tests/mutations/*.json`; change the matching expectations and `find` strings in the same commit, replay the earlier group's affected entries (`--only <id>`), and name the files in the log as g4 did.
- proof: `grep -rn "STUB(B6 step 4)" app/src app/scripts` prints nothing; `grep -n "b6-g3-ready-late-terms" -A3 app/tests/mutations/B6.json | grep file` → `src/server/payments/invoice-settings.ts`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2319 · `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` replays the whole slice's diff since the merge base: 135 entries, over eight minutes
- symptom: g6 touched one layout file and three registry entries, ran the step (c) replay with `--changed origin/main`, and the run replayed 134 entries of B6, B7, B11 and others for more than 500 seconds (the Bash call moved to the background); `--only a,b,c` answered `no entry with id a,b,c`. One entry, B2:f-matrix, ended bad, which looks like a regression and is not.
- cause: `--changed <ref>` diffs from `merge-base(<ref>, HEAD)` (35dfdc56 for this lane), so it selects every entry on every file the slice changed since then: 135 here, 92 of B6 and 43 of other slices on files B6 edited. Merging main does not grow that set. `--only` takes one exact id. B2:f-matrix is a `--project db` entry (B6 g2 added `void` to `PaymentStatus` in `src/domain/workflow.ts`); a unit shell without the dev profile refuses at global-setup (`refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set`), so it goes bad for the environment.
- rule: for your own new entries run one `--only <id>` call each in a single command line (`for id in ...; do node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only "$id"; done`); `--changed` is the one replay that catches a cross-slice regression on a shared file, so run it once before the slice closes in a free window, in the background, and read a bad `db`-project entry as a missing dev profile until it fails under `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"`.
- proof: `cd app && for id in b6-g6-baseline b6-g6-label-weight b6-g6-two-inks; do node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only "$id" | tail -1; done` → three `replayed 1: ok 1, bad 0, stale 0` lines; `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only f-matrix | tail -1` in a shell without the dev profile → `replayed 1: ok 0, bad 1, stale 0` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2320 · No PDF rasteriser on this laptop, and `bun` plus Playwright hangs: the eye check of a PDF is the layout runs drawn in Chromium by `node`
- symptom: g6's design review needs to see `out/invoice.pdf`; `pdftoppm`, `mutool`, `gs` and ImageMagick are not installed, headless Chromium does not show PDFs, and a bun script that imported `playwright` ran past 120 seconds with no output.
- cause: nothing here converts a PDF to pixels; bun's loader and Playwright's browser launch do not finish together on this laptop (cause not isolated).
- rule: dump `layoutInvoice(snapshot)` to JSON with a bun script, and draw those runs as absolutely positioned text in a 612 x 792 page with a plain `node` Playwright script (Times New Roman and Arial stand in for the standard fonts, same metrics); say in the log that the picture is a stand-in for the PDF, and that the real `out/invoice.pdf` still needs one look once it exists on mop-dev.
- proof: `for t in pdftoppm mutool gs magick; do command -v $t; done; echo end` → only `end` (no rasteriser); `cd app && node --input-type=module -e "import('playwright').then(m=>console.log(typeof m.chromium.launch))"` → `function` (node loads Playwright; the hang is bun's, so the same import under `bun -e` is the one that does not return).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2321 · A browser mirror of a server Zod schema is a `jscpd` clone, and so is a test fixture copied from a sibling component test: the schema goes to `src/domain`, the fixture gets its own values
- symptom: B6 step 7's first `bun run check` stopped at `jscpd` with six clones: the invoice snapshot schema in `src/admin/invoices/payments-api.ts` against `src/server/payments/invoice-layout.ts` (9 and 14 lines, 84 and 95 tokens), and the request fixture, the `me` helper and the `mount` helper of `InvoiceDetail.test.tsx` against `RequestDetail.test.tsx` and `people.test.tsx` (111, 75, 71 tokens). Typecheck and lint had passed, so the first red came late.
- cause: `src/admin` may not import `src/server` (R06, `admin-boundaries.test.ts`), so the browser needed its own parse of the same answer, and `.jscpd.json` has `minTokens 70` and `threshold 0` (R04); the tests copied the fixtures they sit beside.
- rule: a response shape both sides read lives once in `src/domain/payments.ts` (here `invoiceSnapshotSchema`, `invoiceListRowSchema`, `paymentStatuses`) and the server file imports it (`invoice-layout.ts` re-exports it for its older importers). A component test builds its fixture with its own values and its own key order, never a paste of a neighbour's; run `bun run jscpd` (4 seconds) before the long `check`.
- proof: `cd app && bun run jscpd` → `Found 0 clones.` on slice/b6 after the move (2026-10-07); with the schema pasted back into `payments-api.ts` it prints two clones against `invoice-layout.ts`.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B6 c3h round 3: after `git merge origin/main` brought B7's `src/admin/properties/properties.test.tsx`, `bun run jscpd` reported one clone between its `serve` fetch stub and the one in `InvoiceDetail.test.tsx`. The hand-in renamed the local `key` to `route` (three lines), which breaks the token match without removing the duplicate: the same stub is now written in `InvoiceDetail.test.tsx`, `properties.test.tsx` and `RequestDetail.test.tsx`. The hand-in's cost line named P-537, which covers stale registry anchors only. The right fix is one shared helper under `tests/fixtures`; until it exists the rename is a recorded exception (B6-followups.md, c3h).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2322 · B6 step 7: five lines of the brief met a tree that already differed (route options helper, `?state=`, a settings read, `box-shadow`, sheet order)
- symptom: the brief says each route is "built with B7's shared route options helper"; `admin-route-shells.test.ts` (ruling H66) allows only the router, `pageHead` and a stylesheet address as static imports of a route file, so every screen is a shell plus a `.lazy.tsx` page and `adminRouteOptions()` is not used. The brief says the picker reads `?state=Accepted`; the list input names it `workflow_state`. Screen 6's form needs the readiness list and the payment methods, and no route reads `settings.invoice` before screen 24: the list comes from the message of the 409 `invoice_not_ready` (`missingSettings`), and the preferred method is a text field of the method's id. The plan wants "no shadows" in print, and `admin-motion.test.ts` bans the word `box-shadow` in any admin sheet, so `box-shadow: none` cannot be written (the print test asserts the sheet holds no shadow). The same test wants the imports of `index.css` in alphabetical order, so `invoices.css` goes after `admin.css`.
- cause: the plan lines were written before H66 and B7's list input, and no screen-24 read exists yet.
- rule: follow the shell pattern of `people.index.tsx` and its `.lazy.tsx`, read the list input in `src/domain/admin-submissions.ts` before naming a filter, treat a missing read as a follow-up (a select of methods once `settings.get` is built) and not as a hard-coded list, and keep admin sheets free of the word `shadow`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/admin-route-shells.test.ts tests/unit/admin-motion.test.ts` passes on slice/b6; `grep -n "workflow_state" src/domain/admin-submissions.ts` → the filter's real name.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2323 · A live admin spec on mop-dev needs `CSRF_SECRET` in the shell and the lane's `action_roles` migration pushed: without them every admin write is a 503 or a 403
- symptom: (since ruling H70 the spec skips without `E2E_FULL_STACK=1`, so reproduce with that variable set) B6 step 9's spec reached the "Issue and email" confirmation and the dialog answered `Saving is unavailable at the moment. Please try again later.` (503 `csrf_secret_missing`); with the secret exported it answered `This change could not be made.` (403 `forbidden`, body `{"error":{"code":"forbidden",...}}` read from the trace's resource file). Each run is a minute of `vite dev` plus the fixture setup.
- cause: `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` exports the six dev names and not `CSRF_SECRET`, and the dev server inherits the shell, so `verifyCsrf` has no key. The 403 is `write_audit` (DB-04): `public.action_roles` on mop-dev has no `payments.*` row until main pushes the lane's `action_roles` migration (`select action from action_roles where action like 'payments.%'` returns no row), and a lane may not push it (ruling H57).
- rule: before a live admin e2e export the key without printing it, `export CSRF_SECRET="$(grep '^CSRF_SECRET=' ../.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r')"`, and read an admin write answer from the trace (`trace.zip`, `resources/*.json`), not from the dialog's calm copy; a write that answers 403 on a fresh action is the unpushed `action_roles` migration, so the proof is UNPROVEN until main pushes it.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev | grep -c CSRF_SECRET` → `0`, and `grep -n "csrf_secret_missing" src/server/lib/csrf.ts` → the 503 branch; the two answers were measured 2026-10-07 on mop-dev with `E2E_FULL_STACK=1 E2E_TARGET=dev E2E_PORT=8978 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts`.
- added: 2026-10-07

- hit again: 2026-10-08, B6 g3: the rule line was first written through the Bash tool and lost its backslash (P-008), so the printed command held a real line break instead of the two characters backslash and r; a reviewer found it. The repair note itself then wrote a real carriage return into GOTCHAS.md, the file went mixed-eol and `git diff` showed 9725 lines (P-2328); a script that read and wrote the file as latin1 removed the carriage returns and restored the rule line.

## P-2324 · A committing e2e spec calls `assertNotProduction()` first in `beforeAll`, before the lock and before its first write; B6's spec had no call and a reviewer caught it
- symptom: `tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts` took the G34 lock and rewrote `settings.site.legal` and `settings.invoice` at once, committed four submissions, issued and voided invoice numbers and rewound `invoice_counters`, with no production guard; `grep -c assertNotProduction app/tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts` printed `0` while `live-forms.spec.ts` and `coming-soon.spec.ts` carry the call.
- cause: `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts` checks only when `E2E_DATASET=1`, and the plan's proof line for a spec does not set it, so the spec's own `beforeAll` is the only guard that runs after the launch switch (ruling H35 (5)); nothing tests that a committing spec holds the call (the `guardedScripts` case of `assert-not-production.test.ts` reads `scripts/`, not `tests/e2e/`).
- rule: the first line of a committing spec's `beforeAll` is `await assertNotProduction();` (import from `../../scripts/lib/assert-not-production.mjs`), then `holdDevLock()`; a spec that only reads needs neither.
- proof: `cd app && grep -L assertNotProduction $(grep -l "holdDevLock" tests/e2e/*.spec.ts)` → no file (measured 2026-10-08 after the fix).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2325 · `email_messages.entity_id` holds the recipient's entity, not the event's: the invoice mail is about the submission, so a test looks it up by the request id
- symptom: the `E2E_RESEND=1` check of B6 step 9 polled `email_messages` by `entity_id = <payment id>` and could never find the row (it would have timed out after 180 s on every run); found by a reviewer reading, the check had never run.
- cause: `send_email` writes `recipient.entity` and `recipient.entityId` (`src/server/jobs/steps/send-email.ts`), and for the `invoice` key the recipient is `submitter`, whose `submitterRecipient` answers `entity: "submission"` and `entityId: submission.id` (`src/server/email/variables.ts`), because the `invoice.issued` payload carries `submission_id`.
- rule: look a mail up by `entity = 'submission' and entity_id = <request id>` (or through `jobs.event_id` as `scripts/invoice-smoke.ts` does), never by the payment id; an assertion that has never run once is written against the code that fills the row, not against the column name.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "entityId: submission.id" src/server/email/variables.ts` → the `submitterRecipient` line; `grep -n "entity = 'submission'" tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts` → the lookup.
- added: 2026-10-08

## G-1050 · The admin `Dialog` has no portal: a dialog form rendered inside a `<form>` nests, and its submit bubbles into the outer form
- paths: app/src/admin/invoices/**, app/src/admin/ui/Dialog.tsx
- severity: warn
- symptom: B6 g2 recorded "Waive without invoice" and the "Issue and email this invoice" confirmation opened with it (a reviewer probe: `{"before":false,"after":true,"nested":1}`), React printed `<form> cannot contain a nested <form>`. A refused waiver left both dialogs open; the Issue confirmation could have numbered and emailed an invoice the waiver was meant to avoid (invariant 12).
- cause: `InvoiceForm` rendered its `children` (the waive dialog, itself a `<form>`) inside its own `<form>`; the submit event of the inner form bubbled to the outer `onSubmit`, which opened the confirmation without checking `ready`. The test that the two buttons share a parent locked the nesting in.
- rule: render a dialog, and anything with its own form, as a sibling of a form, never inside one; tie a button outside the form to it with `form={id}` (`useId`); a form's `onSubmit` refuses when the form is not ready. A layout test asserts no `<form>` has a `<form>` ancestor.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run src/admin/invoices/InvoiceDetail.test.tsx -t "keeps the Waive dialog's form out of the Issue form"` → 1 passed; with the registry entry `b6-s7-form-nested` applied it is red.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2326 · A throwaway component probe belongs inside the tree, not in a scratch config outside it
- symptom: a reviewer's probe test run from outside the worktree failed with `Failed to resolve import "react/jsx-dev-runtime"`; `review-snapshot.mjs create` ran past the 120 s foreground limit and had to be moved to the background.
