- cause: the tree's `vitest.config.ts` resolves React and the JSX runtime from the app's own `node_modules`; a config outside it sees neither, so it needs `root` and aliases for `react/jsx-dev-runtime` and `react/jsx-runtime`. The snapshot copies the tree and takes longer than the foreground limit.
- rule: put the probe as a temporary `*.probe.test.tsx` next to the component inside the app and run it with the tree's own config (`bunx vitest run <file>`), then delete it before committing; start `review-snapshot.mjs create` with `run_in_background`.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run src/admin/invoices/InvoicesTable.test.tsx` → passes with no extra config, JSX runtime resolved.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2327 · Python's `open(path, "w")` on Windows writes CRLF into an LF file; the mutation registry then reports every multi-line `find` as stale
- symptom: after a Python patch script edited `InvoiceForm.tsx`, `invoices.css` and `tests/mutations/B6.json`, `watchfail --registry --changed` printed `STALE ... find occurs 0 times` for entries whose text was untouched, and git warned `CRLF will be replaced by LF`.
- cause: the files were LF (G-008); Python's text mode translated `\n` to `\r\n` on write. A registry `find` with `\n` no longer matched.
- rule: patch with Edit, or open with `newline=""` / write bytes; after any script edit run `file <path>` and `sed -i 's/\r$//'` if it says CRLF, then replay the registry.
- proof: `git ls-files --eol app/src/admin/invoices/InvoiceForm.tsx` → `i/lf w/lf`; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` from `app` prints `stale 0`.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 c459: a new migration written with the Write tool arrived as CRLF (`git ls-files --eol` read `w/crlf`); `grep -c` of a carriage return answered 0 (P-057), so only `git ls-files --eol` showed it, after `git add` had printed the CRLF warning. A registry `sql` entry that embeds the file would have carried the carriage returns into the replay; `sed -i` on the file and a rewrite of the entries fixed both.

## P-2328 · A bank note that quotes a carriage return must say "backslash r", never contain one: GOTCHAS.md went mixed-eol and `git diff` showed 9725 lines
- symptom: after the P-2323 rule line lost its backslash (P-008), the repair note written into GOTCHAS.md held a real carriage return; `git ls-files --eol GOTCHAS.md` read `w/mixed` and `git diff --stat` listed the whole file (9725 lines) as changed.
- cause: the note's text was written with the real byte; one carriage return in a file whose other lines end in LF is enough for `git ls-files --eol` to report mixed endings. Taken from the reviewer's account of the B6 g3 hand-in; the exact tool that wrote the byte is UNPROVEN.
- rule: describe an escape in words (backslash and r, the two characters), never type it; after any edit of GOTCHAS.md run `git ls-files --eol GOTCHAS.md` and expect `w/lf`; repair a mixed file by reading and writing it as latin1 with the carriage returns removed, then `git diff --stat` must show only the lines you meant.
- proof: `git ls-files --eol GOTCHAS.md` → `i/lf    w/lf` (measured 2026-10-08, B6 c3h).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2329 · A registry entry for a describe-level env guard: run the mutant where the stack is missing, because that is the case the guard exists for
- symptom: B6 c3h had to see `test.skip(!process.env["E2E_FULL_STACK"], ...)` of `admin-invoice.spec.ts` go red. With the guard removed and the whole stack present the seven serial tests run for minutes and may even pass once the runner and B7 step 7 are deployed, so a mutant of the guard would go stale ("stayed green") the day the stack is complete; the status-set mutant of the seventh test cannot run at all while test 1 fails first.
- cause: a skip guard is red only when the code under it cannot run, and the serial tests share `paymentId`, so no single test can be selected with `-g` to isolate it.
- rule: the replay line blanks the first variable the spec needs (`DEV_DB_URL=` as a leading assignment, which `watchfail.mjs` passes to the child), so the mutant fails in `beforeAll` with `refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set`, the situation of CI's admin step; unmutated, the same command prints `7 skipped` and exits 0. A mutant that needs the full stack is a `kind: manual` entry with its replay command and the dependency named in `what`, and the log says UNPROVEN. The guard entry itself is `kind: manual` too (corrected 2026-10-08, c3h round 3): its replay starts Playwright's webServer, which CI's db job does not have, and an entry without `kind` is replayed there (P-1908).
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile loaded, the single-entry form with the registry entry's `file`, `find`, `replace`, `run` and `expect` (`--only` skips a manual entry) → `WATCHED-FAIL OK`; `bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-invoice.spec.ts --reporter=line` without `E2E_FULL_STACK` → `7 skipped`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2137 · A bank rule that names a response header goes false when a later step changes the header, and the next worker writes the assertion that turns e2e red
- symptom: P-1917's rule told a test to assert that `/?preview=<x>` answers no `x-mop-cache`. B7 step 7a made that request answer `x-mop-cache: bypass` (P-2024); a worker who followed the rule would write the assertion that failed `tests/e2e/essentials.spec.ts:155` in CI (P-2025). The B7 g3 review found the rule still standing.
- cause: P-2024 and P-2025 recorded the new behaviour and left the older entry's rule unchanged; nothing checks a rule's claim against the code, and the check script only reads entry structure.
- rule: the step that changes a header, status or other behaviour a bank entry states as a rule searches the bank for the old behaviour (`grep -n "<header name>" GOTCHAS.md`) and corrects each rule it finds in the same commit, naming the entry that explains the change.
- proof: `grep -c "neverCached[`]: no [`]x-mop-cache" GOTCHAS.md` → 0 (P-1917 now says "since B7 step 7a, `x-mop-cache: bypass`"); `grep -n "x-mop-cache.*toBe(.bypass.)" app/tests/e2e/essentials.spec.ts` → line 155 (measured 2026-10-08, B7 g3 follow-ups).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2501 · An axe scan taken while a dialog fades in reads the colours against the half-faded ground: red on CI, green on the laptop
- symptom: `admin-assets.spec.ts:258` (PR 211) and `admin-newsletter.spec.ts:135` (PR 227) failed in CI, retry included, with `axe: new violations on <route> approve dialog` (`color-contrast` on both dialog buttons); the same specs passed on the laptops.
- cause: `.admin-dialog[open]` animates opacity from 0 over 0.24 s and axe computes a colour with the element's opacity at that moment; a slower runner scans inside the window (measured with the fade stretched: opacity 0.0067, contrast 1.03 to 1.05).
- rule: an audit that reads computed style (axe, a contrast or overflow measure) first awaits the animations that end: `settleAnimations(page)` in `tests/e2e/fixtures/a11y.ts` (ruling H72); never skip the dialog, never baseline the violation, never edit the motion for it.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b17-a11y-settle-wait` -> `WATCHED-FAIL OK B17:b17-a11y-settle-wait` (2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2027 · bank-merge refuses a lane edit of an entry main did not touch: its lost-line check counts the lane's own rewrite as a line main lost
- symptom: the B7 merge into main at 5bfdf875 + origin/main 5bfdf875..6eda9a41+ stopped with `bank-merge: refused, nothing written` and `line lost: main P-1917: - rule: a test that claims "the HTML does not vary" ...`, while `P-008` was the only conflict it resolved.
- cause: the lane rewrote the rule line of P-1917 (step 7a, `x-mop-cache: bypass`); main still holds the base text of that line, so the git merge takes the lane's body cleanly, but `lostLines(theirsById, "main")` reports every main line absent from the result, including lines the lane changed against an unchanged base.
- rule: a main line that equals the base line and is absent from the result is a lane edit, not a loss; until `workspace/05-plans/bank-merge.mjs` skips such lines (a plan change, ruling needed), a merge-only run returns blocked with the helper's words, never resolves GOTCHAS.md by hand (P-525).
- proof: `git show 6eda9a41:GOTCHAS.md | awk '/^## P-1917/{f=1;next}/^## /{f=0}f' | grep '^- rule' | md5sum` equals the same command on `origin/main` -> same hash (main's line is the base's).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2028 · B7 step 8's smoke cleanup names "the values of variants" as media keys, and its `deleteObjects` reads the shell's `SUPABASE_URL`
- symptom: B7 g1 (step 8): the plan's Files line says the `upload --render` cleanup deletes `deleteObjects("media", [media_key, ...values of variants])` of `src/server/lib/media-store.ts`. Reading B9's code took the time: `property_media.variants` holds sizes (`{ "hero": { "w": 1600, "h": 1067 } }`), not keys, and `deleteObjects` builds its address from `readVar("SUPABASE_URL")`, the name G-901 says belongs to another business on this laptop unless the dev profile overwrote it.
- cause: the plan was written before B9 fixed the key layout: every rendition key is derived from the master, `v/<owner>/<n>-<sha8>/<size>.<ext>` (`variantKeys` in `scripts/variants.ts`, P-335).
- rule: a script that removes a stored photograph from the bucket `media` derives the keys with `variantKeys(owner, n, sha8)` from the master `o/<owner>/<n>-<sha8>.webp`, and removes them through `serviceClient()` (the dev profile's own names), never through `deleteObjects` from a laptop script.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "variantKeys\|serviceClient" scripts/admin-smoke.ts` → the import lines and the cleanup's `storage.storage.from("media").remove(storedKeys(mediaKey))`; `grep -n "const sizes" src/server/jobs/steps/render-variants.ts` → `z.record(z.string(), z.object({ w: z.number(), h: z.number() }))` (2026-10-08). The `--render` leg itself is UNPROVEN until B9's render_variants is deployed.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-731 · A brief that says a file "does not exist on main" can name a file the lane branch already holds: Write overwrote it
- symptom: B9 c5n's brief said `tests/unit/assets/templates.test.ts` does not exist on main; the builder wrote it with Write, the hook raised no refusal, and the 197-line SSR snapshot file of B9 g4 (Cover, Story, OgCard, carousel, 22 registry entries) was replaced until `git status` showed ` M` instead of `??`. `git checkout --` restored it and the new cases were appended.
- cause: the brief was written against main, and the lane branch carries earlier groups' commits (`7982a01` added the file); Write replaces a file it was not told to read.
- rule: before a Write of a file the brief calls new, run `git ls-files <path>` and `git log --oneline -1 -- <path>` on the lane branch; a tracked file is Read and edited, never written over.
- proof: `git log --oneline --diff-filter=A -1 -- app/tests/unit/assets/templates.test.ts` → `7982a016 B9 g4 steps 4,5: ...` (without `--diff-filter=A` the newest commit that touched the file prints, which is c5n's own)
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-732 · After a merge of main the lane's node_modules can be stale: `Cannot find package '@react-email/render'`
- symptom: B9 c5n's first `bunx vitest run` after `git merge origin/main` failed at import with `Cannot find package '@react-email/render'`; the package is in `app/package.json`, the lane's `node_modules` predates it.
- cause: a lane's `app/node_modules` is its own and is not refreshed by a merge, so a dependency another lane added to the lockfile is missing until it is installed.
- rule: after a merge that touches `app/package.json` or `app/bun.lock`, run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` in `app` before the first test; an import error for a package the manifest lists is this, not a code defect.
- proof: `cd app && bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun -e 'import("@react-email/render").then(() => console.log("ok"))'` → `ok` (measured 2026-10-07).
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B9 g1 step 10: the first `bun run build` after the merge failed with `Rolldown failed to resolve import "web-vitals" from "src/lib/web-vitals.ts"`; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` (`+ web-vitals@6.2.3`) fixed it. Run the install right after the start command's merge, before the first build.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-737 · A plan's "through `withRollback`" proof of a service that reads with the supabase-js query builder needs a `pg` adapter, and `table-stub.ts` had no `range` or count
- symptom: B9 step 10 asks `tests/db/assets-service.db.test.ts` to prove `listAssets` (`select(..., { count: "exact" })`, `.order`, `.range`), `approveAsset` and `rejectAsset` "through `withRollback`", and the unit test to page 60 rows; `market-opening.db.test.ts`'s `pgRpc` adapter answers only `rpc`, and `withTables` in `tests/fixtures/table-stub.ts` answered no `range`, no count and no `payload->data->>key` in `eq` or `in`.
- cause: `withRollback` holds one `pg` transaction; the service's supabase-js client is a second connection over PostgREST and cannot see its rows. The table stub was written for services that read with `eq`, `or` and `limit` only.
- rule: a db test of a service that uses `from()` passes an adapter over the test's own `pg` client (`pgDb` in `tests/db/assets-service.db.test.ts`: `rpc` as `select public.<fn>(name => $n)`, each statement under a savepoint, `Date` values turned back into ISO text as PostgREST answers them); a unit test of a paged list uses `withTables`, which now answers `range(from, to)` and `select(columns, { count })` and reads a JSON path in `eq` and `in`.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" && env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx vitest run --project db --testTimeout=60000 tests/db/assets-service.db.test.ts` → `Tests  5 passed (5)` (it printed `4 passed (4)` until the rework added the PostgREST case, P-738); `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/assets/service.test.ts -t "pages 60 rows"` passes and registry entry `b9g1-page-50` turns it red (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-738 · A proof that names a pass count goes stale the moment a rework adds a test case, and the review is the first to notice
- symptom: B9 g1's review re-ran the proof line of P-737 and read `Tests  5 passed (5)` where the entry promised `Tests  4 passed (4)`; the rework had added the PostgREST case `listAssets through PostgREST` (G-252) to `tests/db/assets-service.db.test.ts` and the entries written before it kept the old count.
- cause: a proof copies the number a command printed on the day it was written; nothing ties that number to the test file, so a later commit on the same file leaves the entry's expected output wrong while the code is right. A reader who sees a mismatch cannot tell a regression from a stale line.
- rule: when a rework adds or removes a case in a test file, grep the bank for the file name and re-run every proof that names it, correcting the count in the same commit; prefer a proof that names the case (`-t "<title>"` → `1 passed`) or says `0 failed` over one that depends on the size of the whole file.
- proof: `grep -n "assets-service.db.test.ts" GOTCHAS.md` → the P-737 proof reads `Tests  5 passed (5)`; from `app/` with the dev profile, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx vitest run --project db --testTimeout=60000 tests/db/assets-service.db.test.ts` → `Tests  5 passed (5)` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-743 · `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` on a long slice replays every group's entries, and a replay killed half way leaves its mutation in the file
- symptom: B9 g2's replay of its 20 new entries ran `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main`: it replayed the entries of g1 to g5 (31 done in 3 minutes, over 300 to go), and the first kill left `src/templates/social/NewsletterBlock.tsx` mutated (`git diff` showed `<td style={deck}></td>`). A second try, `--registry <scratchpad>/reg`, replayed other agents' B12 and B15 registries instead, because that scratchpad folder already existed from an earlier session, and one of its entries hung for 10 minutes on a mutated `src/server/jobs/steps/webhook-omnikom.ts`. About 25 minutes.
- cause: `--changed <ref>` selects the entries whose file differs on `<ref>...HEAD`, which on a slice branch is every earlier group's file, and it counts committed changes only, so a group's own uncommitted files are not selected before the commit. The session scratchpad is shared by every agent of the session, so `mkdir -p` on a common name finds foreign files.
- rule: replay a group's own entries from a registry folder made with `mktemp -d` under the scratchpad (`b9g2-only-$$`) holding a filtered copy of its entries; before and after any replay run `git status --short | grep -v '^??'` and restore a tracked file a killed replay left mutated with `git checkout -- <file>`; never kill a replay without that check.
- proof: `D=$(mktemp -d); node -e '...' ; node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry "$D"` → `watchfail: replayed 15: ok 15, bad 0, stale 0; manual 5 not replayed` for B9 g2 (measured 2026-10-08); `git status --short | grep -v '^??'` afterwards lists only the files the group changed.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-744 · A card button that changes state or starts a render sends on one click: the review rejected Approve and Re-render for C17
- symptom: B9 g2's first screen 10 had `Approve` and `Re-render` as plain buttons next to `Edit caption`. A click on Re-render ran `rerender_asset`, which marks the current revision `rejected` with the note `superseded` (an approved one too, with no way back, because `approve_asset` accepts only `pending`) and enqueues a heavy render for GitHub Actions. `RerenderAssetsButton` did the same for every current asset at once. The review rejected both.
- cause: STANDARDS C17 and `src/admin/ui/README.md` rule 4 say every destructive or outward action goes through `ConfirmDialog`; the first build used it for Reject only (which asks for a note) and wrote the other moves as in-place buttons, and no gate counts the dialogs of a screen.
- rule: a control that calls a write route which rejects, supersedes, approves, publishes or enqueues a job opens `ConfirmDialog` first, names what follows in one sentence taken from the SQL function (read it, do not guess), and its test asserts that nothing was sent before the confirm and nothing is sent on Cancel.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project component src/admin/assets src/admin/properties/RerenderAssetsButton.test.tsx` → `Tests  21 passed`; with `setOpen({ dialog: "rerender", asset });` replaced by `rerender.mutate([asset.id]);` in `AssetCards.tsx` the case "asks before it approves or re-renders" fails with `Unable to find an accessible element with the role "dialog" and name "Re-render cover, revision 1"` (registry entry `b9g2-confirm-rerender`).
- hit again: 2026-10-09, B7 g4 (screen 23): `Disable` (an account), `Remove` (a role) and `Send invitation` (Supabase Auth mails the person) sent on one click while the key revokes on the same screen used `ConfirmDialog`; the review rejected the group and cost one fix round. The rule reaches account and role writes and any button that makes an outside service send mail. Proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run src/admin/team/team.test.tsx` → `Tests  5 passed`; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b7-14-screen-disable-confirm` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-739 · The built Worker answers every admin write 503 on this laptop because `.dev.vars` has no `CSRF_SECRET`, and `.env` has none for `dev-vars.mjs` to copy
- symptom: B9 g2's first full run of `tests/e2e/admin-assets.spec.ts` passed the three read cases and failed "approving a pending card turns it to approved": the card stayed Pending for 30 s. The first reading was a database or approve-guard fault. The Playwright trace of the run showed `POST /api/admin/assets/<id>/approve 503` twice, with `Cache-Control: no-store` and no body kept.
- cause: `admin-signin.spec.ts` only reads, so no earlier admin spec on this worktree wrote through the built Worker. `scripts/dev-vars.mjs` lists `CSRF_SECRET` as optional and copies it only when `.env` holds it; this tree's `.env` has no such name, so `.dev.vars` had 8 keys and none was it. `csrf_secret_missing` is a 503 in `src/server/lib/error-codes.ts` (the cause is inferred from that table and from the fix, not from a kept response body).
- rule: before an e2e spec that writes through `/api/admin/*`, run `node scripts/dev-vars.mjs` with the dev profile loaded and then append a local random `CSRF_SECRET` to the git-ignored `app/.dev.vars` (`node -e` with `crypto.randomBytes(32).toString("base64url")`, never print it). A local value is enough: only the Worker under test reads it.
- proof: `awk -F= 'NF{print $1}' app/.dev.vars | grep -c '^CSRF_SECRET$'` → `1`, then `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8818 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-assets.spec.ts` (dev profile loaded) → `5 passed`; with the line removed the approve case fails as above (measured 2026-10-08, B9 g2).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-740 · A bulk PostgREST insert of rows with different keys sends null for the keys a row lacks, so a not-null column with a default fails 23502
- symptom: B9 g2's spec seeded five `assets` rows in one `db.from("assets").insert(rows)`; two rows had no `meta` or no `files`, and the insert answered `code 23502, Failing row contains (..., null, ...)`.
- cause: supabase-js sends the union of the keys as columns of one statement and fills a missing key with `null`, not with the column default; `assets.files` and `assets.meta` are `not null default`.
- rule: in a bulk insert give every row every not-null column it relies on a default for, or insert the rows in separate calls.
- proof: `grep -n "A bulk insert sends null" app/tests/e2e/admin-assets.spec.ts` → the comment above `base`; without `files: []` and `meta: {}` in `base` the `beforeAll` fails with `23502` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-741 · Plan line "no committed row survives the run" is false for an approve or a reject: `audit_log` is immutable, and the events are deletable only with `mop.retention`
- symptom: B9 step 11 says the spec's `afterAll` deletes the assets and the property in one `pg` transaction "so no committed row survives the run". The spec also approves and rejects through the Worker; each write inserts one `audit_log` row (`approve_asset`, `reject_asset`) and one `events` row (`emit_event`).
- cause: `audit_log_immutable` raises `append_only` on every update or delete, retention flag or not; `events_append_only` lets a delete through only when `mop.retention` is `on`. So the plan's transaction cannot remove the audit rows, and without a line for events it also leaves those.
- rule: an e2e that writes through the admin API deletes the events it caused in the same retention transaction (`delete from public.events where entity_id::text = any($1)`) and names the audit rows it leaves behind in its header comment; a plan line that promises "no committed row" for a spec that writes through `write_audit` is a plan defect.
- proof: `bun run db:psql -- -At -c "select count(*) from audit_log where action like 'assets.%' and at > now() - interval '30 minutes'"` after one run of `tests/e2e/admin-assets.spec.ts` → `2`; the same query on `events where type like 'asset.%'` → `0` (measured 2026-10-08, dev profile loaded).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-742 · The plan names `src/routes/admin/assets.index.tsx` as the whole screen 10 route, but ruling H66 allows an admin route file only the router, `lib/seo` and a stylesheet address
- symptom: the plan files list for B9 step 11 names one route file with the screen's search params. `tests/unit/admin-route-shells.test.ts` fails a route file whose static imports include `src/admin/**`.
- cause: the plan was written before H66 (2026-10-07); `people.index.tsx` plus `people.index.lazy.tsx` is the form in use, and H66a keeps the lazy sibling harmless.
- rule: a new admin screen is two files, a shell (`head` only) and a `.lazy.tsx` sibling holding `createLazyFileRoute`, the page and its imports; name both in the log.
- proof: `bunx vitest run tests/unit/admin-route-shells.test.ts` → passes with `assets.index.tsx` as built; with `import { AssetCards } from "../../admin/assets/AssetCards";` added to it the test prints `× src/routes/admin/assets.index.tsx imports only the router, the head helper and a stylesheet address` and `AssertionError: src/routes/admin/assets.index.tsx imports ../../admin/assets/AssetCards statically` (measured 2026-10-08, import removed again).
- added: 2026-10-08

## G-253 · A mouse swipe on an `<img>` starts the browser's native image drag and cancels the pointer stream
- paths: app/src/admin/assets/CarouselViewer.tsx
- severity: warn
- symptom: B9 g2's e2e drag from a quarter to three quarters of a slide with the mouse moved nothing: the counter stayed at "Slide 8 of 8". The component test, which fires pointer events directly, passed.
- cause (inferred: removing `draggable={false}` turns the case red and putting it back turns it green; the `pointercancel` itself was not logged): a press on an image with `draggable` unset starts HTML5 drag-and-drop, the browser sends `pointercancel`, and the `pointerup` the swipe waits for never arrives.
- rule: the slide `<img>` carries `draggable={false}`; a swipe is proved in a browser (Playwright `page.mouse`), because jsdom has no native drag.
- proof: `grep -n "draggable={false}" app/src/admin/assets/CarouselViewer.tsx` → one hit; with it removed, `E2E_TARGET=built bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-assets.spec.ts --grep "carousel goes"` fails at `Slide 7 of 8` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-733 · A new required prop on `EmailProps` breaks every other caller of `Message`, and a zod `satisfies` of an optional field fails under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`
- symptom: B9 c5n added `variables` to `EmailProps`; `bun run typecheck` then failed in `scripts/build-auth-templates.ts`, which builds `Message` itself without `renderTemplate`. A first `satisfies NewsletterBlockProps` on the zod schema's optional `alt` failed with `Type 'string | undefined' is not assignable to type 'string'`.
- cause: `EmailProps` has two callers, `renderTemplate` and the auth-template build script, and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` (R01) makes `alt?: string` refuse the explicit `undefined` that zod's optional produces.
- rule: before adding a field to `EmailProps`, grep `createElement(Message` and `EmailProps` under `app/src` and `app/scripts` and give every caller the field; a prop that receives a zod-optional value is typed `alt?: string | undefined`, as `NewsletterBlockProps` does.
- proof: `grep -n "variables: {}" app/scripts/build-auth-templates.ts` → one hit, and `cd app && bun run typecheck` exits 0 (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-09, B7 g2: a service input typed `expected_updated_at?: string` refused the Zod output `string | undefined` of the route (`TS2379` under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`); a service that takes a Zod output type writes `?: string | undefined`.

## P-734 · An email block was drawn without running the email gate on it: B5's `lintEmail` found `img-width` and `link-text` on the first Campaign block
- symptom: the first c5n build of `NewsletterBlock` passed its tests and was rejected on review: `lintEmail(html, text, "standalone")` of a row with a block gave `img-width` (the `<img>` had only a CSS width, which Outlook ignores) and `link-text` (the image link held no visible text). The sample row of B5 has no block, so `tests/unit/email/lint.test.ts` stayed green.
- cause: a block that only a variable draws is in no sample render, so the lint test never saw it; the author wrote "no mail client was used" and did not run the deterministic gate that was in the repository.
- rule: a component that draws into an email is rendered through `renderTemplate` and passed to `lintEmail` in its own test; an image carries a numeric `width` attribute, and a link carries visible text (an image is not clickable on its own).
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/assets/templates.test.ts -t "passes the email gate"` passes; with the `width` attribute renamed (registry entry `c5n-block-width`) it fails on `img-width`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## G-251 · A component that throws inside `render` resolves with a fallback under Node and rejects in the Worker: refuse both, and test the edge build
- paths: app/src/templates/email/**, app/src/server/email/render.ts
- severity: warn
- symptom: B9 c5n's first test of a malformed `block` expected `renderTemplate` to reject; under vitest it resolved with HTML that began `<!--$!--><template data-msg="Switched to client rendering because the server rendering errored: standalone_block_invalid" data-stck="...`. The fix that checked for that marker went green and was rejected in review: in the Worker the same render rejects with a plain `Error`, so the job runner (`error instanceof NonRetryableError`) retried it until its attempts ran out.
- cause: `@react-email/render` ships two builds. The Node build (`dist/node`, what vitest resolves) recovers from a throw by emitting a Suspense error marker and does not reject. The `workerd` export condition resolves to `dist/edge`, whose `renderToReadableStream` has `onError: reject`. A check measured under vitest's conditions says nothing about the Worker.
- rule: `renderTemplate` refuses both outcomes as `NonRetryableError("template_render_failed")` (a rejection keeps the original as `cause`; output holding `<!--$!-->` is refused); a throw inside an `Email` component is never the refusal by itself. A test of a render failure runs against `dist/edge` as well (`vi.doMock("@react-email/render", ...)` with the edge file path).
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/assets/templates.test.ts` → 22 passed; registry entries `c5n-edge-build` (the mocked path changed from `dist/edge` to `dist/node`: no cause, the test is red), `c5n-edge-rejects` (plain `Error`), `c5n-edge-cause` (no `cause`) and `c5n-block-invalid` (the Node marker check deleted) are each red (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B9 c5n rework: the first version of this entry described the Node build alone and told the next worker that a throw never rejects.

## G-252 · supabase-js `.range()` past the last row answers 416 `PGRST103`, and `fromRpcError` turns it into a 500
- paths: app/src/server/**/service.ts
- severity: warn
- symptom: B9 g1's `listAssets` answered 500 `server` for `GET /api/admin/assets?page=2` with 8 assets, and for a page that emptied after approvals; the unit stub and the db test's `pg` adapter both answered an empty page, so every test stayed green.
- cause: with `select(..., { count: "exact" })`, PostgREST refuses a range whose offset is larger than the number of matching rows with HTTP 416 `PGRST103` ("An offset of 50 was requested, but there are only 8 rows.") and no count; an offset equal to the count still answers 206 with no rows (measured on mop-dev 2026-10-08: offsets 7 and 8 of 8 answered 206, 9 and 50 answered 416). `fromRpcError` maps only `PGRST000` to `PGRST003` and named codes, so the 416 becomes `AppError("server")`.
- rule: an offset-paged admin list treats `error.code === "PGRST103"` as an empty page and takes the total from a `head: true` count of the same filters, as `listAssets` does; a test of it runs once over the real client (a read-only case in its db test), because a stub or a `pg` adapter shares the author's idea of the answer. `tests/fixtures/table-stub.ts` now answers the same 416 for a counted range past the last row. `src/server/channels/service.ts` pages with `.range()` the same way (suspected by reading, not run).
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx vitest run --project db tests/db/assets-service.db.test.ts -t "listAssets through PostgREST"` → `1 passed`; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b9g1-db-past-last-page` (the PGRST103 branch disabled) → `WATCHED-FAIL OK`, its red run `AppError: Something went wrong` from `fromRpcError`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-735 · `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` refuses an `import("...")` type annotation: use `import type` at the top
- symptom: while B9 c5n wrote the edge-build test, lint refused an `import()` type annotation with `@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports` and the test was reworked (reported by the author; the refused line is not in a commit, because the rewrite replaced it before the commit).
- cause: `app/eslint.config.js` sets `"@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports": "error"` with the rule's default `disallowTypeAnnotations: true`, which forbids the `import("x").T` form.
- rule: a type from a module the test loads with `await import(...)` is named by `import type { T } from "..."` at the top of the file, or inferred from the awaited value; never written as `import("...").T`.
- proof: `grep -n "consistent-type-imports" app/eslint.config.js` → line 160 `"@typescript-eslint/consistent-type-imports": "error"`; `cd app && bunx eslint tests/unit/assets/templates.test.ts` → no output, exit 0 (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-736 · A module imported directly before `vi.doMock` keeps the real dependency: import it dynamically after `vi.resetModules()`
- symptom: while B9 c5n tested the edge build of `@react-email/render` (G-251), a direct import of the module path that `vi.doMock` replaces ran the real module and skipped the mock; that is what made the author drop the premise test (reported by the author; the dropped test is not in a commit).
- cause: `vi.doMock` is not hoisted and replaces a specifier only for modules loaded after the call. A static import, or a direct import of the replaced path, binds the real module when it first loads, and the mock cannot reach it. The mock factory itself must import the edge file by its own path, because importing the mocked specifier from inside it would recurse.
- rule: a test that replaces a dependency with `vi.doMock` calls `vi.resetModules()`, registers the mock, then loads the module under test with `await import(...)`; `afterEach` runs `vi.doUnmock` and `vi.resetModules()`. A mocked test is watched-fail on the mock itself (point it at the wrong path and see it red).
- proof: `cd app && grep -nE "underEdge|doMock|resetModules" tests/unit/assets/templates.test.ts` shows `underEdge` (resetModules, doMock, dynamic imports); `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only c5n-edge-build` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK` (the mocked path changed to `dist/node`) (2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2218 · `watchfail.mjs --registry <dir>` replays every JSON file in the folder, so a scratch folder that still holds an earlier copy doubles the count and a green `ok N` counts stale entries too
- symptom: B10 g5 review: the replay of the 71 `b10g5-*` entries printed `watchfail: replayed 142: ok 142, bad 0, stale 0`. The scratch folder held `B10.json` from an earlier run (02:23) next to the new `B10g5.json` (02:56), the same 71 ids with the same content, and the two files had to be diffed to trust the number.
- cause: `loadRegistries` reads every `*.json` of the folder (a registry is a file name, an id shared by several registries replays them all). Had the old copy held other entries, the green total would have included entries of an older tree.
- rule: replay a group's entries from a new, empty folder (or one named for the run) and check that the `replayed N` count equals the number of entries copied; `ls` the folder before the replay.
- proof: from `app/`, `grep -c '"id": "b10g5-' tests/mutations/B10.json` → `71`; after the replay written to a file, `grep -c 'WATCHED-FAIL OK' <output>` must print the same `71`, and `ls <folder>` before it lists only the file you copied (the review measured 142 for 71 entries with a stale copy beside the new one, 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2223 · A review snapshot taken after the group's pull request merged has an empty `git diff origin/main...HEAD`; the diff base is the log's "Branch started from" commit
- symptom: the B10 g2 reviewer ran `git diff origin/main...slice/b10 --stat` from the brief and it printed nothing, although the group had changed files. PR #214 had already merged the reviewed commit b8e8d9f into origin/main, so there was nothing to compare.
- cause: a three-dot diff is the commits of HEAD that origin/main lacks. Once the group is merged, origin/main is a descendant of HEAD and the set is empty. P-838 is the other half (the branch moved on past the frozen commit); this is the frozen commit already in main.
- rule: in a review snapshot take the diff base from the log block's "Branch started from" line or from `git log --first-parent --oneline`, never from origin/main; when `git diff origin/main...HEAD --stat` prints nothing, check `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/main` before reading it as "no change". The brief template's owner names the base commit instead of origin/main.
- proof: `git merge-base --is-ancestor b8e8d9f origin/main && echo ancestor` → `ancestor`, and `git diff origin/main...b8e8d9f --stat | wc -l` → `0` (measured 2026-10-08, B10 g2 follow-ups; the group's real range was 64ab67b..8236af0 from the first-parent log).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2224 · `plan-brief.mjs --steps "1,3b"` reads a list, not a range: the brief for steps 1-3b quoted steps 1 and 3b and left out step 3
- symptom: the B10 g2 review brief called `node workspace/05-plans/plan-brief.mjs B10 --steps "1,3b" ...` for a group whose plan steps are 1-3b. Under "The steps, verbatim" the output holds only the lines starting `1. Owner setup` and `3b. LinkedIn confirmation`; step 3, the only step the group ran, is missing and the reviewer grepped its text from B10.md.
- cause: `plan-brief.mjs` splits `--steps` on commas and spaces into a set of exact step ids (lines 17 and 31); it has no range syntax, and the sizing step wrote the group's first and last step ids only.
- rule: a brief names every step id of the group (`--steps "1,2,3,3a,3b"`), taken from the plan's step list, never the two ends of a range. The same brief also tells the reviewer to run plan-brief from the lane folder while forbidding any run there (P-706); the reviewer ran it in the snapshot.
- proof: `node workspace/05-plans/plan-brief.mjs B10 --steps "1,3b" 2>&1 | grep -nE "^(1|2|3|3b)\. " | cut -c1-30` → two lines, `4:1. Owner setup` and `5:3b. LinkedIn confirmat`, none for step 3 (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2450 · Agents of one workflow run share one scratchpad, and a generic file name in it (`wf.txt`, `check.txt`, `reg/`) is overwritten or interleaved by the parallel reviewer
- symptom: the B10 g6 reviewer wrote its watched-fail replay to `<scratchpad>/wf.txt` while the B11 reviewer wrote the same path. The file came out interleaved (`mutated src/server/channelsWATCHED-FAIL OK B11:b11-resend-skip-live-side-ef...`), `grep -c "WATCHED-FAIL OK B10:b10g6-"` printed 12 where the run itself ended `replayed 66: ok 66`, and the replay ran a second time.
- cause: the session scratchpad is one folder for every agent of a workflow run, and reviewers of different slices run at the same time. Two writers to one bare name overwrite each other (each `>` truncates) or interleave their lines.
- rule: inside the shared scratchpad write only under a subfolder named for your own run, `<scratchpad>/<slice><group>-rev-$$/` (`b10g6-rev-13186` worked), and never to a bare `wf.txt`, `check.txt` or `reg/`. Count a replay's lines from that file only. This extends P-088 and the scratch-file rule of the lane entry: the scratchpad is not private to the agent.
- proof: `d=$(mktemp -d); for r in A B; do (for i in $(seq 1 200); do echo "$r line $i"; done > "$d/wf.txt") & done; wait; grep -c . "$d/wf.txt"; rm -rf "$d"` → `200`, not 400 (two writers, one name, half the lines are gone; measured 2026-10-08 on this laptop). Re-run into `$SP/b10g6-rev-13186/wf.txt` printed 66 `WATCHED-FAIL OK B10:b10g6-` lines.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2451 · One `preview` run of `deploy` hung in lighthouse on `/property/west-village-townhouse` and hit its 20-minute timeout; the rerun passed
- symptom: PR 223 (B10 merge, no change under the public property route): `deploy` job `preview` (run 37708860863) failed at step `lighthouse`, "The operation was canceled." after `timeout-minutes: 20`; attempt 1 was the hang (run #1 of the property page took 9 minutes 46 s and the third run never finished), attempt 2 was cancelled by the next push 26 s later. The rerun of the same deploy passed lighthouse on that page in 4 min 04 s (01:34:37Z to 01:38:41Z), and B7's preview did the same page in 3 min 49 s.
- cause: that preview run's environment, not the page and not the lane (orchestrator, 2026-10-08 04:45). The B10 diff touches admin channels, `domain/channels.ts` and tests only.
- rule: a `preview` failure at the lighthouse step is one rerun (`gh run rerun <id> --failed`) before anything else; read the step timestamps first, a run #1 that takes minutes is the signal. Only a second hang on the same page is reported as a defect with the log lines.
- proof: `gh run view 37708860863 --json jobs --jq '.jobs[]|select(.name=="preview")|.conclusion'` → success after the rerun
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08 23:08 to 23:18 +0300, on the laptop, not a runner (H73's first real local run, PR 227 number, head d62b9238): `bun run lhci` (lighthouserc.json, 6 urls) finished the three runs of `/` and then printed `Running Lighthouse 3 time(s) on http://127.0.0.1:8970/properties` and `Run #1...` and nothing more until the 10-minute bound stopped it, while the `wrangler dev` log shows `GET /properties 200 OK (620ms)` and the Worker kept answering. So "the preview run's environment" above is not the whole cause: a Lighthouse run can hang on a page the server answers quickly, on Windows as on Linux. Proof: `grep -n "Run #1...$" <tmp>/mop-preview-local/pr-227-d62b923/lighthouse.out` is the last line of that file.

## P-2219 · A full-stack e2e spec that saves through `/api/admin` answers 503 `csrf_secret_missing` under the dev profile
- symptom: `bunx playwright test tests/e2e/admin-channels.spec.ts` after `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"`: the sign-in and read cases passed, the Retry click got `503 {"error":{"code":"csrf_secret_missing","message":"Saving is unavailable at the moment. Please try again later."}}`, found only by reading the response body in `trace.zip` (the page shows the message, the test shows the status).
- cause: `verifyCsrf` answers 503 for a session write when `CSRF_SECRET` is undefined, and the dev profile exports the `DEV_*` names, `SUPABASE_URL` and `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (both mapped to mop-dev), `OPS_HEALTH_TOKEN` and `PREVIEW_RATE_LIMIT_SALT`, but not `CSRF_SECRET`, so the `vite dev` server that Playwright starts has no key. Loading the whole `.env` instead would export `SUPABASE_URL` and the service role key of the other business (G-901).
- rule: before a spec that saves through a session, export that one value without printing it: `export CSRF_SECRET="$(grep '^CSRF_SECRET=' ../.env | cut -d= -f2- | tr -d '\r')"` in `app/`, after the dev profile. Never `env -u SUPABASE_URL -u SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` after the dev profile: the profile sets both to mop-dev, and without them the sign-in answers 503 `unavailable` ("The database is not available.") at `helpers/session.ts`. For a 503 from a route, read the body (`unzip` the trace, `*.network`, `resources/<sha>.json`) before reading SQL.
- proof: from `app/`, with the dev profile and that export, `E2E_PORT=8968 env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx playwright test tests/e2e/admin-channels.spec.ts` → `4 passed`; without the export → `1 failed`, `Received: 503`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2220 · Before a4c12d73, `watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` selected committed entries only, so a group's uncommitted registry lines were never replayed and the summary still read `ok N, bad 0`
- symptom: B10 g9 added 75 entries (`b10g9-*`) to `tests/mutations/B10.json` and ran the reviewer's command before committing: `watchfail: replayed 60: ok 60, bad 0, stale 0; manual 4 not replayed; 3696 not selected`, and `grep -c b10g9 /tmp/wf.out` printed 0. The 60 were earlier groups' entries, about 12 minutes of replay.
- cause: `--changed <ref>` lists files with `git diff --name-only --relative <ref>...HEAD` (`scripts/watchfail.mjs`, `replayRegistry`), which holds commits only. A file changed in the working tree is not in the list, so no entry that names it is selected, and the count printed is whatever the commits selected.
- rule: on a tree whose `scripts/watchfail.mjs` has no `registryAt` (a lane that has not merged main past a4c12d73, P-539), replay the group's own entries from a scratch registry folder that holds only them (P-2218) before the commit and compare the replayed count with the entries added. Never read `ok N, bad 0` without checking that N includes the ids you wrote.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c registryAt scripts/watchfail.mjs` → `0` on the tree that measured the symptom (B10 g9 before its merge of main) and at least `2` after a4c12d73, which also replays the entries the working registry gained since the ref; there `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main | grep -c "<id prefix of an uncommitted entry>"` is not 0 (measured 2026-10-08, B10 g9).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2221 · A plan proof that greps a function name for "one line" is true only when the file imports it under an alias, as B8's reconcile.ts does for `reconcileUploads`
- symptom: step 9's proof `grep -n "reconcileSocial" src/server/jobs/system/reconcile.ts` must print one line. The first handler took the social part as a parameter named `reconcileSocial`, like B8's `reconcileUploads` parameter, and the grep printed three lines (the import, the parameter, the call).
- cause: B8's file writes `import { reconcileUploads as settleUploads }` so that its parameter can carry the name; a grep for the name counts the import line and every use of the parameter.
- rule: import the function as `reconcileSocial as settleSocial` and name the parameter `socialPart`, so the name stays on the import line alone; read a plan's grep for the count it expects before the file is written, not after.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "reconcileSocial" src/server/jobs/system/reconcile.ts` → one line, the import (measured 2026-10-08, B10 g9).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2222 · tableDb compares ISO timestamps as text, so the excluded instant of a half-open week is counted when it is seeded with a fraction the code does not send
- symptom: B10 g9's `buildCampaignReport` case seeded a visit at `2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z`, the first instant after the week that ends before `2026-10-12T00:00:00Z`; `clicks` came back 3 instead of 2.
- cause: `tests/fixtures/channel-db.ts` implements `gte` and `lt` on the strings, and `.` sorts before `Z`, so `…00:00.000Z` is less than `…00:00Z`; the real database compares instants and would not count it.
- rule: in a unit case that uses tableDb, seed a boundary value in the exact format the code sends or a clear hour inside the neighbouring day; prove the boundary itself in a `db` case.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/channels/reports.test.ts -t "first-party visits"` passes with the outside visit at `2026-10-12T09:00:00.000Z`; with `2026-10-12T00:00:00.000Z` the case fails with `clicks: 3` (measured 2026-10-08, B10 g9).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2225 · A db case that counts `audit_log` rows by action alone passes on CI's empty database and fails on mop-dev once an e2e spec has saved real rows
- symptom: `tests/db/social.db.test.ts` "raises enqueue_failed and changes nothing when no job is made (DB-09)" failed on mop-dev with `"audit": 5` where 0 was expected, with no prelude and no change of this group in its path, after g8's `admin-channels.spec.ts` had committed `channels.retry` rows.
- cause: the case summed `auditRows(db, "channels.retry")` and `auditRows(db, "channels.metrics_refresh")` with no entity, so every committed row of those actions on the shared database counted, not the rows of the transaction.
- rule: a db case counts audit rows by the `entity_id` it made (`auditRows(db, action, id)`); mop-dev holds committed rows from e2e specs and other lanes, and CI's fresh database hides the difference.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c 'auditRows(db, "channels.retry")' tests/db/social.db.test.ts` → `0`; with the dev profile, `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/social.db.test.ts -t "raises enqueue_failed"` → `Tests  1 passed | 21 skipped (22)` (measured 2026-10-08, B10 g9).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2226 · A `sed s/old/new/g` rename of a test helper also rewrote a longer identifier that contains it
- symptom: renaming the helper `posted_` to `writes` in `channels.test.tsx` turned the fixture field `posted_at` into `writesat`, and the WithdrawList cases failed with a Zod error `items.0.posted_at Required` printed as 900 lines of DOM.
- cause: `sed 's/posted_/writes/g'` matches inside `posted_at`; a short name with an underscore is a prefix of real field names.
- rule: rename with a name that is not a prefix of another identifier, or anchor the pattern with `\b`, and run `git diff --stat` for the test before the first run.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "writesat" src/admin/channels/channels.test.tsx` → `0`; `grep -c "posted_at" src/admin/channels/channels.test.tsx` → `3` or more.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2452 · Plan defect, B10 step 10: restoring the `instagram` row before the next runner tick leaves the tick nothing to schedule
- symptom: step 10 says the script "restores the `instagram` row to its previous values" and its proof expects, "after the next runner tick", one `instagram` row `scheduled`. Taken in that order the proof cannot pass.
- cause: `postToChannel` (`src/server/channels/post-to-channel.ts`) reads `channel_settings` when the job runs, not when the asset was approved: a row with `enabled = false` ends `skipped_disabled` before `schedule_social_post` writes anything, and a system approval (`approved_by` null) on a row no longer `auto` for the tier ends the row `failed` with `human_approval_required`.
- rule: the rehearsal keeps the `instagram` row open until the Feature asset's `social_posts` row exists (poll every 5 s, 150 s at most; the runner ticks every minute), then restores it in a `finally`. A plan step that restores a setting a later asynchronous job reads names the wait, or it is a plan defect to report. The `post_meta` job of the fixture asset ends `retry_at` outside the window (`result` `{"instagram":"retry_at"}`), so the `social_dry_run` log line is not what the proof shows: UNPROVEN until a run inside the Tuesday to Thursday window.
- proof: `grep -n "skipped_disabled\|human_approval_required" app/src/server/channels/post-to-channel.ts` → both lines; `grep -n "awaitInstagramPost" app/scripts/auto-approve-rehearsal.ts` → the wait before the restore.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2453 · `watchfail --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` on a lane branch with unmerged groups replays every earlier group's entries: over 15 minutes for ten new ones
- symptom: B10 g10's replay selected the entries of all earlier groups of slice/b10 (about 380 in `B10.json` alone, plus other registries), mutated other groups' `src/` files one after another and had not finished after 15 minutes; killing it left `src/server/lib/admin-route.ts` mutated until `git checkout -- <file>`.
- cause: `--changed <ref>` selects what differs from `<ref>`, and the branch carries every earlier group's unmerged work (P-539 widened it to entries the registry gained since the ref); `--only <id>` takes one exact id.
- rule: replay a group's own entries from a registry directory that holds only them: copy the group's entries to a temporary directory outside the tree and run `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry <dir>` from `app/` (ten entries in 9 s on 2026-10-08); never kill a replay between a `mutated` line and its `WATCHED-FAIL OK`, and after any interruption run `git status --short` and restore a tracked file with `git checkout -- <file>`.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b10g10-ara-poll --changed origin/main` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B10:b10g10-ara-poll`.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B10 g9 fix round: `--changed origin/main` ran past the 120-second tool limit and went to the background; the group's entries were replayed one id at a time with `--only` in a shell loop.

## P-2454 · The adapters raise a database failure and a platform outage as the same `AppError("unavailable")`, so a catch on `AppError` swallows database errors
- symptom: B10 g9's review ran `reconcileSocial` with `record_channel_check` and `record_channel_usage` answering an error: the run resolved `done` with `tokens {x: "error", linkedin: "error"}` and the messages in `errors`, where the plan says a database error throws so B8's backoff retries the job. A skipped `record_channel_usage` leaves an X read uncounted and breaks the budget of invariant 11; a skipped `record_channel_check` leaves `token_checked_at` unwritten for a day.
- cause: `oauth-tokens.ts`, `meta.ts` and `meta-token.ts` raise their database failures as `AppError("unavailable")`, the same class and code as "X did not answer"; the first version of `isPlatformError` counted every `AppError`. The test that was meant to prove it only failed `set_social_post_metrics`, which sits outside the try blocks.
- rule: a catch that counts platform errors names `GraphError`, `ChannelApiError` and the `AppError` codes that are not `unavailable`; an `unavailable` throws (the job is retried), as `platformFailure` in `post-to-channel.ts` already does. A test of "a database error throws" fails each database call the try block can reach (the token check, the usage count, the Vault read), not one call beside it.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/channels/reconcile.test.ts -t "throws when"` → `Tests  3 passed`.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B10 g9 second fix round: the rule "an `unavailable` throws" was too wide the other way. The adapters also raise the platform's own answers under `unavailable` ("X answered an unexpected shape (metrics)." for a deleted tweet that X answers with 200 and an errors array; "X did not answer." for a network failure), and a withdrawn X post (status stays `posted`, only `withdrawn_at` is set) was still selected for metrics, so every daily run threw at that post's day 7 or 28 and B8's backoff repeated it. Now `isPlatformError` also counts an `unavailable` whose message names the platform (`PLATFORM_UNAVAILABLE`: "<Platform> did not answer." or "answered an unexpected shape"), every other `unavailable` still throws, and both metrics queries skip rows with `withdrawn_at`. The match is on wording because the adapters (g4, g5) give the two kinds no separate class: a new database message that reads like the platform's would be swallowed, so a new adapter message is added to the test of "throws when" first. Proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/channels/reconcile.test.ts -t "no longer answers|does not answer|withdrawn"` → `Tests  3 passed`.

## P-2455 · A reviewer's scratch vitest probe outside the repository cannot load a `vitest.config.ts`, because the scratch folder has no `node_modules`
- symptom: `bunx vitest run --config <scratchpad>/probe/vitest.config.ts` → `Startup Error: Cannot find module 'vitest/config'`.
- cause: the config imports `defineConfig` from `vitest/config`, which resolves from the config file's folder, and the scratch folder has no `node_modules`.
- rule: write the probe's config as a plain-object `vitest.config.mjs` (`export default { test: { include: [...], setupFiles: [...] } }`) and pass `--config` and `--dir`; a reviewer then probes the snapshot without writing into it.
- proof: the same object as `.mjs` ran a probe against the g9 snapshot → `Tests  1 passed (1)` (reviewer's measurement, 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2456 · A merge of main into a lane that renumbers entries, conflicts in `routeTree.gen.ts` and `admin/index.css` and trips jscpd is three costs, and a log line that cites an entry for it must cite one that holds it
- symptom: B10 g9's merge of main cost three attempts: `bank-merge.mjs` refused the collision of the lane's P-2405 and P-2406 with main's entries of the same numbers (H69, the park's WIP commit), `routeTree.gen.ts` and `src/styles/admin/index.css` conflicted, and `bun run check` then stopped at jscpd on the `serve` helper that `channels.test.tsx` and B7's `properties.test.tsx` both carried. The group's costTime named P-2223, which is a different entry (an empty three-dot diff), so the cost had no entry.
- cause: a lane that numbers from its own base still collides when a P-24xx number is handed out on both sides (P-503); the generated route tree and the admin stylesheet index are shared lines every lane appends to; a helper copied into two test files is a clone once the second copy arrives.
- rule: renumber by `bank-merge.mjs` and write the old and new number in the log; regenerate `routeTree.gen.ts` with the build and keep both sides' lines in `index.css`; put a test helper two files need in `tests/fixtures/` before the merge (`admin-serve.ts`); cite the entry that holds a cost, and add one when none does.
- proof: `grep -c "fixtures/admin-serve" app/src/admin/channels/channels.test.tsx app/src/admin/reports/reports.test.tsx` → `1` for each file.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B8 g1 (steps 9, 10a): the merge of main into slice/b8 conflicted in `GOTCHAS.md` (`bank-merge.mjs`, 0 lost), `routeTree.gen.ts` (took main's side, then `bun run build` regenerated the jobs routes, 83 lines mention jobs, no markers) and `admin/index.css` (both `@import` lines kept: `jobs.css` and `media.css`). It cost about ten minutes; the rule above was followed once it was found.

## P-2457 · P-2453's rule names a temporary registry folder, but `--only <id>` replays a group's entries one at a time with nothing to copy or clean up
- symptom: B10 g10's reviewer replayed all ten `b10g10` entries with `--only <id>` in seconds and left nothing behind, where P-2453's rule has the builder copy the entries into a temporary folder outside the tree and run `--registry <dir>`.
- cause: P-2453's own cause line says `--only <id>` takes one exact id, yet its rule chose the copy. The folder is a second registry that can go stale (P-2218) and must be removed.
- rule: replay a group's entries with `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only <id>` once per entry id of the group, from `app/`, as the first choice; the temporary folder of P-2453 is only for a replay that must run without the committed registry. The interruption rule of P-2453 stands: never kill a replay between a `mutated` line and its `WATCHED-FAIL OK`, then `git status --short`.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b10g10-ara-poll` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B10:b10g10-ara-poll` and `replayed 1: ok 1, bad 0, stale 0` (on 2026-10-08 `4041 not selected`).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2458 · `bunx supabase secrets list` fails with `AccessTokenRequiredError` under the dev profile alone, and its output carries a sha256 digest of every secret
- symptom: B10 g10's review ran `bunx supabase secrets list --project-ref $DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF` with only `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` loaded and got `{"code":"AccessTokenRequiredError"}`; after the `.env` set -a line it exited 0.
- cause: the dev profile exports the project ref and the database names, not `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, which only the full `.env` load (the set -a line) sets. P-2400 records this only for `secrets set`. `secrets list` prints each secret's value as a sha256 digest, not as text.
- rule: load the `.env` with the set -a line before any `supabase secrets` command. To check a flag's value, compare the listed digest with the sha256 of the expected value (for `SOCIAL_DRY_RUN` = `1` the digest is `6b86b273...`); never print or paste a value, and keep the full listing out of the log.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; env -u SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN bunx supabase secrets list --project-ref "$DEV_SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF" | head -c 200` → `{"_tag":"Error","error":{"code":"AccessTokenRequiredError", ...` (shell without the token); `printf 1 | sha256sum` → `6b86b273ff34fce1...`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-541 · A check stage on a shared lane machine dies with "JavaScript heap out of memory": node's 2 GB heap ceiling under five concurrent checks, not the machine running dry
- symptom: 2026-10-08 11:44, Dell, B11 g1 builder (lane D:/mop-build/b11): `bun run check` printed `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory` (Mark-Compact 2036 MB -> 2028 MB of a 2054 MB limit) after 304 s while five agents ran; the system had 1.96 GB free.
- cause: the stage was `eslint . --max-warnings 0` (type-aware lint, R01 projectService, holds the program of about 2,000 files in memory; exit 134); node sizes its default old-space limit from the machine (the Dell gave 2054 MB, this laptop gives 4288) and under load eslint crosses the smaller one. The machine was not out of memory.
- rule: re-run as `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 bun run check` and keep the variable for the group's later checks, builds and tests; the builders' brief carries the line. No lane pause for a node heap OOM; a pause needs a killed process, a worker crash or a Chromium failure with low free memory.
- proof: `node -e "console.log(require(v8).getHeapStatistics().heap_size_limit/1048576|0)"` prints about 2096 (the default) and `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096 node -e ...` prints about 4144.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B8 g1 step 10: the first `bun run check` after merging origin/main died in the lint stage with exit 134 (heap out of memory, other lanes running); the re-run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` passed.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B7 g1 (step 8): `bun run lint` alone died with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit` after 173 s; rerun with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` it finished and reported the real findings.

## P-2502 · B8b step 6 puts `putFlags` in `src/server/lib/flags.ts` and has the flags route call it, but an admin route may import only services
- symptom: B8b g6, `bun run check`: `tests/unit/admin-authz-sweep.test.ts` "import only the wrapper, services and domain" failed with `automation.flags.ts: ../../../server/lib/flags`.
- cause: the plan's Files line names `src/server/lib/flags.ts` (B3b's reader file) as the home of `putFlags` and says the route's PUT calls it; B7's sweep allows a route file only `server/lib/admin-route`, `server/**/service`, `domain/**`, the router and zod (R11).
- rule: a write that a plan puts outside a service file reaches its route through the group's service (`export { putFlags } from "../lib/flags.ts"` in `src/server/automation/service.ts`); never widen the sweep's allow-list for one route.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/admin-authz-sweep.test.ts` passes on slice/b8b at B8b g6; with `import { putFlags } from "../../../server/lib/flags";` in `src/routes/api/admin/automation.flags.ts` it fails as above (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2503 · A registry `expect` of `× .*<describe> > <title>` never matches: vitest's `×` line carries the test title alone
- symptom: B8b g6, first replay of the new unit entries: `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: wrong reason` for `b8b-g6-putrecipe-authorize` and `b8b-g6-puttemplate-authorize`, whose expects were `× .*putRecipe > commercial gets 403 and no database call`; the red run printed `× commercial gets 403 and no database call 6ms` and `FAIL  |unit| tests/unit/automation/service.test.ts > putRecipe > commercial gets 403 ...`.
- cause: the reporter's `×` line is indented under its describe and names only the test; the describe path appears only on the `FAIL` line. Two describes with the same test title cannot be told apart by `×`.
- rule: a registry `expect` matches `× .*<title>` when the title is unique in the file, and `FAIL .*> <describe> > <title>` when it is not.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b8b-g6-putrecipe-authorize` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B8b:b8b-g6-putrecipe-authorize` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1004 · Generated function types mark no argument nullable: a typed `db.rpc` refuses `p_actor: null`
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g2's `applySiteSettings` passed `p_actor: writer.id` (`string | null`) and `p_request_id: null` to `db.rpc("settings_put_site", ...)`; `tsc` printed `Type 'string | null' is not assignable to type 'string'` and `Type 'null' is not assignable to type 'string'`, although the function stores both as SQL null (the plan's call is `p_actor` null for the operator's script).
- cause: `supabase gen types` writes every argument of a function without a default as required and non-null (`"p_actor": string` in `src/db/types.ts`), whatever the SQL accepts; the one other null-actor caller (`newsletter/assemble.ts`) casts its whole client under a STUB.
- rule: build the arguments with the generated `Args` type and the nullable members widened (`Omit<Args, "p_actor" | "p_request_id"> & { p_actor: string | null; ... }`), then cast that one object to `Args` with an `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-type-assertion -- <reason>`; never cast the client, and never send a placeholder uuid as "no actor".
- proof: `cd app && bunx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exits 0 on slice/b16 at B16 g2; `grep -n '"settings_put_site"' -A2 src/db/types.ts` shows `"p_actor": string`.
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1005 · The CI `db` job skips a draft pull request, so a builder told to open a draft and never mark it ready cannot get the `db` proof
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g2's brief made "the CI `db` job is green on the pull request" the group's proof and also said to open a draft and never mark it ready; on draft PR 209 `gh pr checks 209` listed `db	skipping` (with `e2e` and `merge-gate`) while `check` and `build` passed.
- cause: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` gates the job with `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.draft == false && vars.CI_HEAVY != 'off'`, which saves Actions minutes on drafts; the brief template predates that line or ignores it.
- rule: a builder of a draft pull request runs the db test file itself on mop-dev against the pushed function (or inside rolled-back transactions for an unpushed migration, P-312) and reports the CI `db` job UNPROVEN until the orchestrator marks the PR ready; it never marks the PR ready to get the run. Do not wait on a `db` check of a draft.
- proof: `grep -n "draft == false" .github/workflows/ci.yml` prints the `db:` job's `if:` line (line 151 at bc9ed11); `gh pr checks 209` lists `db	skipping` while the PR is a draft (measured 2026-10-07, B16 g2).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1939 · A readiness probe on the proof URL spends the first `miss`, and the first requests after `wrangler dev` starts can be 503
- symptom: B16 g3's edge-cache proof printed `x-mop-cache: bypass` twice (HTTP 503, the log showed status 503 at about 2000 ms), then `miss` only for the third request (the one with a query string). An earlier start had already answered the `until curl .../api/public/site` readiness loop with the miss, so the first printed pass was a `hit`.
- cause: the loop that waits for the Worker requests the very URL the proof then expects to be a `miss`, and a stored copy is keyed by path only. On a cold start the first calls reach `public_state` before the connection to Supabase is warm and fail at the 2 s read timeout in `state.ts` (503, nothing stored).
- rule: wait for `Ready on` in the wrangler log, never for a request to a URL under proof; warm the isolate with a request to another path (`/api/public/markets` until 200); only then run the miss and hit passes, on a fresh persist folder. A proof that printed `bypass` is not a miss: look at the status first.
- proof: start `bunx wrangler dev --config .output/server/wrangler.json --env-file "$(pwd)/.dev.vars" --port 8799 --persist-to ../.tmp/wrangler-cache-x` with its output in `../.tmp/w.log`, then `grep -q "Ready on" ../.tmp/w.log`, then `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8799/api/public/markets` until `200`, then `for i in 1 2; do curl -s -o /dev/null -D - http://127.0.0.1:8799/api/public/site | grep -i x-mop-cache; done` → `x-mop-cache: miss` then `x-mop-cache: hit` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-1006 · Swapping a server read for the shared public state breaks every test world that serves the old table, and the state memo carries one test's site into the next
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 step 4 made `loadSiteContext` and `resolveAdminRecipients` read `getSiteSettings(db)` instead of the `settings` table. `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/email tests/unit/jobs` went from green to 42 failures in 5 files (plus a timeout of `render-hook.test.ts` that is load, G-031) (`AppError: The catalog is not available right now.`, raised by `fakeDb` refusing the unregistered `public_state` RPC), and two registry entries of B5 (`b5-v-admins`, `b5-v-malformed`) named code that no longer existed or a test that no longer covered it.
- cause: the email worlds (`tests/fixtures/email-send.ts`, the `dbWith` of `variables.test.ts` and `preview.test.ts`) modelled the site as a `settings` row. The plan names `context.ts` and `site-context.test.ts` only. `getPublicState` memoises per isolate for 15 seconds, so a second world with another `contact` still read the first one's site.
- rule: a step that moves a read from a table to `getPublicState` lists the test fixtures that model the old read in its brief; the fixture answers `public_state` with `stateJson(7, { site })` built from the same value and calls `resetPublicStateMemo()` when it builds a world. Registry entries whose `find` or covering test changed are replayed with `--only <id>` the same hour, never left for the review.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/email tests/unit/jobs` prints `Tests  ... passed` with no failure; take `resetPublicStateMemo()` out of `emailWorld` and `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/email` fails `notify_admin > sends to then ADMIN_NOTIFY_EMAIL`, which reads the previous world's contact (measured 2026-10-07, B16 g4; restored).
- added: 2026-10-07

- severity: warn
- symptom: B16's watched-fail (e) expects `t.footer.line` containing `siteConfig.parentCompany` to fail with the line changed back to "An Omnikom company."; `"An Omnikom company.".includes("Omnikom")` is true, so a `toContain` assertion stays green and the watched-fail would have passed for no reason.

## P-1009 · A domain file cannot import `src/config/site.ts`: the job runner loads the domain under Deno, where `import.meta.env` does not exist
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 step 5 says `currentRightsVersion` in `src/domain/contracts.ts` is redefined as `legalVersions.terms` from `src/config/site.ts`. With that import, `deno check --frozen --config supabase/functions/job-runner/deno.json supabase/functions/job-runner/index.ts` printed `TS2339 [ERROR]: Property 'env' does not exist on type 'ImportMeta'` at `src/config/site.ts:9`, and at run time the module would throw on `env.VITE_SITE_URL`.

## P-1011 · `textContent` joins neighbouring elements with no space, so a word-boundary test for `null` on a whole page misses `Contactnull`
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g5's first "no null" case ran `expect(mainText()).not.toMatch(/\bnull\b/)` over the terms page; its watched-fail (the contact link printing `String(null)`) stayed green (`BAD: wrong reason`) because the page text read `...new version.Contactnull, or the contact page.`, where a heading's last letter and `null` form one word.
- cause: `textContent` of a container concatenates its children without separators, so a word boundary the eye sees is not in the string.
- rule: look for a literal in a page element by element: `[...document.querySelectorAll("main *")].filter((el) => /\bnull\b/.test(el.textContent))`, which matches the link that holds it.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b16-g5-unset-null` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B16:b16-g5-unset-null`; with the whole-page `not.toMatch` back in the test it printed `BAD: wrong reason` (measured 2026-10-08, B16 g5).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1012 · A privacy-page sentence names a retention period the build does not enforce, and the retention test cannot see it because it reads only the table rows
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g5's CCPA table said hashed IP addresses were kept 25 hours in the Identifiers row. Only `rate_limits` rows are deleted after 25 hours; `submissions.rights_ip_hash`, `submissions.ip_hash`, `inquiries.ip_hash` and `subject_requests.ip_hash` are never cleared (215 submissions on mop-dev held a `rights_ip_hash` older than 25 hours). A fresh reviewer found it; `legal-pages.test.tsx` only compared the `tr[data-retention]` cells.
- cause: a period was copied from `retentionPeriods` into prose about a data category, and the key's own scope (rate-limit records) was lost on the way.
- rule: write every retention sentence against the retention functions in `20261004065712_retention.sql` (`grep -n ip_hash` there finds none), name the table the period belongs to, and say plainly what stays; a test reads the prose cell, not only the table.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c ip_hash supabase/migrations/20261004065712_retention.sql` → `0`; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b16-g5-ip-hash-kept` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B16:b16-g5-ip-hash-kept`.
