## P-1013 · `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` run from the tree root loads nothing and exits 0, so a `&&` chain goes on without `DEV_DB_URL`
- severity: warn
- symptom: a reviewer ran the brief's dev-profile line from the tree root: `Cannot find module '...\scripts\load-env.mjs'` on stderr, then `eval` of the empty substitution exited 0 and the db test ran with no `DEV_DB_URL`.
- cause: the script lives in `app/scripts`, and `eval "$(cmd)"` returns the status of `eval`, not of `cmd` (a sibling of P-1930).
- rule: run it from `app/`, keep the output in a variable and fail on its status: `out=$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev) && eval "$out" && test -n "$DEV_DB_URL"`.
- proof: `cd app && out=$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev 2>/dev/null) && eval "$out" && test -n "$DEV_DB_URL" && echo ok` → `ok`; from the tree root `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"; echo $?` → the module error, then `0` (measured 2026-10-08, B16 g5 review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1014 · A smoke POST to `/api/public/subjects/request` answers 429 after three requests of the day from the laptop, and deleting `rate_limits` rows on the shared database is not the fix
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g6's smoke POST answered 429 until the author deleted 14 `rate_limits` rows of the last 30 hours from mop-dev, after which it answered 201. The log called the 429 the day's spent counters (`subjects-request:ip`, `subjects-request:email`); a fresh reviewer found the deletion had no rule anywhere, and the rows were not only this lane's.
- cause: the route allows 3 hits per ip and 2 per email a day, stored in `rate_limits`; `wrangler dev` sends no `cf-connecting-ip`, so every caller from the laptop shares the `0.0.0.0` bucket (P-1317) and earlier runs of any lane had used the hits. P-1317's clearing line covers `subscribers:%` buckets only. The plan itself says a second same-day run can answer 429, and that is the limit working.
- rule: never delete `rate_limits` rows of the shared database to get a 201. Send the smoke with its own `cf-connecting-ip` header (a documentation address such as `203.0.113.77`, never reused) and a fresh `.invalid` email: each gets a bucket no other run has spent. A 429 that remains is reported as the limit working, not cleared.
- proof: `grep -n -A5 '"/api/public/subjects/request"' app/src/server/public/routes.ts` → `limits` of `{ scope: "ip", ... limit: 3, windowSeconds: DAY }` and `{ scope: "email", ... limit: 2, windowSeconds: DAY }`; `grep -n cf-connecting-ip app/src/server/lib/ids.ts` → `?? "0.0.0.0"` (measured 2026-10-08, B16 g6 review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1015 · A hydration test that renders a whole route fails on the document shell and on a partial `vi.mock` of the analytics module: render the route's component under a bare root and spread `importOriginal`
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g6's first full-page hydration test for `/privacy-request` failed twice before it tested anything: the document shell's head assets did not match between the server markup and the hydrated tree, and a `vi.mock("../../src/lib/analytics")` factory that returned only `track` left `analyticsEvents` undefined for the modules that import it.
- cause: the root route's shell (head assets, scripts) is not under test and differs between `renderToString` and the jsdom hydrate; a mock factory replaces the whole module, so every export it does not list is missing. The group's log put both under G-701, which is only about the `useSearch()` split.
- rule: build the test router with `createRootRoute({ component: Outlet })` and the route's own component and `validateSearch`, so only the page hydrates; mock a module with `async (importOriginal) => ({ ...(await importOriginal<typeof Module>()), track: vi.fn() })`, typed through `import type * as Module` (G-103), never a bare factory.
- proof: `grep -n "createRootRoute|importOriginal" app/tests/unit/privacy-request.test.tsx` → the bare root (line 94) and the spread (line 27-28); `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b16-g6-stored-ignores-kind` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK B16:b16-g6-stored-ignores-kind` (measured 2026-10-08, B16 g6 review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1940 · A test that makes hundreds of requests needs its own timeout, and its watched-fail must not count a timeout as red
- symptom: B16 g3's `site-read-path.test.ts` case (200 calls of `handlePublic`, one request log line each) went red with `Test timed out in 5000ms` in 2 of 4 runs of the bare `bunx vitest run` proof under load; `bun run check` stayed green because `bun run test` passes `--testTimeout=60000`. The registry entry `b16-g3-read-table` expects `FAIL .*> the site read path > makes one public_state call`, which a timeout satisfies too.
- cause: a loop test inherits the 5 s default of the project when it is run by name, and a registry `expect` that names only the test matches any failure of that test, including a timeout.
- rule: give a loop or counter test its own timeout (`it(name, fn, 30_000)`) and keep the loop short; a watched-fail is genuine only when the red output carries the assertion text (`AssertionError`), so read the saved output of the replay once, not only the `WATCHED-FAIL OK` line.
- proof: `grep -n "30_000" app/tests/unit/site-read-path.test.ts` prints the timeout on the first case.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1941 · A plan line for a public route row is written for an older table shape: the path, the method and the response schema do not match the tree
- symptom: B16 step 3 says the row is path `/site`, handler `GET`, with a `PublicSite` response; the tree has full paths in every row (`/api/public/site`), every file under `src/routes/api/public` is `ANY` (`routes-parity.test.ts` asserts it), the row is `catalogRead(path, service)`, and `src/domain/settings.ts` has no response schema. ## P-1942 · `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` on a lane replays the whole lane's registry and outlives a 600 s tool call; killing it leaves a mutation in the tree
- symptom: the replay moved to the background at 600 s; stopping its `node.exe` left `turnstile: true` changed to `false` in `src/server/public/routes.ts` (an entry of another group), visible only in `git status`.
- cause: `--changed origin/main` selects every entry whose file differs from main, which on a lane is hundreds; the restore step does not run when the process is killed.
- rule: replay by `--only <id>` for the entries of your own files, or run `--changed` in the background from the start; after any stopped replay run `git status --short` and `git checkout --` the file it names.
- proof: `git status --short` after a killed replay names the mutated file; `git checkout -- <file>` clears it.
- added: 2026-10-08

- symptom: B16 g6 added `subject_request_submitted` and `/privacy-request`; the first `bun run check` stopped at `tests/unit/analytics.test.ts(7,7): error TS2741: Property 'subject_request_submitted' is missing`, the second at `jscpd found too many duplicates` (the button, `FormError` and `DeliveryNotice` block copied from `contact-form.tsx`), the third at `routes-covered.test.ts > are all classified` naming `_site.privacy-request.tsx`. Each cycle took 10 to 15 minutes; the plan's step 6 names none of the three files.

- rule: for a new analytics event add it to `everyEvent`; for a new page route add it to `staticPaths` and `routeFileCoverage`; before the full check run `bun run typecheck && bun run jscpd && bunx vitest run tests/unit/analytics.test.ts tests/unit/routes-covered.test.ts`, and lay a new form out so it does not repeat a 70-token block of an older one.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/analytics.test.ts tests/unit/routes-covered.test.ts` → `Test Files  2 passed`; deleting `subject_request_submitted: true,` from `everyEvent` makes `bun run typecheck` print TS2741 (measured 2026-10-08, B16 g6).

- symptom: `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b16-g6-event-listed` printed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: wrong reason` with `expected /× .*lists every event name.../` and, two lines below, `× lists every event name that a track() call in src spells out 383ms` in the red output; the entry had been written by a `node -e` script from the shell.

## P-1945 · A merge of main into a lane left `bun run check` red on a test neither side touched: B16 made `loadSiteContext` read the public state, B7's decline-preview test stubs no `public_state`
- symptom: B16 g7, after `git merge origin/main`, `bun run check` failed only at the unit tests: `tests/unit/submissions.service.test.ts > decisions > the decline preview is the letter send_email renders ...` threw `AppError: The catalog is not available right now.` from `getPublicState`, `getSiteSettings`, `loadSiteContext`, `emailPreview`. - rule: after merging main into a lane, run the unit tests of the files main changed that import anything the lane changed (`git diff --name-only <merge-base> origin/main -- app/tests` then `bunx vitest run` on them) before the first full `check`; fix the stub in the test (here `public_state: () => stateJson(7, { site: null })` in `decisionDb`) and say so in the log.

- symptom: B16 g5 review: following lesson 5 ("`--check` runs after every edit of a mutated file (P-066)") printed `watchfail: Unknown option '--check'` and exit 64. The P-066 body names no such option either.

Never pass `--check` to watchfail. Before stopping a process by its id (P-094 left a stray python pid in B16 g5), confirm its command line first: `powershell -NoProfile -Command "(Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ProcessId=<pid>').CommandLine"`, because another lane may own it.

## G-701 · A page that seeds a controlled input from `useSearch()` hydrates out of step with its state, because the stored HTML ignores the query
- paths: app/src/routes/_site.*.tsx, app/src/components/forms/*.tsx
- severity: warn
- symptom: B16 g6 review: `/privacy-request?kind=opt_out` showed "Know what you hold about me" selected while React state, and so the `kind` submitted, was `opt_out`; clicking the visibly selected radio fired no change, so a CCPA request was recorded as the other kind. Server HTML carried `checked` on `access`.
- cause: the HTML edge cache keys pages by pathname only (S52, `src/server/public/cache.ts`), so the stored page never reflects the query; the route read `Route.useSearch()` during render and seeded `useState` with it, and React 19 hydration leaves the DOM `checked` as the server rendered it. A cold cache whose first render came from a query would store that query's markup for every visitor.
- rule: a search-driven value must not reach the first render. Gate it behind `useSyncExternalStore(() => () => undefined, () => true, () => false)` and derive the shown value as `chosen ?? linked ?? default` in the form (no effect, no seeded state), as `_site.privacy-request.tsx` does; `_site.properties.tsx` applies `q` in an effect for the same reason.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/privacy-request.test.tsx -t "stores the page without the kind"` → passes; with the first render reading the link (registry entry `b16-g6-stored-ignores-kind`) it fails on `Expected: "access" Received: "opt_out"`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1947 · Appending an entry to `healthChecks` breaks `health.test.ts` unseen, and a module memo cannot be emptied from inside a test file that mocks the module
- symptom: B16 g8 added `site_identity` to `healthChecks`. `tests/unit/jobs/health.test.ts` then listed ten check names, not eleven, and its `fakeDb` answered no `public_state`, so every case would have failed `site_identity` and emitted a second `health.failed`. In the new `health-site.test.ts` the case "no last good copy" returned `public_state_stale`, not the error code: an earlier case had filled the memo of `state.ts`, `vi.resetModules()` did not empty it, and the module was mocked with a factory that kept the old instance.
- cause: the plan's text says the entry calls `getPublicState(ctx.db)` and reads `stale: true` from it; `getPublicState` returns the state only, `readState` (same file) returns `{ state, stale }`. `resetPublicStateMemo()` keeps the last good copy by design, so only a fresh import has none.
- rule: a slice that appends a health check edits `health.test.ts` in the same step (the name list and the rpc the check reads). To get a cold isolate in a test, `vi.doUnmock(<module>)` then `vi.resetModules()` then a dynamic `import()` of the module under test. Use `readState`, not `getPublicState`, where `stale` matters.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/health-site.test.ts tests/unit/jobs/health.test.ts` -> `Tests  22 passed (22)` (2026-10-08); `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b16-g8-cold-code` -> `WATCHED-FAIL OK B16:b16-g8-cold-code`
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1948 · A runbook row copied from the plan named "the one reader" of a settings row and the stored copy's cache header as what the visitor gets; both were false on the tree
- symptom: the review of B16 g8 rejected `docs/runbooks/api.md` twice. The "Site identity" section said the one reader of `settings.site` outside the public state was `send_email`; `readInvoiceInputs` (`src/server/payments/invoice-settings.ts`, on main since B6) also reads the row from the table. The `/api/public/site` row gave `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, s-maxage=31536000`, which is the header of the stored copy; `answer()` in `src/server/public/cache.ts` resets it to `public, max-age=60` before the response leaves.
- cause: both sentences were written from the plan, not from a grep of the tree and a read of the function that sets the header. A slice that lands on main later (B6) adds a reader the plan could not know, and the plan's header line names the stored copy and the visitor's copy in one breath.
- rule: a runbook sentence that lists readers of a row is written from `grep -rn '"<key>"' src/server` run on the merged tree, and one that quotes a header names whether it is the visitor's or the stored copy's, read from `answer()`; a word like "the one" or "only" is a second case to look for (ruling H60 (b)).
- proof: `cd app && grep -rn '"site"' src/server | grep -v test` -> `send-email.ts:234` and `payments/invoice-settings.ts:33` both read the table; `grep -n 'headers.set("cache-control"' src/server/public/cache.ts` -> line 94 (stored copy, with s-maxage) and line 118 (a 200 to the visitor, `browserCacheControl(kind)` only).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1949 · A group re-launched with "paused before its fix round" was already fixed and merged: `git merge origin/main` fast-forwarded the lane to main
- symptom: B17 c8 (second launch), `git merge origin/main` printed the new files of other slices and `git log --oneline -3` then showed main's tip, `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` equal to HEAD. The brief said the fix round had not run; `grep -n "^## c8" workspace/05-plans/logs/B17.md` showed a finished "c8 · steps 8" block and "c8 · follow-ups recorded" (fcae302 on main, review found no blocking defect).
- cause: the brief's verdict text is the first review's evidence, kept by the workflow while a later round had landed; at that launch the lane's starting point was 191 commits behind main (a point-in-time count taken when the brief was written; it moves with every merge and cannot be measured again, so do not quote it as a current number).
- rule: before editing for a re-launched group, run `git merge origin/main`, then `git log --oneline -3 -- <the group's files>` and `grep -n "^## <group>" workspace/05-plans/logs/<slice>.md`; when the fix is already in the log and on main, the work is to re-measure against today's numbers (the bundle budget moved to 163,840 by ruling H66) and re-run the proofs, not to edit.
- proof: `git log --oneline -2 -- app/src/components/property/gallery.tsx` → the c8 commit `fcae3028`; `cd app && node scripts/bundle-check.mjs | tail -1` → `bundle-check: OK 24 routes under 163840 gzip bytes` on a live build.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-1950 · `bun run lhci:local` from an agent shell stops every run with `NO_NAVSTART` and prints no score, on every URL
- symptom: B17 c8 review, 2026-10-08: `bun run lhci:local -- --collect.url=http://127.0.0.1:8939/...` ended `Run #1...failed! ... (NO_NAVSTART)` and exit 1, three times, with a single URL and `numberOfRuns=1` as well, so it does not depend on the page. The log showed "Waiting for browser" for about 2 s, then about 12 s to "Connecting to browser". The review cost about 15 minutes and produced no score, so the author's medians of step 8 (perf 0.72 to 0.91, LCP 2.86 to 3.27 s) are UNPROVEN by that review.
- cause: two causes, FOUND 2026-10-09. (1) The Bash tool's sandbox (found 00:15) is one: every sandboxed run failed, three of four unsandboxed runs passed. (2) NO_NAVSTART also occurs outside the sandbox on a loaded laptop: one of the four unsandboxed runs (2026-10-09 00:46, PR 249 head 1abe2591, 154 s, three other workloads running) ended `Runtime error encountered: Something went wrong with recording the trace over your page load (NO_NAVSTART)`; log `workspace/05-plans/logs/preview-local/pr-249-1abe259.md`. The same `preview-local.mjs` run on the same head, same port range, same load, with the sandbox off (`dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on the Bash call) passed Lighthouse on all six pages (311 s), and so did the next two runs (PR 249 head c38264be, 528 s); every sandboxed run ended `NO_NAVSTART` or hung. Chrome's trace recording does not work under the sandbox. (The old text said: two candidates, neither tested: the sandbox, or Chrome starting too slowly on a busy laptop.) The same command ran to a score in the author's shell, so the preview and the config are not the cause.
- rule: run every local Lighthouse (`lhci`, `lhci:local`, `preview-local.mjs`) from a Bash call with the sandbox disabled AND with two attempts, as CI does (ruling H71; the `lighthouse` step of `preview-local.mjs` makes both and says `attempt 2 of 2` in the log); an agent whose Bash cannot disable the sandbox records the step as BLOCKED on this entry and hands it to the orchestrator. When a Lighthouse run ends `NO_NAVSTART` twice, never a third time in the same shell. Record the step as BLOCKED with this entry, and unblock it by running `bun run lhci:local` from the operator's normal shell (or by testing whether the sandbox blocks Chrome tracing). Do not call the scores proven or the step closed.
- proof: `grep -n "NO_NAVSTART" GOTCHAS.md` → this entry; to reproduce, start a live build on the lane port and run `cd app && bun run lhci:local -- --collect.url=http://127.0.0.1:8938/ --collect.numberOfRuns=1` → `NO_NAVSTART`, exit 1 in the reviewer's shell (2026-10-08); not re-run for this entry.
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08 23:33 +0300, H73's second real local preview run (`node scripts/preview-local.mjs --pr 227 --port 8970`, head ed3296de, spawned from an agent's background Bash call): `bun run lhci` (lighthouserc.json) failed `Run #1...failed!` on `http://127.0.0.1:8970/` with `Runtime error encountered: ... (NO_NAVSTART)` and exit 1 after 176 s, while the same run's essentials (49 passed) and overflow (59 passed) drove Chromium through Playwright without trouble; the first run of the same command 20 minutes earlier had finished `/` three times and then hung on `/properties` (P-2451). So an agent shell can produce both outcomes, and the lighthouse step of a local preview is BLOCKED here until it runs from the operator's normal shell. Proof: the `lighthouse` line and its tail in `workspace/05-plans/logs/preview-local/pr-227-ed3296d.md`.

## P-542 · `watchfail.mjs --changed <ref>` never selected an entry anchored outside `app/`: `git diff --name-only --relative` run from `app/` drops every path above it
- symptom: 2026-10-08 14:55, orchestrator: 273 registry entries anchor on a `file` or `test` that starts with `../` (`../.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, `../launch/reel/cues.mjs`, `../workspace/05-plans/merge-gate.mjs`). `B17:b17-deploy-lighthouse-gate` went stale when PR 241 changed `deploy.yml`; no `--changed origin/main` replay selected it, and PR 244's CI tripped on it by accident.
- cause: `replayRegistry()` listed changed files with `git diff --name-only --relative <ref>...HEAD` from `app/`; `--relative` keeps only paths under the current folder and strips that prefix, so the set held `src/x.ts` but never `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`, and an entry's raw `../.github/...` could not match it either way.
- rule: list changed paths from the repository root (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `git diff --name-only <ref>...HEAD` run there, no `--relative`) and compare each entry's `file` and `test` as repository-root paths (`relative(top, resolve(path))`). Any new selection test for `--changed` needs a fixture whose registry sits in a sub-folder of the repository and anchors on a file above it.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/watchfail.test.ts -t "above the registry"` passes both cases; `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only wf-outside-resolve` and `--only wf-outside-quiet` print `WATCHED-FAIL OK B4:<id>`.
- added: 2026-10-08
- enforced-by: tests/unit/watchfail.test.ts ("--changed <ref> replays an entry anchored on a changed file above the registry's folder (P-542)" and its unchanged-file sibling)

## P-2600 · A new keyset list service that copies `listPayments`' page logic fails `jscpd` at `bun run check`, after every unit test was green
- symptom: B8 g1 step 9: the first `bun run check` failed `jscpd` on a 93-token clone of `listPayments`' page logic in `listJobs` (`src/server/jobs/service.ts`); typecheck, lint and the unit tests had passed. `listJobs` was rewritten to page through its own `pageOf`, and a full `bun run check` ran again.
- cause: `.jscpd.json` has `minTokens 70` and `threshold 0` (R04); the limit-plus-one trim and `next_cursor` build of `src/server/payments/service.ts` is longer than that, and the plan line "keyset paging as listPayments" invites copying it (same cause as P-2121 and P-1221).
- rule: a new keyset list service writes its own page helper from the start (`pageOf` in `src/server/jobs/service.ts`) instead of copying `listPayments`' trim, and runs `bun run jscpd` right after the first green unit run, before the full check.
- proof: `cd app && bun run jscpd` -> `Found 0 clones.` on slice/b8 (2026-10-08); with `listJobs` carrying `listPayments`' page block again it prints the clone.
- hit again: P-2121 and P-1221 name the same gate for a render step and a script; none covers a list service.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2601 · A registry `sql` mutant that replaces a function must keep the parameter defaults the migration gives, or the replay is WATCHED-FAIL BAD
- symptom: PR 238's `db` job, step mutation replay: `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: wrong reason (B8:emit-entity)`, expected `+ "entity_id": null`, got `error: cannot remove parameter defaults from existing function` from `withRollback`.
- cause: the entry's `create or replace function public.emit_event(...)` was written against an older signature without `default null` on `p_entity_id` and `default '{}'` on `p_payload`; the branch's migration `20261004060603_system_jobs.sql` gives both, and Postgres refuses a replacement that drops a default, so the mutant never ran.
- rule: copy the mutant's signature from the migration as it stands on the branch (defaults included) and change only the line the mutant is about; when a migration changes a function a registry entry replaces, re-read the entry in the same commit.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" && env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only emit-entity` -> `WATCHED-FAIL OK B8:emit-entity`; the PR's `db` job runs the replay against a from-zero database where the defaults exist.
- added: 2026-10-08

## G-1200 · Browser code under `src/admin/**` cannot import `src/server/**`: only `vite build` says so
- paths: app/src/admin/**
- severity: warn
- symptom: B8 g1 step 10: `jobs-queries.ts` imported `jobEntityKeys` from `src/server/lib/jobs.ts`, as the plan line says. Typecheck, lint, knip and every unit test passed; the first `bun run build` failed with `[import-protection] Import denied in client environment ... Denied by file pattern: **/server/**`.
- cause: TanStack Start's import protection refuses any module under `server/` in the client graph, and only the bundler runs it. Nothing in `bun run check` imports the route tree, so the error shows at build time, after a full check.
- rule: a constant or schema that both the Worker and a screen read lives in `src/domain/` (dependency-free, explicit `.ts` import from the server side, R07) and the server file re-exports it; a plan line that names a `src/server/**` symbol for a screen is a plan defect, so move the symbol and say so in the log. Run `bun run build` right after the first import of a shared symbol in `src/admin/**`.
- proof: `cd app && bun run build` -> `built in` on slice/b8 with `jobEntityKeys` in `src/domain/job-entities.ts`; importing `../../server/lib/jobs` from `src/admin/jobs/jobs-queries.ts` prints the `Import denied in client environment` error (2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2602 · Proof commands that work in Git Bash fail on this laptop through `playwright --project`, `quiet.mjs` and `watchfail.mjs --run`
- symptom: B8 g1 step 10 lost about 15 minutes to four commands. (1) The plan's `bunx playwright test --project admin tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts` printed `Project(s) "tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts" not found`. (2) `node workspace/05-plans/quiet.mjs -- bunx playwright test ... --grep "a|b"` printed `'opens' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. (3) `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --file ... --run "bun run build && { ...; }"` printed `'{' is not recognized`, and an earlier `--run "bun run build && env -u X bunx playwright ..."` was marked `WATCHED-FAIL OK` against a loose `--expect` although nobody had seen the red output. (4) A registry `expect` typed through a Bash heredoc lost its backslash (P-008) and the replay said `expect is not a regular expression`.
- cause: `--project` is variadic in Playwright, so the next word is read as a second project; `quiet.mjs` and the `--run` of `watchfail.mjs` run their command through `cmd.exe`, which splits a space inside a quoted argument and treats `|`, `{` and `env` as its own; `watchfail.mjs` prints only OK or BAD, not the red run.
- rule: write `--project=admin <file>`; give a grep without spaces or `|` (use `.` for a space) and do not wrap Playwright in `quiet.mjs`; for a watched-fail that needs a build and a run, put the steps in a `bash` script in the scratchpad (`--run "bash <script> <arg>"`), have the script print the failing part, read it, and use an `--expect` taken from that output; put a backslash into a registry file with the Edit tool.
- proof: `cd app && E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8998 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts --grep "entity.filter"` runs the test (with `--project admin` it prints the `not found` error above), 2026-10-08.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2603 · The laptop e2e of a screen whose RPCs sit in an unmerged migration is red with a 500, by design
- symptom: B8 g1 step 10: `admin-jobs.spec.ts` passed its navigation, banner, axe checkpoint, entity-filter and drawer cases against mop-dev, and failed at `Retry` with status 500 and a `{"event":"unhandled_error","route":"jobs.retry"}` line in the Worker log.

A missing function is not translated by `fromRpcError`, so the screen sees a 500.
- rule: before reading a laptop e2e failure as a UI bug, ask whether the screen's RPCs exist on mop-dev; if they sit in an unmerged migration the Retry, Cancel and Approve cases are UNPROVEN until main pushes it, and the CI live e2e job (built from the branch's migrations) is the proof. Run the cases that need no new function with `--grep`.
- proof: `cd app && eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)" && node -e "const pg=require('pg');(async()=>{const c=new pg.Client({connectionString:process.env.DEV_DB_URL});await c.connect();console.log((await c.query(\"select proname from pg_proc where proname like 'admin_%job%'\")).rows);await c.end()})()"` -> `[]` until the migration is pushed (2026-10-08).
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B8 c8j: the full `admin-jobs.spec.ts` failed at Retry with 500 on mop-dev, twice, because `20261008135942_jobs_admin.sql` is not on main; the Retry and Cancel cases of the spec are UNPROVEN on the laptop and the two cases that need no new function were run with `--grep`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2604 · Never run `bun run check` or a build in a tree while a `watchfail.mjs` replay with file entries is running there: the typecheck reads the mutant
- symptom: B8 c8e review: `watchfail.mjs --changed origin/main` ran in the background and `bun run check` ran at the same time in the same tree. The check failed with `src/domain/enums.check.ts(26,10) TS2344` and a `Probe` workflow_state error in `submissions/service.ts`, which looked like a real regression until `git status --short` showed ` M app/src/domain/contracts.ts`. After the replay finished the tree was clean and `bun run check` exited 0.
- cause: a `file` entry of the registry is applied by writing the mutated bytes into the working file for the length of its run (`writeFileSync` in `scripts/watchfail.mjs`) and restored afterwards, so every other command in that tree reads the mutant.
- rule: while a replay that has file entries runs, run no gate, build, test or editor save in that tree; wait for the replay to end, then confirm `git status --short` is clean before reading any red as a defect. A red check with a ` M` file you did not edit is this; a second tree (a worktree) is the way to run both at once.
- proof: start `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main > /dev/null` in the background and run `git status --short` from another call: it lists ` M app/src/domain/contracts.ts` (or the file of the entry running) until the replay ends, then prints nothing (2026-10-08, B8 c8e review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2605 · Plan step 10a reads `variants` values as keys and guards `assets` and `social_posts` with `to_regclass`, but `variants` holds sizes only and both tables are on main
- symptom: B8 g2 (step 10a): the Files line says `takedown_media_keys` returns `property_media.media_key` "and each value of `variants`", reads `assets` "once `to_regclass('public.assets')` is not null, through `execute`", and `takedown_mark_posts` works "through `execute`, once B10's `social_posts` ... exist", logging `takedown_posts_unavailable` while it returns 0. On the lane's main, `variants` is `{ thumb: { w, h }, ... }` (no key in it), `20261004172321_assets.sql` and `20261007040240_social.sql` (with `withdraw_required_at`) are merged, so the guards would be dead code and a 0 would only mean "no posted row", not "table absent".
- cause: the plan was written before B9 and B10 merged and before P-335 changed the stored `variants` shape to sizes only; a size's key is derived from the master `o/<owner>/<n>-<sha8>.webp` as `v/<owner>/<n>-<sha8>/<size>.<ext>`.
- rule: a SQL function that lists a photograph's keys derives each size's key from `media_key` with `variantKey`'s pattern (`og` and `carousel` are `.jpg`, the rest `.webp`), never from the values of `variants`. Before writing a `to_regclass` guard a plan asks for, `git grep -n "create table public.<name>" -- supabase/migrations`; a table that is already on main gets static SQL and no "unavailable" log.
- proof: `cd app && git grep -n "create table public.assets\|create table public.social_posts" -- supabase/migrations` → two lines; `bunx vitest run --project db tests/db/jobs.db.test.ts -t takedown_media_keys` with the takedown migration as `MOP_MUTATION_SQL` → `Tests  3 passed | 50 skipped (53)`, and the registry entry `b8g2-keys-sizes` (sizes from `'{}'`) replays red (measured 2026-10-08, B8 g2).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2606 · A system job's `maxAttempts` is read by nothing: `jobs.max_attempts` is whatever the enqueue passes as `p_max_attempts`, default 5
- symptom: B8 g2 declared `maxAttempts: 12` on `takedown_media` as the plan says, and the runbook draft said the job has 12 attempts. `git grep -n maxAttempts -- src/server/jobs/runner.ts src/server/lib/jobs.ts` shows the runner never reads the definition's value; it compares `job.attempts + 1 < job.max_attempts`, the column the enqueue wrote.
- cause: `SystemJobDefinition.maxAttempts` is declarative (`step-specs.test.ts` checks it for the outside system jobs); `enqueueJob()` and `enqueue_job` take `p_max_attempts` from their caller, and the column default is 5.
- rule: whoever enqueues a system job passes the definition's attempts (`enqueueJob({ ..., maxAttempts: 12 })`, or `p_max_attempts => 12` in SQL). For `takedown_media` that is B7's `unpublish_property` and the live proof's `enqueueJob()` call; a runbook says "the enqueue passes 12", never "the job has 12 attempts".
- proof: `cd app && git grep -n "max_attempts int not null default 5" -- supabase/migrations` → one line in the jobs migration; `git grep -n "maxAttempts" -- src/server/jobs/runner.ts` → no output (measured 2026-10-08, B8 g2).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2607 · An e2e spec's `afterAll` delete of a job passes until Retry gives the job a `job_events` row, then CI is red with `append_only`
- symptom: B8 c8j: PR 238's e2e job failed in `admin-jobs.spec.ts`'s `afterAll` with `could not remove the dead job: append_only` while the same spec had passed on the laptop; with the delete put back and the two cases that never press Retry, the delete succeeded on mop-dev.
- cause: `job_events.job_id` is `on delete cascade`, and `job_events` refuses every delete outside `mop.retention`; a job that was never retried has no event row, so its delete works, and the Retry case (or a runner) adds one.
- rule: an e2e spec, which commits to mop-dev, deletes nothing from a table that has an append-only child (`jobs`, `events`, `audit_log`): it leaves its rows with a marker in the key and the error, finds them by that text, and ends a job through the admin cancel action (`tests/mutations/B8.json` `c8j-e2e-no-delete`). Some api and db tests delete from `jobs` or `events` after `set_config('mop.retention', 'on', true)` (`tests/db/jobs.db.test.ts:279`, `tests/api/inquiries.api.test.ts:57`, `tests/db/assets.db.test.ts:663`); this rule does not cover them. A laptop run in which an earlier case fails leaves its `e2e_jobs` row `dead` for good, and the five-row Dead jobs banner of mop-dev's `/admin/jobs` then lists `e2e-jobs dead job <uuid>` rows until the launch switch's `db:reset`: they are not a real failure.
- proof: `cd app && grep -c "delete()" tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts` -> `0`; with a `job_events` row inserted before the delete, `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8998 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts --grep "entity.filter|opens.the.job"` fails in `afterAll` with `Error: could not remove the dead job: append_only` (2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2608 · A laptop e2e proof command copied from a log without the dev profile fails at `assertNotProduction` before any case runs, and reads like the red result the log claims
- symptom: B8 c8j review: the proof lines in `workspace/05-plans/logs/B8.md` (and the `run` fields of the registry entries `c8j-e2e-cancel` and `c8j-e2e-no-delete`) start at `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8996 env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts`. Run as written, `beforeAll` stops with `Error: refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set` (`assert-not-production.mjs:50`) and no case runs; it looks like a red proof but is not the failure the log describes. It cost one wasted e2e run.
- cause: the spec reaches mop-dev only through the dev profile (G-901); a shell that did not run `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` has no `DEV_DB_URL`, and the guard refuses on purpose.
- rule: every laptop proof line that starts Playwright, a db test or a script that calls `guardEnv()` begins with `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` in the same shell call, and the red output a log quotes names the case that failed, never `refusing:`. A `refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set` result is a missing profile, not a finding.
- proof: `cd app && E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8996 env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-jobs.spec.ts` -> `Error: refusing: DEV_DB_URL is not set`; the same line after `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` reaches the cases (2026-10-08, B8 c8j review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2609 · A cost line for "migrations:check asked for a restamp and passed only after the merge was committed" cites P-511, which is about two lanes pushing to mop-dev; P-318 and P-2314 hold it
- symptom: B7 g2's costTime and log line for the merge of main (B8 g1) read "`bun run migrations:check` asked for a rename and `bun run migrations:restamp` moved the migration ... (P-511)". The reviewer opened P-511 and found nothing about a restamp, a merge or a commit: it is the entry for two lanes writing migrations to mop-dev, so the cost had no entry that holds it.
- cause: P-511 is the first entry a search for "migration order" finds, and its title sounds close. The lesson that `check-migrations.mjs` reads only committed files, so a staged rename is not seen until it is committed, is held by P-318; the lesson that after a merge of main the check asks for a restamp and the newest `action_roles` file must be regenerated is held by P-2314.
- rule: a cost for a restamp after a merge of main cites P-2314, and one for a check that printed OK or crashed because the rename was not committed cites P-318, each with a "hit again" line when the lane hit it again. Open the entry before citing it (P-2456).
- proof: `awk '/^## P-511 /{f=1;next} /^## /{f=0} f' GOTCHAS.md | grep -c "restamp\|migrations:check\|committed"` → `0`; the same filter on `P-318` with `committ` → `4`, on `P-2314` with `restamp` → `2`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2036 · The preview job's `wait` fails when the Cloudflare account has reached the Workers free daily request limit: every workers.dev host answers 429, Error 1027
- symptom: B7 g3, PR 250: `preview` failed twice (runs 37817747700 and 37819990255) at `wait` with `the Worker did not answer ten times in a row in 180 s`, then at `observatory` with `no grade for pr-250.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev: status 422, error scan-failed`, while `check`, `build`, `db` and `e2e` passed. `curl` of `pr-250`, `pr-249` and `matter-of-place.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev` answered `429 Too Many Requests`, body "This website has been temporarily rate limited", `Error 1027`.
- cause: Error 1027 is Cloudflare's answer once an account on the Workers free plan has used its daily requests (100k a day, P-009); every Worker of the account answers it until the daily reset at 00:00 UTC. Inferred from the error code: the dashboard's usage figure was not read (UNPROVEN). Every lane's preview smoke, e2e and Lighthouse traffic shares the one account.
- rule: when `preview` fails at `wait`, curl the preview host once and read the status before reading the code: a `429` with `Error 1027` is the account's daily limit. Report the preview job UNPROVEN with that line, rerun it after 00:00 UTC (`gh run rerun <run id> --failed`), and change no code for it.
- proof: `curl -s --max-time 20 https://pr-250.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/ | grep -o "Error 1027"` → `Error 1027`; `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" https://matter-of-place.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/` → `429` (measured 2026-10-08 18:03 UTC).
- hit again: 2026-10-08 21:38 +0300, merge run for PR 250 at 66ab8d30: deploy run 37823989582 failed `preview` at `wait` in attempt 1 and again after `gh run rerun --failed` (attempt 2); `curl` of pr-250 answered `429` at 18:38 UTC. The merge gate printed `merge-gate: checks are not all green`. Waiting for 00:00 UTC is the only way through.
- hit again: 2026-10-08 21:48 +0300, merge-gate run for PR 250 at 31b9bb22: `preview` failed at `wait` (run 37825886936) while `check`, `build`, `db`, `e2e` and `preview-db` passed; `curl` of pr-250 answered `429` with `Error 1027` at 18:47 UTC; `merge-gate.mjs 250` printed `merge-gate: checks are not all green`. The merge agent returned blocked until 00:00 UTC.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2037 · `watchfail --changed <ref>` diffs `ref...HEAD`, so its replay count depends on whether the work is committed and whether the dev profile is loaded: a builder's "replayed 19" became 78 for the reviewer
- symptom: B7 g3 (step 11): the log quoted `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main --kinds unit` as `replayed 19: ok 19, bad 0`. The reviewer ran the same command at the handed-in commit d4b58b9 and read `watchfail: replayed 78: ok 62, bad 16, stale 0`, exit 1. All 16 BAD were db-project `file` entries printing `No test files found`; every `b7-11-*` entry was `WATCHED-FAIL OK`.
- cause: `--changed` runs `git diff --name-only <ref>...HEAD`, which sees committed files only. Before the commit it selects just the registry's new entries (19). After the commit it also selects every entry anchored on a file the group touched (here `src/domain/contracts.ts`, `tests/db/admin.db.test.ts`, `tests/db/admin-cache.db.test.ts`, `tests/unit/admin-routes-parity.test.ts`), and a db-project entry finds no test files unless the dev profile is loaded. The 19 was most likely measured before the commit (suspected, not confirmed).
- rule: quote a `--changed` replay line only from a run made after the commit, with the dev profile loaded (`eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"`, then `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`), or say it was run before the commit; a reviewer comparing counts runs it the same way. Compare the entry ids, not the totals.
- proof: `grep -n 'name-only' app/scripts/watchfail.mjs` → `309:          execFileSync("git", ["diff", "--name-only", `${changed}...HEAD`], {`; from `app/` on a committed tree, `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main --kinds unit` without the dev profile prints `No test files found` for each db-project entry it selects (measured by the B7 g3 reviewer at d4b58b9: 16 of 78).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2038 · `bun run db:fn` hangs for good when its stdin is an open pipe: `supabase migration new` reads the new file's SQL from stdin
- symptom: B7 g1 (step 11a): the first `bun run db:fn --name admin_withdraw withdraw_submission` wrote its migration in seconds; the second, in a Bash call that the tool moved to the background after 120 s, left an empty `supabase/migrations/20261008190908_admin_withdraw.sql` and never ended. `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` showed `supabase.exe migration new admin_withdraw` still alive minutes later, under `bun.exe scripts/db-fn.mjs`.
- cause: `scripts/db-fn.mjs` spawns `bun x supabase migration new <name>` with `stdio: "inherit"`, and the Supabase CLI copies piped stdin into the new file when stdin is not a terminal, so it waits for an end of input that an open pipe never sends. The file exists from the start, empty, so `db-fn.mjs` never reaches its write.
- rule: run `bun run db:fn ... < /dev/null`. If a run hung, stop only its own processes by id (`taskkill //F //PID <id>` for `supabase.exe migration new`, its `bun x` parent and the two `bun` above it) and delete the empty migration before running it again.
- proof: from `app/`, `timeout 100 bun run db:fn --name admin_withdraw withdraw_submission < /dev/null` → `wrote supabase/migrations/20261008222354_admin_withdraw.sql` in seconds (measured 2026-10-08, B7 g1).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2039 · Editing a test file that many registry entries anchor on makes `watchfail --changed origin/main` a long run, and killing it mid-replay leaves a shared source file mutated
- symptom: 2026-10-09, B7 g2: the first replay of the group's entries ran `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main --kinds unit` in the foreground; after two minutes it was still on `b7-g1-*` entries of `src/server/lib/admin-route.ts`, the Bash call moved to the background, and the run was killed. The kill left `src/server/lib/admin-route.ts` and then `src/server/lib/admin-response.ts` in their mutated state (`git status` showed both modified) until `git checkout -- <file>` restored them.
- cause: the group had edited `tests/unit/admin-routes-parity.test.ts` (it removes five `routesPending` entries), and dozens of entries of B7, B8 and later slices name that file as their test, so `--changed` selects all of them (about 20 s each, P-537); `watchfail` writes each mutation into the real source file for the length of its replay.
- rule: before editing a test file, count the entries that name it (`grep -c <file> app/tests/mutations/*.json`). To replay one group's own entries, write a scratch registry folder holding only those entries (outside the repository) and run `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry <folder>`; for `sql` entries prepend the unpushed migration and rewrite `bunx vitest run` to `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` (P-312). The full `--changed origin/main` pass of P-537 starts after `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"` (its first run without the profile printed `bad 24`, every one a db-project entry that stopped on `DEV_DB_URL is not set`; the second run with it printed `ok 24`), goes in `run_in_background` with its output in a file, and is never killed while a replay runs: wait for it, or after a kill run `git status` and restore every file you did not edit with `git checkout -- <file>`.
- proof: `cd app && git status --short | grep -v '^??'` right after a killed replay lists the mutated file; `git checkout -- <file>` empties the list (measured 2026-10-09, B7 g2).
- added: 2026-10-09

## P-2040 · `bun run db:psql` needs `psql` on PATH, and this machine has none although ASSUMED E11 lists psql 18.4
- symptom: 2026-10-09, B7 g2: `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bun run db:psql -- -Atc "select 1"` printed `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"` and exited 1, so the plan's catalog checks against `mop-dev` (`to_regproc`, `pg_indexes`) could not run that way.
- cause: `scripts/psql-dev.mjs` spawns `psql`; the laptop of this session (user `ka`) has no PostgreSQL client installed (`command -v psql pg_ctl` prints nothing), unlike the machine ASSUMED E11 measured.
- rule: a catalog check on `mop-dev` is a db test case or a node `pg` script that reads `DEV_DB_URL` after `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"`; the db vitest project needs no `psql`. Do not install a client to make one command work.

## P-2421 · A second email shell next to `layout.tsx` is a jscpd clone: the Html, Head, Body, Preview, Container run is 91 tokens
- symptom: B11 g4's `place-notes.tsx` (its own shell, because `Layout` prints a footer of its own and the issue footer carries the unsubscribe link) passed tsc, lint and knip, then `bun run check` stopped at `ERROR: jscpd found too many duplicates (0.0%) over threshold (0.0%)`: `layout.tsx` 96:78-107:12 against `place-notes.tsx` 64:87-75:12 (12 lines, 91 tokens). About 6 minutes with the full check run twice.
- cause: the head (`title`, the `viewport` meta, the `color-scheme` meta), `Body style={page}`, `Preview` and `Container style={column}` in that order are the same token run in both files; the threshold is 70 tokens and 0 percent.
- rule: a template that needs a different footer shares the shell with `layout.tsx` (export its `page`, `column` and `rule` styles, or give `Layout` a footer slot); copying them and reordering `Preview` inside the `Container` only hides the clone from jscpd and lets the two shells drift, so keep that reorder as a last resort with a reason in the entry. (Hit at B11 g4, which took the reorder; the reviewer called it a follow-up, and `layout.tsx` belongs to another group.) Run `bunx jscpd` (seconds) before the full `bun run check` (minutes) whenever a new `.tsx` under `src/templates/email/` repeats a shell.
- proof: `cd app && bunx jscpd 2>&1 | grep -i "found"` → `Found 0 clones.` on slice/b11 at B11 g4; with the `Preview` line moved back above `<Container style={column}>` in `src/templates/email/place-notes.tsx` it prints `Found 1 clones.` (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2407 · `watchfail --registry --changed origin/main` on a lane replays the whole slice, about 15 minutes, and `--only` is the quick path for one entry
- symptom: B11 g4's fix round ran rule (c) of the hand-in (`node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main`) and it ran past the 120 second tool limit, then 15 more minutes of polling: `watchfail: replayed 177: ok 177, bad 0, stale 0; manual 0 not replayed; 3287 not selected`, because every entry of g5 and earlier groups of the slice is also a changed file against origin/main. Polls that only slept returned nothing, and a `pgrep` poll failed at once (`pgrep: command not found` in Git Bash).
- cause: `--changed` selects every registry entry whose `file` or `test` differs from the base, and a lane's base is main, not the previous group; the replay mutates source files, so nothing else can be edited while it runs.
- rule: start the replay in the background with output redirected to a file (`> /tmp/wf.txt 2>&1`, `run_in_background`) and edit nothing until `watchfail: replayed` is the last line; poll that file with a bounded loop of `sleep 9` calls, not `pgrep`. For one new entry use `--registry tests/mutations --only <id>`.
- proof: `cd app && node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b11-g4-render-rgb-typed 2>&1 | tail -1` → `watchfail: replayed 1: ok 1, bad 0, stale 0; manual 0 not replayed; 3464 not selected` (measured 2026-10-07, B11 g4 fix round).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2408 · `playwright test --project admin <file>` reads the file as a second project name: use `--project=admin`
- symptom: B11 g6's proof command `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_DATASET=1 bunx playwright test --project admin tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts` stopped at once with `Error: Project(s) "tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts" not found. Available projects: "desktop", "phone", ...`, before any server started.
- cause: `--project` takes a list of names, so the next word is another name; a plan line copied the space form.

- proof: `cd app && bunx playwright test --project admin tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts --list` prints the `Project(s) ... not found` error, and `bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts --list` lists the spec (measured 2026-10-07).

## P-2410 · A plan line that gives one route file two actions on one method cannot be built: the second action needs its own file
- symptom: B11 step 7 says `newsletter.subscribers.ts` answers `GET` with `listSubscribers` (action `newsletter.subscribers_count`) and `GET ?format=csv` with `exportSubscribers` (action `newsletter.subscribers_export`).
- cause: `server.handlers` has one handler per HTTP method, `defineAdminRoute` takes exactly one `action` and authorizes that one before the handler runs (R11), and `admin-routes-parity.test.ts` needs each matrix action as the tag of some handler. One GET cannot carry two actions; dispatching on `?format=csv` inside the count handler would authorize the export as the count (all six roles) and leave `newsletter.subscribers_export` without a route.
- rule: give each action its own route file; the export is `src/routes/api/admin/newsletter.subscribers.export.ts` (`GET /api/admin/newsletter/subscribers/export`), which the Export CSV link of the subscribers tab opens. Do not reach a second matrix action through a query parameter.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/admin-routes-parity.test.ts` passes with `newsletter.subscribers_count` on `newsletter.subscribers.ts` and `newsletter.subscribers_export` on `newsletter.subscribers.export.ts`; `grep -n "format=csv" workspace/05-plans/B11.md` still prints the plan line to correct (measured 2026-10-07).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2411 · A new server module can regroup Nitro's `_ssr` chunks into an import cycle, and the built Worker then answers 500 on every page: `siteConfig` is undefined when `lib/seo` is evaluated
- symptom: B11 g6 moved the sign-in address lookup of the send test from the route file into `src/server/lib/staff-email.ts`, imported by `src/server/newsletter/service.ts`. `bun run check` and `bun run build` were green, then `E2E_TARGET=built bunx playwright test --project=admin ...` ended `Error: Timed out waiting 120000ms from config.webServer.` and wrangler's log printed, for every request, `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')` at `.output/server/_ssr/<hash>.mjs`, the module-level line of `lib/seo` that builds the title suffix from `siteConfig.name`. The same code with the route importing `staff-email.ts` directly had booted an hour earlier.
- cause: Nitro re-bundles Vite's SSR chunks into `.output/server/_ssr/<hash>.mjs`; with the `$initial` group of `vite.config.ts` (H62) the partition is a function of the whole module graph. In the bad build `<hash>2.mjs` (holding `config/site`) imported route and schema names from `<hash>.mjs` while `<hash>.mjs` (holding `lib/seo`) imported `siteConfig` from it: a cycle, entered from the second chunk, so `lib/seo` ran first. Nothing in `check`, the unit tests or `bundle-check` evaluates the built server.
- rule: a module reads `siteConfig` inside a function, never in a statement that runs when it loads (`src/lib/seo.ts` built the title suffix and `src/lib/jsonld.ts` the publisher at load; both now do it per call, and `tests/unit/site-config-lazy.test.ts` fails a new load-time read). After a group adds or moves a module under `src/server` or `src/domain`, or merges main, boot the built Worker once (the first request of any `playwright --project=admin` spec starts it, or `bun run cf:preview` and `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`) and read its log for a `TypeError` before the hand-in. When it appears, look for a load-time read of a shared module's export (the test above), and only then change the module graph (here the function lives in `service.ts`, no `staff-email.ts`); do not chase the cycle in the chunks.
- proof: three builds of slice/b11 measured on 2026-10-07 under the same command, `E2E_TARGET=built E2E_PORT=8988 bunx playwright test --project=admin tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts`: route importing `staff-email.ts` boots (the spec runs); `service.ts` importing `staff-email.ts` times out with the TypeError above; the function inside `service.ts` boots again (test 1 then fails on the 403 of P-2409, not on boot).
- hit again: 2026-10-07, B11 g6, after merging origin/main (the channels and reports groups): the same 500 on every page returned although `staff-email.ts` was gone, and a build of the merged tree with the newsletter files moved away booted, so the trigger is the graph as a whole. Fixing the two load-time reads made the merged tree boot (`--grep "subscribers tab counts"` -> `1 passed`).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2412 · An axe scan of a page that holds a sandboxed iframe never returns: `browserContext.newPage: Test ended`, with `Blocked script execution in 'about:srcdoc'` in the browser log
- symptom: B11 g6's `checkpoint(page, "/admin/newsletter/:id")` on the issue editor, which holds the sandboxed `srcdoc` preview of the mail, ran until the 120 second test timeout and failed `Error: browserContext.newPage: Test ended ... Please check out .../axe-core-npm/.../error-handling.md` at `fixtures/a11y.ts:33`; the log was full of `Blocked script execution in 'about:srcdoc' because the document's frame is sandboxed and the 'allow-scripts' permission is not set`.
- cause: `@axe-core/playwright` injects axe into every frame of the page and waits for each; a frame with `sandbox=""` takes no script. The preview frame must stay sandboxed (it shows mail built from editors' text), so the frame is the one to leave out of the scan.
- rule: pass the frame's selector as the third argument of `checkpoint(page, label, exclude)` (`runAxe` takes the same list; added in B11 g6 to `tests/e2e/fixtures/a11y.ts`); do not add `allow-scripts` to the frame to please the test. A scan taken before the preview loads is not a way round it: the frame appears with the page.
- proof: with `[PREVIEW_FRAME]` removed from the two editor checkpoints of `tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts`, a Playwright run on the built Worker with the issue API stubbed by `page.route` fails with the error above after 2.0 minutes; with it the same run passes in 17 seconds (`1 passed`), including the scans of the list, the editor, the approve dialog and the subscribers tab with no serious or critical violation (measured 2026-10-07, B11 g6).
- added: 2026-10-07

## P-2414 · A group already merged into main is launched again as if it were unbuilt
- symptom: on 2026-10-08 a builder was launched for B11 g3 (step 4) on slice/b11 with the full build brief; the group's work commit de18bb4 had been on main since PR 200 merged on 2026-10-07 03:20 UTC (CI `db` job green), and its log block and follow-ups were already in `workspace/05-plans/logs/B11.md`. Finding that out took the plan brief, the log and three `gh` calls before any work could start.
- cause: the brief is built from the plan's step list, not from what main holds; after the park (11:45, 2026-10-07) the resumed run did not know g3 was accepted and merged by `mergeEach`.
- rule: a builder first runs `grep -n "^## g<N> " workspace/05-plans/logs/<slice>.md` and, when a block exists, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <its work commit> origin/main`; if it is on main, the builder does not rebuild: it reports what of the group is still open (the log's NOT DONE and BLOCKED lines) and returns `blocked` on that, or `done` when nothing is open. The launcher checks the same before it sizes a resumed slice.
- proof: `git merge-base --is-ancestor de18bb4 origin/main && echo on-main` → `on-main`; `gh pr view 200 --json state --jq .state` → `MERGED` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2415 · `psql` is not on the PATH of this session, and a node one-off that imports `pg` by a `D:/` path fails
- symptom: on 2026-10-08 a read of `select count(*) from action_roles` on mop-dev failed twice: `bun run db:psql` and `psql` gave `command not found`, and a scratch `.mjs` outside the tree that imported `pg` from `D:/mop-build/b11/app/node_modules/pg/lib/index.js` gave `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` (node reads `D:` as a URL scheme).
- cause: `scripts/psql-dev.mjs` spawns a `psql` that only some laptops have on the PATH (scoop); node's ESM loader on Windows takes an absolute import path only as a `file:///` URL.
- rule: for a one-line read of mop-dev without `psql`, write the probe with `import pg from "file:///D:/.../app/node_modules/pg/lib/index.js"`, connect with `new pg.Client({ connectionString: process.env.DEV_DB_URL })` after `eval "$(node scripts/load-env.mjs --profile dev)"`, and run it under `env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`; keep the probe in the scratchpad, never in the tree (P-2413).
- proof: `which psql` prints nothing on this session; the probe with the `file:///` import printed `{ n: 0 }` for the `newsletter.%` rows of `action_roles` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 g9: `bun run db:psql -- -c ...` printed `Executable not found in $PATH: "psql"` for all of steps 10 to 12, so the plan's `db:psql` commands ran through a scratchpad probe (`q.mjs`, statements as arguments, rows printed as JSON) built the same way; the first call of a new probe after the bank was read would have saved the failed `db:psql` attempts.

## P-2417 · `watchfail --changed origin/main` reads committed work only: before the commit it replays other groups' entries and skips the new ones, in about ten minutes
- symptom: after g8 added `src/server/newsletter/standalone.ts` and 18 entries for it, `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --changed origin/main` ran about 10 minutes (307 entries of every group already on the branch) and replayed only 3 of the 18 new ones (those whose file, `send-email.ts`, is tracked and committed earlier).
- cause: the script selects by `git diff --name-only --relative origin/main...HEAD`, a three-dot diff to `HEAD`: nothing uncommitted counts, `git add -N` included, while the branch's earlier groups are all in the diff.
- rule: replay the entries of uncommitted work by id (`node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only <id>`, one call per id in a shell loop), and run `--changed origin/main` only after the commit, as the last gate; never edit a mutated file while a replay runs.
- proof: `cd app && git diff --name-only --relative origin/main...HEAD | grep -c newsletter/standalone` printed `0` with the file written and staged with `git add -N`, and `--only b11-standalone-wait-shortened` printed `WATCHED-FAIL OK B11:b11-standalone-wait-shortened` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2419 · A job of a type the deployed runner does not know is claimed and put back 15 minutes later with `attempts` 0: it never ends `done`, and a lane cannot prove a new system job on `mop-dev`
- symptom: B11 g9 step 11: `select enqueue_job('newsletter_hygiene', ...)` on `mop-dev` returned a job id, and two minutes later (and ten after) the row read `status queued`, `attempts 0`, `locked_by` set, `run_after` 15 minutes after `locked_at`; the plan's "ends `done` within two minutes" cannot happen before the handler is on main and the runner is redeployed from it. Step 12's `scripts/newsletter-test-send.ts --make-draft --i-mean-it` does not exist either (the file holds `--dry` only; step 8 adds the rest).
- cause: the lane's handler is not on `main` and so, most likely, not in the Edge Function runner deployed to `mop-dev` (the deployed commit was not read). The row shows that its claim loop leaves a type it cannot run queued with a later `run_after` instead of failing it.
- rule: before an Edge Function proof of a new handler, compare `git ls-tree origin/main` with the lane; if the handler is only on the lane, record the proof UNPROVEN until main deploys it and cancel the stray job (`update jobs set status = 'cancelled', finished_at = now() where id = '<id>' and status = 'queued'`), so the first deploy does not run it by surprise. The proof that can run today: the handler's unit and db tests, the `schedule_settings` and `cron.job` reads, and the approval inside a rolled-back transaction (an actor, the staff role and the `newsletter.approve` row of `action_roles` made inside it).
