## P-2420 · A shared helper placed in `<feature>-api.ts` cannot be imported by a component: `boundaries.test.ts` refuses it, so the helper belongs in its own module
- symptom: B11 g6 put `failureText` (the message plus the request id to quote) in `src/admin/newsletter/newsletter-api.ts` and imported it from `IssueEditor.tsx`; `bunx vitest run tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` then failed `keeps admin components away from *-api modules`. The cost sat under P-2410 in the slice log, which is about one action per route file and says nothing of imports.
- cause: R41 forbids a `.tsx` under `src/admin` importing a `*-api` module (components reach the server through `<feature>-queries.ts`), and the test matches any resolved module whose name ends in `-api`, whatever the export is.
- rule: a helper that a component and a query module both need (an error text, a formatter) goes in its own file beside them (`src/admin/newsletter/failure-text.ts`); `-api.ts` holds the `fetch` calls only. Apply it on first write, not after the refusal.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/boundaries.test.ts` → `Tests  ... passed` with `IssueEditor.tsx` importing `./failure-text`; with that import pointed back at `./newsletter-api` it prints `× keeps admin components away from *-api modules`; `grep -n "failure-text" app/src/admin/newsletter/IssueEditor.tsx` → line 9.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2423 · Step 13's proof "`bun run stubs` lists no `STUB(B11)` marker" cannot pass in step 13: two `STUB(B11 step 4)` markers of other groups remain, and one cannot go until `newsletter_save_draft` takes a null actor
- symptom: B11 g10 deleted the scheduler's `STUB(B11)` branch; `bun run stubs | grep "STUB(B11)"` still printed `src/server/channels/resend.ts:177` and `src/server/newsletter/assemble.ts:71`, because the script prints a `STUB(B11 step 4)` marker as `STUB(B11)`.
- cause: both markers wrap a cast that waited for step 4's generated types. The types are on main now (`"newsletter_set_audience":` and `"newsletter_save_draft":` in `src/db/types.ts`), but the generated `Args` of `newsletter_save_draft` make `p_actor` and `p_actor_kind` non-null strings (P-915), and `queue_digest` calls it with both null (G43), so the typed call does not compile and the `assemble.ts` cast has to stay until the function gives those two arguments defaults and moves them last. Neither file is a g10 file, and the plan's step 13 names only the scheduler marker.
- rule: a step whose proof says "no `STUB(<slice>)` marker" greps the whole slice's markers before it starts (`bun run stubs | grep "STUB(<slice>"`) and lists every marker it does not own as NOT DONE with its owner; the `resend.ts` cast can go now (typed `db.rpc("newsletter_set_audience", { p_key, p_audience_id })`), the `assemble.ts` one needs `newsletter_save_draft` with `p_actor uuid default null, p_actor_kind public.actor_kind default null` moved after the other arguments (P-915) and a regenerated `src/db/types.ts`.
- proof: `cd app && bun run stubs | grep -c "STUB(B11)"` → `2` and `grep -A1 '"newsletter_save_draft":' src/db/types.ts | grep -c '"p_actor": string'` → `1` on slice/b11 at B11 g10 (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2424 · In vitest, `toMatchObject({ key: {} })` passes when the value is `null`: an empty object in the expected subset matches anything object-shaped or null
- symptom: B11 g10's watched-fail `b11-g10-db-empty-posts-null` (SQL `kpi_weekly` without the `coalesce(..., '{}'::jsonb)` around `jsonb_object_agg`, so `posts_by_channel` came back `null` for an empty week) replayed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: stayed green`: the case asserted `expect(value).toMatchObject({ ..., posts_by_channel: {}, ... })`. A probe of the mutated function on mop-dev printed `"posts_by_channel":null`.
- cause: the subset check of `toMatchObject` walks the keys of the expected object; `{}` has none, so nothing is compared and the null passes.
- rule: assert an empty object or a value that may be null with `toEqual` (the whole object, or the one property: `expect(value.key).toEqual({})`); keep `toMatchObject` for subsets whose leaves are scalars or non-empty objects.
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile, `node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b11-g10-db-empty-posts-null` → `WATCHED-FAIL OK` with the case's `toEqual`; with the case put back to `toMatchObject` it printed `WATCHED-FAIL BAD: stayed green (B11:b11-g10-db-empty-posts-null)` (measured 2026-10-08, B11 g10).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2425 · After merging main, the newest `action_roles` migration misses main's matrix rows: `action-roles.sync.test.ts` is red although no conflict said so
- symptom: B11 merge of main (invoices, newsletter, KPI): `bun run check` failed in `tests/unit/action-roles.sync.test.ts` with eight expected rows missing (`payments.*`, `submissions.activate`); the merge had been conflict-free in `supabase/migrations/`, and `migrations:restamp` had put the lane's three `action_roles` files after main's, so the lane's file was the newest and held only the lane's matrix.
- cause: each `action_roles` file is generated from the matrix of the tree it was made in; after a merge the matrix is the union, and the newest file (the lane's) no longer equals it.
- rule: after every merge of main that touches `src/server/lib/permissions/`, run `bun run scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs` in the app folder (it upserts one row per action and deletes none), then `bun run migrations:check` and commit the new file in the merge fix.
- proof: `cd app && bun run scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs && bun run test -- tests/unit/action-roles.sync.test.ts` → the generator prints `wrote supabase/migrations/<ts>_action_roles.sql 115 actions` and the test passes (2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08 B11 merge
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 g2: the merge of main at the start of the group left `action-roles.sync.test.ts` red with 115 rows against 121; the lane's own newest file (`20261008070146_action_roles.sql`) was removed with `git rm` and `gen-action-roles.mjs` wrote one file over the merged matrix (`20261008141204_action_roles.sql`, 121 actions). `bun run migrations:check` cannot read the removed file until the removal is committed (it reads the file HEAD still lists), so it is run after the commit.
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 c11u: the merge of main that brought B8 jobs rows into the matrix left the lane newest `20261008141204_action_roles.sql` with 121 actions against 127; `git rm` of it and one run of `gen-action-roles.mjs` wrote `20261008170651_action_roles.sql` (127 actions). The log and bank mentions of the removed name are history, not references.
- hit again: 2026-10-09, B7 g2: after the merge of B11's main and `migrations:restamp`, `action-roles.sync.test.ts` was red (`expected [ …(118) ] to deeply equal [ …(128) ]`) because the lane's newest `action_roles` file, renumbered past main's, lacked B11's ten actions; `bun run scripts/gen-action-roles.mjs` wrote `20261008222914_action_roles.sql` with 128 actions and the test passed.

## P-2426 · CI's e2e job fails on a flaky first attempt of `admin-signin.spec.ts` (`state=expired`) because `failOnFlakyTests` is on, twice in a row on the B11 merge
- symptom: PR 227 (B11 merged with main at 6eda9a41), runs 37741531482 and its rerun: `[admin] admin-signin.spec.ts:16 a magic link opened in a new browser context signs the managing editor in` waits 2.0m at `helpers/session.ts:71 page.waitForURL(/admin)` after the page `navigated to /admin/sign-in?state=expired`, passes on retry #1 in 1.9 s, and the job ends `1 flaky, 10 passed, 7 skipped` with exit 1 (playwright.config.ts: `failOnFlakyTests: Boolean(process.env[CI])`). Main's own CI run 37741950353 is green.
- cause: measured 2026-10-08 (c11s, one failure in two runs before the fix, so not a rate): on slice/b11 before the fix, `CI=1 E2E_TARGET=built E2E_DATASET=1 E2E_PORT=8988 bunx playwright test --project=admin --workers 2` ended `1 flaky` in the first of two runs, the flaky test being `admin-signin.spec.ts:16` (2.0m, then retry passes); after the newsletter spec took `staff+chief@matterofplace.com`, two such runs ended with no flaky line. The failed attempt is the first test of its worker and runs at the same second as `admin-newsletter.spec.ts` on the other worker; both sign in as `staff+managing@matterofplace.com`, and a second `generateLink` for one user probably voids the first token hash. The B11 spec `admin-invoice.spec.ts` (all seven tests skipped without `E2E_FULL_STACK`) shifts the order so the two sign-ins overlap.
- rule: a rerun does not help (the first attempt fails the same way); the fix is one seeded staff user per e2e spec file that signs in (admin-newsletter.spec.ts now uses the chief editor); `tests/unit/e2e-staff-isolation.test.ts` fails when another e2e file names the newsletter spec's address. admin-signin and admin-invoice still share `staff+managing@` and would collide if invoice ran beside signin (it is skipped without E2E_FULL_STACK). Check `grep -n "signInAs(browser" app/tests/e2e/admin-newsletter.spec.ts` before deciding.
- proof: `gh run view 37741531482 --log-failed | grep -E "state=expired|1 flaky"` → the `navigated to` line and `1 flaky` (2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08 B11 merge

## P-2459 · A merge of main into a lane conflicted in a job three slices extend (`reconcileJob`), and each slice's registry entries and routeTree.gen.ts conflicted with it
- symptom: 2026-10-08, B11 g1: `git merge origin/main` stopped in `src/server/jobs/system/reconcile.ts`, `tests/unit/jobs/reconcile.test.ts`, `tests/mutations/B8.json` and `src/routeTree.gen.ts`. Main's B10 had made `reconcileJob(uploads, socialPart)`; the lane's B11 had made `reconcileJob(uploads, aggregateIssues)`. After the textual resolution `tsc` failed on 14 route files (`'/admin/newsletter/$id' is not assignable to keyof FileRoutesByPath`) and the B10 entry `b10g9-job-result` was STALE (`find occurs 0 times`), both invisible to the conflict markers.
- cause: a job that every slice adds one part to is a merge point: the parts compose (`reconcileJob(settleUploads, settleSocial, aggregateRecentIssues)`, result `{ uploads, social, newsletter }`), they do not replace each other. The registry entries of the other slice and the generated route tree are not in the conflict list when git merges them cleanly or when `--theirs` is taken.
- rule: after such a merge, keep every part, then (1) rewrite the `find` and `replace` of each registry entry that names the changed line, in every registry file (`grep -rn "reconcileJob(" tests/mutations`), (2) take `src/routeTree.gen.ts` from main and let `bun run build` regenerate it, never edit it, (3) run the unit test of the job and `--only` each entry of the touched files.
- proof: `cd app && grep -rn "reconcileJob(" tests/mutations src | head` → the `settleUploads, settleSocial, aggregateRecentIssues` form in `reconcile.ts`, `B8.json` and `B10.json` alike; `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/jobs/reconcile.test.ts` → `Tests 10 passed (10)` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2460 · `bun run lint` dies with `JavaScript heap out of memory` (exit 134) at the default 2 GB Node heap on a lane tree
- symptom: 2026-10-08, B11 g1: `bun run check` stopped in `eslint . --max-warnings 0` after about 300 s with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory`, `error: script "lint" exited with code 134`. No rule was violated.
- cause: the type-aware lint (R01, `projectService`) of a tree of about 2000 files holds the program in memory; Node's default old-space limit here is about 2 GB.
- rule: run `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 bun run check` (or `bun run lint`) from `app/`. A 134 exit is not a lint result: read the last lines of the output before fixing code.
- proof: `cd app && NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144 bun run lint` → `quiet: ok` on slice/b11 at the same tree that exited 134 without it (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 g2: `bun run check` without the option exited 134 in lint after about 220 s; with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144` the same tree went on to the test gate.

## P-2461 · A `watchfail --changed origin/main` replay that the Bash tool moves to the background keeps mutating `src/` and breaks the next `bun run check`
- symptom: 2026-10-08, B11 g2: the replay after a registry edit selected the whole of `B11.json` (about 1400 lines of output, 15 minutes). The Bash call hit its 120 s limit and went to the background; the process kept running, and a `bun run check` started meanwhile failed with `Parsing error: Unterminated string literal` in `variables.ts` and `TS6133` in `hygiene.ts`, files the group never touched. `git status` showed ` M` on `IssueEditor.tsx` and `send-email.ts`, then clean again as each replay restored its file.
- cause: the replay writes each `replace` into the real file, runs the test and puts the file back; a check that reads the tree in that window sees the mutation. Killing the replay midway leaves the current mutation in the file (`send-email.ts` kept a changed idempotency key).
- rule: replay a new group's own entries one at a time with `--only <id>` (a loop, output to a file; P-2457), never `--changed origin/main` from a foreground call; never start `bun run check` while a replay is alive. If one has to be stopped, find it with `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process` (command line contains `watchfail`), stop it by its process id with `Stop-Process -Id`, then run `git status --short` and `git checkout --` every file you did not edit.
- proof: `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match 'watchfail' } | Select-Object ProcessId"` lists the replay while it runs and nothing after it ended; `git status --short` is then limited to the files of the group (measured 2026-10-08).
- hit again: 2026-10-08, B11 c459 review: the reviewer replayed `watchfail` file entries in the foreground while a `bun run check` of the same tree ran in the background; the check failed with `src/domain/email.ts 254:68 Parsing error` and cost one extra full check run (about 5 minutes). Run alone, the same check printed `quiet: ok`, exit 0. The rule covers a reviewer too: no file-mutating replay while any check, build or test of the same tree is running.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2462 · A snapshot check started in the background looks finished when its output file says `exit=0`, and `review-snapshot.mjs remove` then deletes files under the running check
- symptom: 2026-10-08, B11 g2 review: a `bun run check` started with `run_in_background` in the review snapshot was taken for finished because `check.txt` already held `quiet: ok` and `exit=0` while `quiet.mjs`, `bun run check` and vitest were still alive. `review-snapshot.mjs remove` then deleted part of the tree under the running check: it failed with EPERM, but `.github/workflows` was already gone. The check went red with `FAIL tests/unit/one-database.test.ts ... ENOENT ... .github\workflows\ci.yml` and `quiet: exit 1`, and the snapshot had to be removed and created again before the check was run in the foreground, which printed `quiet: ok (74 lines)` with exit 0.
- cause: an earlier write of the output file (a first `quiet: ok` line, a stale `exit=0`) is not the end of the process tree; the output file is evidence of a past moment, and `remove` does not look for processes that still use the folder.
- rule: run the snapshot's check in the foreground. If it has to run in the background, before `remove` confirm that nothing started in the snapshot is alive (command line matches `b11-review`, with the lane's own name); a line in an output file never counts. After a failed `remove`, list what is left of the folder before trusting a new run in it.
- proof: `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-CimInstance Win32_Process | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match '<lane>-review' } | Select-Object ProcessId"` lists the check's processes while it runs and nothing after it ended; run it before `node workspace/05-plans/review-snapshot.mjs remove <laneRoot>` (measured 2026-10-08).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2504 · A migration that sets a transaction-local setting leaks it into every db test that applies the file as the prelude
- symptom: B11 c459, `MOP_MUTATION_SQL` set to `<ts>_standalone_template.sql` (P-312), then `tests/db/automation.db.test.ts` "a direct update writes one revision with a null actor and note direct" failed: the revision note read `B11`. The same case passed without the prelude.
- cause: the migration called `set_config('mop.note', 'B11', true)` so the revision trigger would record its note. A transaction-local setting lasts until the transaction ends, and `withRollback` runs the prelude in the test's own transaction, so the next revision of the test inherited the note.
- rule: a migration or a registry `sql` entry that sets `mop.note`, `mop.actor_id` or `mop.actor_kind` with `set_config(..., true)` ends with `set_config(name, '', true)` for each, so the file leaves the session as it found it. A plan line that names `automation_put_template` for a column (`variables`) does not make the function patch it: it accepts only subject, preheader, body and enabled and raises `invalid_patch_key`, so a column outside that list takes a direct `update` in the same block.
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile, `MOP_MUTATION_SQL="$(cat supabase/migrations/*_standalone_template.sql)" env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN bunx vitest run --project db tests/db/automation.db.test.ts -t "direct update writes one revision"` → `Tests  1 passed`; with the closing `set_config('mop.note', '', true)` removed from the file → `1 failed` (measured 2026-10-08, B11 c459).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2505 · A group brief listed as open the migration and the sample that the branch already held, and the first hour went to building around them
- symptom: B11 g2's brief named the `standalone` row migration and the `standalone` entry of `variablesByKey` as open work ("waited on B9's close-out"). `git log -- app/supabase/migrations/20261008170650_standalone_template.sql` showed commit 59b225d7 (group c459) had built both, with their tests, nine registry entries and a log block; the same commit had already taken `standalone.tsx`'s placeholder out. Only the property block of `render.ts` and the `--dry` sample were open. The brief's "Stale: B5's emailTemplateSchema ... check what main holds" line was the hint, read after the first files.
- cause: the brief was written from the plan's step text and the follow-up list, not from `git log` of the branch; c459 had landed on `slice/b11` while g2's brief was queued.
- rule: before building a part a brief calls open, run `git log --oneline -3 -- <each file the part names>` and `grep -n "<c-number or part>" workspace/05-plans/logs/B11.md`; a part a commit already holds is verified (run its proof once) and left alone, and the log says which parts were found built.
- proof: `git log --oneline -3 -- app/supabase/migrations/20261008170650_standalone_template.sql` -> `59b225d7 B11 c459 (steps 4, 5, 9 remainder): the standalone row, its sample block, the footer, the unstubbed render` (measured 2026-10-08, B11 g2).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2506 · A review brief named the merge that started the group, not the commit that holds its work
- symptom: B11 g2's reviewer was told to snapshot `f7affc3`, the merge "B11 g2 start". At that commit `grep -n "b11-g2" app/tests/mutations/B11.json` and `grep -n P-2505 GOTCHAS.md` returned nothing, so the snapshot held none of the group's work; the hand-in was `2587c2ae`, one commit later, and the reviewer had to check it out detached inside the snapshot.
- cause: the brief took the commit id from the group's start line of the log instead of the hand-in line.
- rule: the snapshot id in a review brief is the commit that holds the group's log block. Check it before sending: `git log --oneline -1 <id> -- workspace/05-plans/logs/B11.md` must name the group, or a grep in the snapshot for an id the hand-in names must find it.
- proof: `git log --oneline -1 2587c2ae -- workspace/05-plans/logs/B11.md` names the g2 hand-in; the same command at `f7affc30` names an older block (measured 2026-10-08, B11 g2 review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2507 · A merge of main swapped the read path under a shared test fixture, and 28 newsletter tests went red on the pull request with the lane green before it
- symptom: 2026-10-08, B11 c11t: after the merge of main (B16), `send.test.ts` 13, `standalone.test.ts` 14 and `service.test.ts` 1 failed in CI with `AppError: The catalog is not available right now.` (`src/server/public/state.ts:73`) via `loadSiteContext` -> `getSiteSettings` -> `getPublicState`; they had been green before the merge.
- cause: `loadSiteContext` stopped reading the `settings` table row `site` and reads the shared public state (`public_state` RPC, memoised per isolate). The fixture `tests/fixtures/newsletter-world.ts` (`newsletterDb`) registered no `public_state` handler, and a first read that fails with no earlier good copy is `unavailable`. `emailWorld` in `tests/fixtures/email-send.ts` had been updated by B16; the second fixture had no owner in that slice.
- rule: when main changes how a service reads (table to RPC, table to state), grep every fixture that builds a fake client for the old read (`grep -rln 'key: "site"' tests`) and give it the new handler in the fixture, once, answering from the same seeded row; never mock the service away in the tests, and reset the memo when the world is built. The product stays as it is: an unavailable state is a retryable `AppError`, and `send.test.ts` holds a case for it on a fresh module.
- proof: `cd app && bunx vitest run tests/unit/newsletter tests/unit/email` -> 29 files, 472 tests passed; with `{ public_state: state, ...rpc }` in `newsletterDb` reduced to `{ ...rpc }` the registry entry `b11-c11t-world-serves-no-state` replays red.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2508 · `renderTemplate` built the plain-text part from the row's blocks alone, so a template that draws its own content (the standalone email) had a text part without its link and unsubscribe address in every path except the real send
- symptom: 2026-10-08, B11 c11u: PR 227 CI, e2e job, step email shots: `standalone: text-url the plain-text part does not hold https://matterofplace.com/property/alder-court` and `... does not hold {{{RESEND_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL}}}`, while `bun run check` and the unit suites were green.
- cause: `plainText(blocks, site)` in `src/server/email/render.ts` writes the text from the resolved blocks and the footer lines, and the standalone row has no blocks (its property block is drawn by `standalone.tsx`). `sendStandalone` hid the gap by overwriting `text` with its own `standaloneText`, and `lint.test.ts` copied that override, so only `scripts/email-shots.ts` (and the preview and the `[Test]` send) linted the text `renderTemplate` returns.
- rule: a template file that draws content of its own exports `textParts(variables)` (`{ lead, trail }`), which `renderTemplate` puts before the blocks and after the footer lines; never rebuild the text in a caller and never copy that rebuild into a lint test. A test that lints a template's mail uses the pair `renderTemplate` returns.
- proof: `cd app && bun scripts/email-shots.ts; echo $?` -> `ok standalone 600x900` ... `0`; with `lead: [title, deck].filter` in `src/templates/email/standalone.tsx` the registry entry `b11-c11u-text-url` replays red (`node scripts/watchfail.mjs --registry tests/mutations --only b11-c11u-text-url`).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2463 · A costTime line names a bank entry from memory, and the entry it names is about something else
- symptom: B11 c11u review: the report said the 84 BAD / 4 stale replay run without the dev profile was "Already banked as P-2508". P-2508 is about `renderTemplate` building the text part from blocks only and does not mention the dev profile. The cost was banked, in the P-066 hit-again line of c11t and in P-310, so nothing was lost, but the pointer sent a reader to the wrong entry.
- cause: the id was written from memory of the lane's own recent entries instead of looked up by the words of the cost.
- rule: before a report names an entry for a cost, run `grep -n "<words of the cost>" GOTCHAS.md` and cite the ids it prints; a cost with no hit gets a new entry, not a guessed id.
- proof: `grep -n "84 BAD\|without the dev profile" GOTCHAS.md` -> lines in P-066 (hit again, c11t) and P-310, none in P-2508 (2026-10-08, B11 c11u review).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2464 · The lane's restamp commit renamed the standalone migration but left the old version in a test's relative path, so `check` fails on ENOENT in CI and the merge gate stops
- symptom: PR 227 `check` job: `tests/unit/email/render.test.ts > equals the standalone row the B11 migration sets` fails with ENOENT on `supabase/migrations/20261008141205_standalone_template.sql`; locally `bun run migrations:restamp` says "nothing to do" because the renames are already ahead of main, so the tool cannot repair it.
- cause: commit 1532632f renamed the five lane migrations (141201 to 170647 and so on) but its diff touches no file under `app/tests`; the test still names 141205. The restamp script rewrites every tracked file, so that commit was not produced by one clean run of it (how the test file was missed is not proven).
- rule: after any restamp, run `grep -rn "<each old version>" app workspace` from the tree root before committing; a hit is a missed reference to fix in the same commit. A merge-only run does not fix it: it returns blocked naming the file.
- proof: `grep -rn "20261008141205" app/tests` -> one hit in `app/tests/unit/email/render.test.ts` while `ls app/supabase/migrations | grep standalone` prints `20261008170650_standalone_template.sql` (2026-10-08, B11 merge run).
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-2499 · Every preview job fails at `wait` once the workers.dev preview hostname answers Cloudflare's "temporarily rate limited" 429
- symptom: B11 merge gate, PR 227 at 35889e44: `check`, `build`, `db` and `e2e` passed; `preview` failed at step `wait` ("the Worker did not answer ten times in a row in 180 s") and then `observatory` ("status 422, error scan-failed"), on run 37816717202 attempt 2 and again on attempt 3 after `gh run rerun 37816717202 --failed`. `curl https://pr-227.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/` answers `HTTP/1.1 429` with the page "This website has been temporarily rate limited". The last eight deploy.yml runs of other branches (slice/b7, slice/b13, chore/preview-local) all ended `failure` in the same hour.
- cause: the workers.dev preview hostname is rate limited at Cloudflare's edge, so the Worker never answers with an `x-request-id` header; the branch's own build is not at fault (its `e2e` runs the same build on Linux and passed, so it is not the chunk cycle of P-2405).
- rule: a red `preview` job whose `wait` step reads "did not answer ten times" and whose URL answers 429 is the environment, not the branch: do not change code. One rerun is allowed; a second red ends the attempt as BLOCKED, since the merge gate needs every check green. The orchestrator waits for the rate limit to lift (or rules on the preview hostname) and reruns the failed job.
- proof: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://pr-227.holy-meadow-4327.workers.dev/` -> 429 (measured 2026-10-08 21:18 UTC); `gh run view 37816717202 --json jobs --jq '.jobs[]|select(.name=="preview")|.steps[]|select(.conclusion=="failure")|.name'` -> `wait` and `observatory`.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-544 · `rmSync` of a `wrangler dev --persist-to` folder right after `taskkill` threw EPERM and the 20-minute local preview ended without its log
- symptom: 2026-10-08 23:18 +0300, the first real `node scripts/preview-local.mjs --pr 227 --port 8970` (H73) ran every step (build to lighthouse) and then died in its `finally` with `Error: EPERM, Permission denied: \\?\C:\Users\DELL\AppData\Local\Temp\mop-preview-local-state-5JtymR` at `rmSync`, before `renderLog` wrote `workspace/05-plans/logs/preview-local/pr-227-<head7>.md`; the whole run had to be repeated.
- cause: `taskkill /T /F` returns before `workerd` has released the files of its persist folder, so an immediate recursive delete on Windows meets a locked file; the cleanup was a bare `rmSync` that could throw out of `main`.
- rule: a cleanup after stopping `wrangler dev` (or any process tree) on Windows never throws out of the run: `rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true, maxRetries: 10, retryDelay: 500 })` inside a `try` that only prints a leftover, and the result file of a long run is written by code that a cleanup failure cannot skip.
- proof: `grep -n "maxRetries: 10" app/scripts/preview-local.mjs` → the cleanup line; the second real run of `node scripts/preview-local.mjs --pr 227 --port 8970` (head ed3296de) still met the lock after ten retries 500 ms apart, printed `preview-local: ...\mop-preview-local-state-bVRpP0 left behind (EPERM, ...)` and then wrote `workspace/05-plans/logs/preview-local/pr-227-ed3296d.md`; a plain `rm -rf` of the folder a minute later succeeded.
- added: 2026-10-08

## P-545 · GitHub's combined status endpoint (`commits/<sha>/status`) has no `creator` field, so "who posted this status" cannot be checked there
- symptom: 2026-10-09, H73 post-merge gate: the first read of `preview-local` statuses through `repos/<o>/<r>/commits/<sha>/status` found no `creator` on any entry, so the owner check could not be written against it.
- cause: the combined endpoint summarises statuses per context and drops the creator; the list endpoint `commits/<sha>/statuses` returns every status with `creator.login`, newest first.
- rule: a check on the author of a commit status reads `commits/<sha>/statuses` and takes the first entry per context as the current one.
- proof: `gh api repos/AbdulrahmanAmer/matter-of-place/commits/<head of PR 248>/statuses --jq '.[0].creator.login'` prints the login; the same path with `/status` and `.statuses[0].creator` prints null.
- added: 2026-10-09

## P-2041 · B7 step 14's `PUT team/limits` calls `put_setting`, which the plan creates only in step 15's `admin_settings` migration
- symptom: B7 g4 (step 14): the Files line says "The cap goes through `put_setting('agent_daily_limits', ...)`" and the step lists the daily caps and `team.limits.ts`, while `put_setting` belongs to step 15's `<ts>_admin_settings.sql`; on slice/b7 `grep -rln put_setting supabase/sql/functions` found nothing.
- cause: the plan orders the route before the function it calls.
- rule: step 14's `admin_team.sql` creates `put_setting` from `supabase/sql/functions/put_setting.sql` with the one key `agent_daily_limits` (audit `team.limits_put`); step 15 adds `coming_soon_global` and `notifications` to its `case`, regenerates it with `bun run db:fn put_setting` into its own migration, and its tests cover the other keys.
- proof: `cd app && grep -n "when 'agent_daily_limits'" supabase/sql/functions/put_setting.sql` prints the `case` line; with the dev profile, `MOP_MUTATION_SQL="$(cat supabase/migrations/20261009004133_admin_team.sql)" env -u CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project db tests/db/admin.db.test.ts -t "put_setting writes agent_daily_limits"` → `1 passed` (2026-10-09).
- added: 2026-10-09

## P-2042 · Postgres has no `max(uuid)`: the id before a uuid is found by order and limit
- symptom: B7 g4: the `team_users` db cases read one user's row with `team_users(1, (select max(r.user_id) from public.user_roles r where r.user_id < $1))` and both failed with `error: function max(uuid) does not exist`.
- cause: `min` and `max` have no `uuid` variant on mop-dev's Postgres (SQLSTATE 42883).
- rule: the predecessor of a uuid is `(select r.user_id from ... where r.user_id < $1 order by r.user_id desc limit 1)`; its null for the smallest id starts the page at the first row.
- proof: from `app/` with the dev profile, `node -e "const pg=require('pg');const c=new pg.Client({connectionString:process.env.DEV_DB_URL});c.connect().then(()=>c.query('select max(gen_random_uuid())')).catch(e=>console.log(e.code,e.message)).finally(()=>c.end())"` → `42883 function max(uuid) does not exist` (2026-10-09).
- added: 2026-10-09

## P-2043 · `z.custom<T>().parse(proxy)` reads the value, so a Proxy that throws on every property cannot be typed through zod
- symptom: B7 g4's first "refuses an agent with human_only" case in `tests/unit/team.service.test.ts` failed with `Error: db_touched` thrown from `getParsedType` (`zod/v3/helpers/util.js:117`), before any service ran.
- cause: zod inspects the input's type on every parse, `z.custom` included, and that reads properties of the Proxy.
- rule: a unit test's "must not touch the database" client is `fakeDb()` with nothing registered (every call throws `unexpected ...`), or a Proxy typed without zod; never `z.custom().parse(proxy)`.
- proof: from `app/`, a scratch `probe.ts` holding `import { z } from "zod"; try { z.custom().parse(new Proxy({}, { get: () => { throw new Error("db_touched"); } })); console.log("no access"); } catch (e) { console.log(e instanceof Error ? e.message : e); }` run with `bun run ./probe.ts` prints `db_touched` (2026-10-09).
- added: 2026-10-09

## P-2044 · A helper typed `PromiseLike<{ data: T; error: unknown }>` infers `T` as `X | null` from a supabase-js answer
- symptom: B7 g4: `tsc` refused five calls of `rpcOrThrow` in `src/server/team/service.ts` (`Type 'string | null' is not assignable to type 'string'`, `'rows' is possibly 'null'`).
- cause: supabase-js answers `PostgrestResponseSuccess<T> | PostgrestResponseFailure`, whose failure side has `data: null`; one object parameter merges both sides into `data: T | null`.
- rule: type the parameter as the union `{ data: T; error: null } | { data: null; error: PostgrestError }` and narrow on `result.error !== null`, as `rpcOrThrow` in `src/server/team/service.ts` does.
- proof: `cd app && bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` exits 0 on slice/b7 at B7 g4; with the parameter written as `PromiseLike<{ data: T; error: unknown }>` it prints the five errors above (2026-10-09).
- added: 2026-10-09

## P-2045 · A proof suite started while `bun run check` runs in the same tree gave one red result nobody could read again
- symptom: 2026-10-09, B7 g4 review: the first run of `bunx vitest run --project unit tests/unit/team.service.test.ts tests/unit/admin-routes-parity.test.ts`, started while `bun run check` ran in the same tree, printed `Tests  1 failed | 24 passed`, exit 1; five later runs, one under load, were green, and the failing test was never captured, so the review spent a series of re-runs and still could not name it.
- cause: UNPROVEN. The check's stages (type-aware lint, knip, the unit project) compete for the same CPU and files as the suite; the suspect was a case that imports 12 route modules after `vi.resetModules`, but it takes 1332 ms alone against the 30 s `testTimeout` of `vitest.config.ts`, so the timeout is not shown to be the cause.
- rule: never start a proof suite while `bun run check` runs in the same tree; run them one after the other. Send the first run of every proof to a file (`... > <scratchpad>/run.txt 2>&1; echo exit=$?`) so a one-off red can be read without a re-run.
- proof: `cd app && node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --project unit tests/unit/team.service.test.ts --reporter=verbose > "$TEMP/out.txt" 2>&1; grep "human_only from every" "$TEMP/out.txt"` → `an agent key gets 403 human_only from every team route 1332ms` and `Tests  10 passed (10)` on slice/b7, no check running (measured 2026-10-09, B7 g4 fix round).
- added: 2026-10-09
